INTRODUCTION
 
         I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture, having been
 authorised by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby present this One Hundred and  Sixteenth Report on
 “Demands for Grants 2007-2008 of Ministry of Civil Aviation”.
 
2.     The Committee, at its meeting held on the 9 th April, 2007, considered the subject and heard the Secretary and other
 officials of Ministry of Civil Aviation.
 
3.     The Committee wishes to express its thanks to the officers of Ministry of Civil Aviation for placing before the Committee
 the material and information desired in connection with the subject and for clarifying the points raised by the Members.
 
4.     The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on the 9th May, 2007.
 
NEW DELHI ;
May, 9, 2007
Vaisakha 19, 1929 (Saka)
SHRI SITARAM  YECHURY
Chairman,

 Committee on Transport, Tourism & Culture.
 
                                                            REPORT
 
The Ministry of Civil Aviation is responsible for the formulation of national policies and programmes for the
 development and regulation of civil aviation in the country and for devising and implementing schemes for orderly
 growth and expansion of civil air transport.  Its functions also extend to overseeing the provision of airport facilities, air
 traffic services, carriage of passengers and goods by air, safeguarding civil aviation operations, regulation of air
 transport services, licensing of aerodromes, air carriers, pilots and aircraft maintenance engineers. In addition to
 framing policies, the Ministry provides guidance to the organisations in the implementation of policy guidelines. It
 supervises implementation by the organisations of special programmes of the Government, particularly those intended
 for weaker sections.  The Ministry also administratively controls the Commission of Railway Safety, a statutory body

13.  IMPORTANT SCHEMES AND PROJECTS OF AI
PAYMENT TO AIRCRAFT MANUFACTURERS
The Committee was informed that during 2007-08, Air India has made provision of  Rs.2198.20 crores for   advance
 payment to aircraft manufacturers, Rs.3066.52 crores for delivery payment to aircraft manufacturers and Rs.738.90
 crores towards payments for spares/workshop.
(b)        INTEREST TO BE CAPITALISED   
It was also informed that Air India has signed the Purchase Agreement with Boeing Company for acquisition of 50
 aircraft (8 B777-200LR, 15 B777-300ER and 27 B787-8) to be inducted over the period February, 2007 and February,
 2012. Air India is required to pay deposits and advance payments to Boeing as per the Advance Payment Schedule
 negotiated in the Purchase Agreement.   Air India expects to incur an expenditure of Rs.183.39 crores during 2007-08
 on interest to be capitalized on advance payments to Boeing. 
 
(c)        OTHER CAPITAL EXPENDITURE  
The Committee was informed that a provision of Rs.150.00 crores has been made by Air India Limited for other capital
 expenditure such as purchase of ground handling equipments, engineering workshop equipments, computers, office
 equipments etc.
 
14.       The Ministry while responding to the Committee's queries on the acquisition of new aircraft by Air India Ltd has
 stated that Air India Limited (AIL) has signed a purchase agreement with Boeing Company on 31.12.2005 for the

 purchase of 68 aircraft for its subsidiary, Air India Charters Limited (i.e. Air India Express), at a net project cost of
 approx. Rs.34,615 crores.  Air India Express has already taken the delivery of 6 B-737-800W aircraft whereas the
 delivery of larger B-777-200LR aircraft to Air India is expected to commence around April, 2007. M/s Boeing has
 agreed to make its best efforts to complete the delivery of all aircraft by 2011 instead of 2012.  The manufacturers viz.
 M/s. Boeing, GE and CFM International have offered an offset programme valued at 30% of the net aircraft price
 (excluding BFE Items) and spare engines which amounts to approximately USD 2 billions, i.e. approx Rs.9,000 crores
 (US$+Rs.45).
 
15.       The Ministry has also stated that Air India has kept a provision of Rs.6337.01 crore under their IEBR for
 acquisition of aircraft in the year 2007-08. This would only meet a part of the complete acquisition cost of Air India. 
 The acquisition plan is spread over the period 2006-2011.  The total acquisition cost is Rs.34, 615 crore. The balance
 payments for the new aircraft project would be made in subsequent years.
 
16.       The Committee was informed by the Ministry that Air India had earned a Net Profit of Rs.14.94 crore during the
 year 2005-06 as against a profit of Rs.96.36 crore for the year 2004-05.  The Ministry in its reply to the query on the
 decline in the profit, has stated that this is due to appreciation in the value of US dollar vis-à-vis the Rupees by 2.2%
 and 21 % increase in fuel prices.
 
17.       The Ministry has also informed that the passenger load factor has declined from 69.8% to 66.9% even though
 the number of passengers carried increased by 10.4% i.e. from 4.40 million in the year 2004-05 to 4.85 million in the
 year 2005-06.
 
18.       The Committee desired to know the details of the steps taken to increase the profit/passenger load factor of the
 Air India as the passenger load factor has a direct impact on the profit or loss of the company.   The Ministry in its reply
 stated that the phased induction of new aircraft in the ageing fleet of Air India will have a very positive impact in its
 operations. The Ministry has further stated that new marketing strategies introduced by Air India such as whole sale
 travel discount, aircraft cabin upgradation, companion free scheme, auction of Air India tickets through Internet will
 yield a positive result in its profits and an increase in the passenger load factor in the ensuing years.
 
19.       The Committee notes that profit of Air India has gone down from Rs.96.39 crore to Rs.14.94 mainly because of
 the reasons of appreciation in value of US dollar and increasing fuel price.  The Committee hopes that acquisition of
 new aircraft would certainly have positive impact on the operations of Air India. But still the Committee is of the view
 that Air India should adopt an aggressive marketing strategy to face the stiff competition at global level. The
 Committee is also of the opinion that more passenger friendly amenities be provided in its aircraft so that more and
 more passengers turn their interest towards the national carrier.   The Committee desires that the number of   bilateral
 agreements which were signed during the last year should be materialised to the maximum possible extent.

(b)        ACQUISITION OF NEW AIRCRAFT         
The Committee has been informed that during 2007-08, Indian Airlines has made a provision of Rs.2057.00 crore for
 acquisition of new aircraft.   Three A319 aircraft and six A321 aircraft out of the new 43 aircraft to be procured by
 Indian Airlines are likely to be received by end of March, 2008.
(c)        The Committee has also been informed that a provision of Rs.295.00 crore has been made for 2007-08 for
 setting up of additional infrastructure for the 43 new aircraft.
(d)        The Committee finds that the Indian Airlines has also made a provision of Rs.155.20 crore for other supporting
 facilities such as procuring GSD equipment, conversion of B-737 aircraft to cargo freighter, computerization, misc.
 assets etc.
22.       The Committee asked the Ministry about the variations in the expenditure to the tune of Rs.356 crore under the
 Annual Plan 2006-07.  The Ministry in its reply stated that the main reason for variation is on account of the fact that
 the Annual Plan was made with the projection that 6 aircraft (out of the 43 aircraft) will be received in 2006-07,
 however, as per the revised delivery schedule, only one new aircraft was scheduled to join in 2006-07, and the same
 (A-319) has already joined in the fleet in October'06.  The difference on this account is Rs.347.71 crore.  The Ministry
 has also stated the remaining difference of Rs.8.29 crore is on account of taking up only essential and operationally
 necessary projects during the year, exchange rate variation and payments made to IGRUA.
23.       The Committee while considering the Demands for Grants in respect of Indian Airlines enquired about the
 acquisition of new aircraft for Indian Airlines.  The Ministry replied that the Government had approved a proposal for
 acquisition of 43 Airbus aircraft, fitted with CFM engines, for Indian Airlines, at an estimated net project cost of
 Rs.9888 crore.  An agreement was executed with Airbus Industries and CFM International on 20.02.2006 in the
 presence of the Prime Minister and the President of France.  These aircraft are scheduled to be delivered between
 October, 2006 to March 2010.  The first A-319 was delivered on 19.10.2006 and the remaining aircraft would be
 delivered at the rate of one aircraft per month from June, 2007 to June, 2009 (except September, 2007).  The aircraft
 delivery during the period of July 2009 to March, 2010 would take place at the rate of two aircraft per month.  On
 induction of new aircraft, the old fleet of A-300 and B-737-200 would be replaced in a phased manner. 
24.       The Committee was informed that the Annual Plan of Indian Airlines for the year 2007-08 has been approved
 with an outlay of Rs.2507.70 crore.  The increase is primarily due to the actual payments to be made to the
 aircraft/engine manufacturers during 2007-08. This would only meet a part of the complete acquisition cost of Indian
 Airlines.  The total acquisition cost is 10,169 crore and the balance payments for the new aircraft would be made in
 subsequent years.
25.       The Ministry informed the Committee that Indian Airlines has earned a Net Profit of Rs.49.50 crore during
 2005-06 as against the Net Profit of Rs.65.61 crore during 2004-05.  The reasons stated for the decline in the profit are
 increase in ATF price, fall in passengers yields owing to intense competition in the domestic aviation market and due to
 exercise capacity and entry of new players in the market.   However, the overall load factor has seen a substantial
 increased from 69.01% in the year 2004-05 to 71.6% in the year 2005-06. 
26.       The Committee notes that even though there is a substantial increase in the passenger load factor for the period
 from April to September, 2006, the profit of the IA seems to be declining. The physical performance of the Indian
 Airlines is showing good signs of improvement but it is not resulting in a good profit to the company. 
27.       The Committee hopes that induction of new aircraft will help Indian Airlines to improve its profitability and the
 merger   of two national carriers will have a positive impact on the performance of both the Airlines.  The Committee
 recommends that Indian Airlines should revamp its marketing strategies to get its due share in the domestic as well as
 in the international market and also to match with the services offered by the private operators.

30.       The Ministry was asked about the latest position of modernization of non-metro airports to which the Ministry
 replied that it has been decided that instead of phasing airports in a sequential manner, development and modernization
 of 35 non-metro airports namely Ahmedabad, Amritsar, Guwahati, Jaipur, Udaipur, Thiruvananthapurm, Lucknow,
 Goa, Madurai, Mangalore, Agatti, Aurangabad, Khajuraho, Rajkot, Vadodara, Bhopal, Indore, Nagpur, Vishakapatnam,
 Trichy, Bhubaneswar, Coimbatore, Patna, Port Blair, Varanasi, Agartala, Dehradun, Imphal, Ranchi, Raipur, Agra,
 Chandigarh, Dimapur, Jammu and Pune, may be taken up simultaneously by AAI.  DPRs in respect of  25 non-metro
 airports have been prepared till date.    In view of the congestion at airports and  in order to improve terminal and air-
side facilities, AAI has initiated action for works pertaining to terminal buildings along with associated infrastructure as
 also air-side works for some non-metro airports on requirement basis.
31.       While responding to a specific question on the delay in taking up the developmental works at these non-metro
 airports, the Secretary stated as under:
"The Airports Authority, while realizing that it has taken them a slightly long to finalise their preliminary activities is
 geared up to completed the development of the airside and their air terminal building in the next two-and-a-half years,
 that is, by the end of December, 2009".
32.       The Committee finds that the modernisation and expansion of some metro airports particularly of Kolkata and
 Chennai is also on hold for one reason or the other and privatised airports like Delhi are not giving the desired
 amenities to the air passengers.

SCHEMES UNDERTAKEN BY AAI IN NORTH EASTERN REGION
36.       On enquiry from the Committee regarding the status of airports in the North-eastern region the Ministry stated
 that Airports Authority of India (AAI) has taken up several schemes pertaining to development of airports in the North
 Eastern Region. The schemes in the North Eastern Region are not economically viable and operation at these airports
 does not generate adequate revenues even to meet the operational/recurring expenditure.   In view of this, airport
 projects in the North Eastern Region, which are being undertaken for socio-economic considerations, are being funded
 jointly by the North Eastern Council and Ministry of Civil Aviation.
37.       Two separate MOUs one for schemes approved by NEC and other for schemes sanctioned under Prime
 Minister’s initiative have been signed by AAI with North Eastern Council for development of airports under financial
 assistance from the North Eastern Council.   In accordance with the financing pattern of North Eastern Council, the
 expenditure to the extent of 60% of the project cost is met by the Council and the balance 40% is being provided as
 budgetary support by Ministry of Civil Aviation in the normal debt equity ratio of 1:1.

MERGER OF AIR INDIA LIMITED AND INDIAN AIRLINES LIMITED
46.       The Ministry was specifically asked about the merger of Air India and Indian Airlines Ltd.  In its response, the
 Ministry has stated that the Government has decided to merge the two airlines into a new company, which would
 further strengthen the public sector airlines.  The new airline would be the largest airline in the country comparable to
 other airlines in Asia and will provide an integrated international and national footprint.   The merger would enable
 these two airlines to pool their resources, achieve synergies, face competition and establish fresh benchmarks for
 efficiency and reliability.   The merger of the two airlines would be completed in a phased manner over the next two
 years.
47.       The Ministry has also stated that the merger is in keeping with the industry trend of moving towards
 consolidation and mergers enabling the airlines to achieve synergies and reduce costs.  The merged airline would be
 able to offer an integrated schedule from interior points in the country(currently served by Indian) to various
 international destinations (currently served by Indian and/or Air India) and vice-versa, offering seamless connectivity to
 passengers and also extending the connectivity of interior points to various international destinations via the major hub
 airports in India. 
48.       A bigger and stronger public sector national carrier will also help in expanding regional connectivity to hitherto
 under-serviced and un-serviced destinations.   While taking the merger decision, employees interests have been
 accorded prime importance.   The Government is committed to ensure that all legitimate interests of employee,
 including their current compensations, status, etc. are protected.   There will be no retrenchment and all employees of
 both the airlines will continue in the merged company.  The exercise of integrating manpower would be completed in a
 phased manner, on the basis of transparent and objective criteria.  A well-defined Grievance Redressal Machinery will
 also be put in place.
49.       The Committee raised the question on the issue of extra expenditure to be incurred on completing the process on
 which the Secretary, stated as under:
"Sir, there would be cost of the integration merger.   But the consultants have given a roadmap which indicates that on
 balance, there would a saving because there would be savings in terms of synergies, savings in terms of avoidance of
 duplication, etc.  So, at the end of the third year, there would be a saving of Rs.400 crore, taking into account the extra
 costs involved in the higher pay scales, etc".
50.       The Committee also expressed its concern over the issue of positioning of employees of both the carriers in the
 new entity for which the Secretary stated as under:
"Sir, I would be less than honest if I say that there will be no problems.  The HR issues in any merger cause problems,
 and when you have two large entities with 18,000 plus employees and 15,000 plus employees, it certainly not going to
 be an easy task.  But apart from the fact that there will be no retrenchment and nobody would lose his job and so which
 is the most basis thing, what the employees have been assured is that there will be a three-tier grievance redressal
 machinery which will be put in place..."

UNIFORM TAXATION OF ATF     
66.       During the course of the oral evidence of the representatives of Ministry of Civil Aviation, the Committee was
 informed that the domestic air transport industry of the nation has been facing serious problems due to high costs of
 operations. One of the major reasons for this is the heavy cost of Air Turbine Fuel (ATF).  Even though the pricing of
 ATF is now on import parity basis, the rates applicable for domestic operations continue to be significantly higher than
 that of international operations.  The cost of ATF goes up even further due to high rates of sales tax levied by the State
 Governments/Union Territory Administration varying from 25 per cent to 30 per cent which affects the viability of
 domestic airline operations.
67.       The Secretary, while tendering his evidence also raised this issue  before the Committee  and stated as under:
".....Sir, as you aware, is a very important and a major component of the variable cost of operations.   Sir, the cost in
 India, the way it is priced and the way there is excise duty and , then there is Sales Tax in the States, is much higher, at
 least 25-30 per cent higher than what it is overseas.  We have been requesting that at least it be notified as a declared
 good under section 14 of the Central Sales Tax Act for all types of aircraft; so that there is a cap on the quantum of levy
 which can be imposed on this.  Sir, presently it is four per cent; ...... we have got some relief in relation to smaller
 aircraft, but it is not yet available for the aviation sector and all the operators, as a whole".
 
68.       The Ministry was asked about the budget proposal to amend the Central Sales Tax to treat aviation turbine fuel
 as a declare goods for all small aircraft with a maximum take of less than 40,000 kg operated by scheduled carriers and
 also the impact of this amendment on the aviation sector for which the ministry replied that until now, this facility was
 available only to turbo-prop aircraft.   The present proposal to extend the concession to all small aircraft including jet
 aircraft operated by scheduled airlines would encourage and facilitate connectivity to non-metro and other smaller cities
 by more efficient small jet aircraft.
 
69.       The Cost of fuel is an important component of cost structure and has direct bearing on the profitability of any
 airline. High cost of ATF in the country increases the cost of operation of carriers which results in escalation in the
 airfares.  The Committee recommends that Ministry of Finance should sympathetically consider and give approval to
 the proposal of Ministry of Civil Aviation regarding notifying ATF as 'Declared Good' under Section 14 of Central
 Sales Tax Act on priority basis to all the aircraft  so that sales tax on ATF could be contained with the maximum rate of
 4%. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of Finance may also discuss the issue with the State
 Governments and try to pursuade them to reduce   the sales tax on ATF.  The Committee feels that restructuring the
 excise duty on ATF will have a positive impact on the development of civil aviation sector of the nation.
UTILISATION OF CAT III SYSTEM AT DELHI AIRPORT
70.       During the winter season, the air passengers are put into great hardship by cancellation/diversion of flights due
 to fog at Delhi airport.  The Committee sought the remedial actions proposed to avoid such a situation during the next
 year. The Ministry in its reply stated that the airlines are encouraged to upgrade their aircraft and train their pilots for
 operations in low visibility conditions.   Their flight schedules are approved on the basis of number of pilots trained by
 the operators for low visibility operations and the suitability of the planes for such operations.   If the operator cannot
 provide data for their capability to fly under low visibility, they are not allowed to schedule their flights during normal
 fog hours.  The Ministry also stated that airlines have been directed not to roster their CAT III trained pilots on
 international routes during the fog season.  DGCA also requires that the airlines should train their pilots for ILS CAT
 II/III operations.   Pilots who are CAT II/III qualified are approved as Instructor/Examiner so as to ensure that more
 trained pilots are available for CAT II/III operations during low visibility conditions. 
71.       The Committee is constrained to note that a huge investment has been made in installation of ILS CAT-III
 facilities at IGI airport.  However there is a lot of delay or cancellation of flights due to fog as there are not enough
 pilots trained to operate the flights during fog. It appears that steps taken by the Government in this regard have proved
 inadequate. The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry that Airlines have been directed not to roster their CAT III
 trained pilots on international routes during fog season and also recommended that  training of pilots to fly on low
 visibility conditions be extended to a maximum number of pilots in both the national carriers. The Committee
 recommends that strict penal provisions should be imposed on the airlines which are failing to give proper training to

The Committee finds that the PHHL is without a regular CMD for quite some time and a Joint Secretary of the Ministry
 is holding additional charge of CMD of PHHL which is affecting the functioning of PHHL.  The Committee desires
 that in the larger interest of PHHL a regular CMD preferably from the PHHL establishment should be appointed on
 priority basis. (Paras 44, 45)
MERGER OF AIR INDIA LIMITED AND INDIAN AIRLINES LIMITED
            The Committee feels that the merger of these two national carriers would definitely result in proper
 synergisation of resources and enhance both financial and physical performance of both these carriers.  The Committee
 also feels that this process will help both the national carriers in long run in consolidating their position in domestic and
 international market.   The Committee hopes that the synergisation process would help to improve the operational
 efficiency of both the carriers. However, the Committee would like the Government to take care of the  interests of the
 employees in the new merged entity as merger of such large institutions always results in resentment amongst the
 employees as they are likely to lose their existing work position in the new merged entity.    The Committee notes the
 assurance given by the Government that there would be a three tier grievance cell to take care of the grievances of the
 employees of both the carriers after the merger. The Committee hopes that the mechanism of grievance redressal
 proposed by Government will be able to clear the doubts in the minds of employees. (Para 51)
NATIONAL CIVIL AVIATION POLICY
            The Committee notes that the present civil aviation sector needs a well balanced and market oriented policy to
 address all the issues relating to the boom in passenger and cargo traffic.  The quantum of increase in passenger traffic
 needs strict enforcement of safety and security related issues.  The Committee, however, is constrained to note that
 Ministry of Civil Aviation has not come out with a Civil Aviation Policy till date. Now the Government plans to have a
 policy with a vision for 2020.  The Committee hopes that the policy will be in place soon and take care of all the issues
 relating to civil aviation sector of current as well as future era.  (Para 54)
RESTRUCTURING OF DELHI AND MUMBAI AIRPORTS
            While scrutinizing the outcome budget of the Ministry for the year 2006-07 the Committee finds that a
 substantial amount of money has been spent by the AAI for repair and maintenance work at international airports at
 Delhi and Mumbai even after these two airports were handed over to the JVCs in May, 2006.  The Committee desires
 to know the reasons for this and also wants to know the expenditure incurred by the JVCs on the respective airports for
 maintenance and up keep of airports till date.
            A Tripartite Committee with the representatives of Ministry of Civil Aviation, Airports Authority of India and
 AAI Employees Joint Forum has been constituted by the Ministry of Civil Aviation on     22
nd February, 2006 to look
 into the issues and proposals of modernizing airports by Airports Authority of India and employees related issues
 including job security.  The Committee desires to know the details of meetings which have been taken so far with the
 decisions arrived therein.  The Committee also reiterates its recommendation contained in its 106
th Report that the
 Tripartite Committee should hold regular meetings and finalise its Report in a time bound manner in view of the
 importance of the issues relating to the Committee.

            There are also reports that after the work of modernisation of Delhi and Mumbai Airports has gone in the hands
 of private operators, the Ministry of Tourism even finding difficult to have space at the airports to display the publicity
 materials meant for information of the tourists particularly coming from abroad.  This gives an impression that there is
 a lack of coordination between the private operators and the Government agencies.  The Committee recommends that
 Government should look into the matter and take remedial action to ensure that Ministry of Tourism and other agencies
 which have to work at the airports to provide amenities to the passengers and tourist in particular do not face any
 problem.                    (Paras 56, 57, 58)       
CHENNAI AND KOLKATA AIRPORTS
 
            The Committee is constrained to note that the indecisiveness is preventing with regard to modernisation of
 Kolkata and Chennai Airport as Government is yet to give its approval for modernisation plans of these two Airports.
 The Committee recommends that the modernisation of Chennai and Kolkata airports should be completed on priority so
 as to ease the traffic over Delhi and Mumbai airports.  The Committee also desires that both these airports may be
 developed as international hubs to cater the needs of the people in the eastern and southern part of the country.  The
 Committee hopes that the Airports Authority of India will complete the all modernisation and developmental works of
 Kolkata and Chennai airports within a specified time frame.(Para 62)
SHORTAGE AND TRAINING OF PILOTS
            The Committee hopes that modernization of IGRUA and establishment of new pilot training institute in Gondia
 will help to meet the shortage of pilots. The Committee recommends that more training institute like that of the
 proposed one of the Gondia may also be established at conspicuous places in the Northern, Eastern and Southern parts
 of the country to meet the shortage of Pilots. (Para 65)
UNIFORM TAXATION OF ATF
The Cost of fuel is an important component of cost structure and has direct bearing on the profitability of any airline.
 High cost of ATF in the country increases the cost of operation of carriers which results in escalation in the airfares. 
 The Committee recommends that Ministry of Finance should sympathetically consider and give approval to the
 proposal of Ministry of Civil Aviation regarding notifying ATF as 'Declared Good' under Section 14 of Central Sales
 Tax Act on priority basis to all the aircraft   so that sales tax on ATF could be contained with the maximum rate of 4%.
 The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of Finance may also discuss the issue with the State
 Governments and try to pursuade them to reduce   the sales tax on ATF.  The Committee feels that restructuring the
 excise duty on ATF will have a positive impact on the development of civil aviation sector of the nation. (Para 69)
UTILISATION OF CAT III SYSTEM AT DELHI AIRPORT
            The Committee is constrained to note that a huge investment has been made in installation of ILS CAT-III
 facilities at IGI airport.  However there is a lot of delay or cancellation of flights due to fog as there are not enough
 pilots trained to operate the flights during fog. It appears that steps taken by the Government in this regard have proved
 inadequate. The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry that Airlines have been directed not to roster their CAT III
 trained pilots on international routes during fog season and also recommended that  training of pilots to fly on low
 visibility conditions be extended to a maximum number of pilots in both the national carriers. The Committee
 recommends that strict penal provisions should be imposed on the airlines which are failing to give proper training to
 their pilots in the upgraded instrument landing systems.  The Committee hopes that incidents of cancellation of flights
 during the winter season in 2007 will be minimum.(Para 71)

 budgetary support is examined and funds apportioned on the basis of progress and requirement of the scheme. To ensure

TONNAGE TAX REGIME
36.       The Government has rationalized the fiscal regime for Indian Shipping Industry by introducing Tonnage Tax system
 from the financial year 2004-05, in order to provide Indian Shipping industry a level playing field vis-à-vis International
 shipping companies and also facilitate the growth of Indian tonnage. In response to introduction of Tonnage tax regime and
 also due to current shipping boom, Indian Tonnage has steadily grown in the last about 2 years. Indian tonnage as on
 01.06.2004 was 7.05 million Gross Tonnage (GT) which has increased to 8.42 million GT as on 03.12.2006. Dredgers have
 also been included in the Tonnage Tax regime as per Finance Act 2005-06.
37.       Inland Water Transport and Coastal Vessel Transport in the country do not have the critical mass to compete with the
 other mode of transport on its own and for its development requires fiscal support from the Government. The Committee in its
 105
th Report on Demands for Grants for 2006-07 of the Department of Shipping had recommended for inclusion of the vessels
 registered under Inland Vessels and Coastal Vessels Acts in the tonnage tax regime for development of the Inland Water
 Transport and Coastal Vessel Transport in the country. The Committee wanted to know about the progress made in the matter.
 The Department of Shipping in their written reply submitted that in the current year also the Department had taken up the
 matter with Ministry of Finance on various occasions, for inclusion of vessels registered under Indian Vessel Act and Coastal
 Vessel Act, under tonnage tax regime.  It was emphasized that these vessels are adversely affected as Section 33 AC benefit,
 which was available to them till 2003-04 (before introduction of tonnage tax) was withdrawn without extending the tonnage
 tax benefits.   However, this issue has not figured in the Budget of 2007-08 presented by Hon’ble Finance Minister in the
 Parliament.
38.       The Committee notes that with the introduction of the Tonnage Tax system and other fiscal incentives the Indian
 shipping companies have registered the growth of the Indian tonnage. However, the Committee is constrained to note that the
 vessels registered under the   Indian Vessels Act, 1917 and the Coastal Vessels Act, 1838 have not been included for the
 purpose of getting tonnage tax benefits. The Committee feels that Inland Water Transport and Coastal Vessel Transport in the
 country do not have the critical mass to compete with the other mode of transport on its own and for its development requires
 fiscal support from the Government. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department to impress upon the Ministry of
 Finance for extending the benefits of tonnage tax to these vessels registered under the Indian Vessels Act and Coastal Vessels
 Act so as to harness the IWT potential in the country.
CRUISE SHIPPING
39.       Cruise shipping is a fast growing sector globally. As a departure from the concept of cargo and passenger ships, cruise
 is like a moving township studded with all state of art facilities including all types of recreational activities. The idea is fast
 catching because journey on cruise is not only pleasurable, but also comparatively free from sea travel health hazards. The
 global scenario for cruise shipping is picking up very fast, with an annual increment from 10-20% in the cruise ship fleet and
 passengers carried. Experience in the Caribbean, Latin American and South-East Asian countries indicate that huge amount of
 foreign exchange can be earned by providing the right policy environment and infrastructure for the growth of cruise shipping.
 India with its vast and beautiful coastline, virgin forests and undisturbed idyllic islands, long historical and cultural tradition of
 architecture, theatre and performing arts can be a fabulous tourist destination. With a view to encourage cruise shipping in the
 country, Government is considering to bring out a comprehensive cruise shipping policy.
40.       The Committee wanted to know from the Department of Shipping about the progress made for development of
 infrastructure and other facilities for development of cruise shipping in both eastern and western coasts of the country. The
 Department of Shipping intimated that in order to promote cruise tourism, a Cruise Shipping Policy is under consideration of
 the Government.   The objective of the policy is to make India a major cruise destination by popularizing cruise shipping,
 facilitating creation of requisite infrastructure by creating a conducive environment.   Phased programme will be evolved for
 development of facilities at ports for cruise shipping. The development of cruise tourism infrastructure is to be done through
 port resources, financial support from Ministry of Tourism under their scheme for promoting tourism as well as private sector

file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/117thReport.htm[22-10-2018 12:22:07]
 investment.  Private sector participation will be encouraged for the development of cruise tourism infrastructure, wherever
 viable.   Moreover, 100% FDI is already permitted in shipping sector.  Guidelines exist permitting Private Sector participation
 in ports including cruise terminals.
41.       As regards the steps taken to promote the cruise shipping in the country, the Department of Shipping stated that the
 following steps have been taken and are being taken to encourage cruise shipping:

50.       The Seamen’s Provident Fund Scheme, 1966 framed under the Seamen's Provident Fund Act, 1966 was introduced
 retrospectively with effect from 1
st July 1964 to provide a provident fund for all seamen in view of obvious need to provide old
 age retirement benefits to seamen and to their family members in the event of the death. This was a contributory Provident
 Fund and the employees were required to deposit the Provident Fund contributions in respect of Seamen employed by them

 belonging to the Funds were invested in the Securities as per the pattern prescribed by the Ministry of Finance. As on 31
st
 December, 2006, the Organization is holding 34,931 accounts and the total amount of provident fund accumulations (including
 interest) is Rs.529,57,96,164/- this also includes an amount of Rs. 90,15,57,516,.17/- at risk due to securities scam, which
 came to notice in May, 2002.
 
51.       The Committee in its earlier Reports had recommended for recouping the shortage of an amount of Rs.92.78 crore in the
 Seamen Provident Funds. The Committee wanted to know from the Department of Shipping about the progress made in the
 matter so far, the Department of Shipping informed that the Government has approved the proposal in its meeting held on
 30.11.2006 to recoup the full amount of Rs. 92.78 crore in the Seamen’s Provident Fund. As per decision of the Government ,
 action is being taken to introduce a Bill to amend the Seamen’s Provident Fund Act 1966 with a view to distancing in

file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/117thReport.htm[22-10-2018 12:22:07]
 sequencing  the Government from the responsibility of the Fund in future and to  release the grant to Seamen’s Provident Fund.

“Sir, you have mentioned about Seamen’s Provident Fund.  You will be happy to note that after great persuasion, the
 Group of Ministers have finally recommended and the Cabinet has finally decided that Rs.92 crore, which were mis-
invested, would be reimbursed by the Government.  So, this is a very great decision of the Government of India.  But
 the Ministry of Finance said that before releasing this money, there must be a legislation in the Parliament that in such

 recoupment of Rs.92.78 crore in the Seamen’s Provident Fund. The Committee also notes that in order to ensure that such
 happenings are not repeated in future, a Bill to amend the Seamen’s Provident Fund Act, 1966 and to release the grant to
 Seamen’s Provident Fund is under consideration. However, the Committee disapproves the idea of linking the proposal for

 infrastructure and 3 for vessels) have been selected and Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between them and IWAI has
 been signed.  
 
73.       The Committee notes that the Department has prepared an action plan with total projected financial implication of Rs.
 751.18 crore for making the existing 3 National Waterways fully operational for navigation and shipping purposes within a
 span of two years. The Committee feels that the inadequate interest and investment in the sector is aggravating the problems of
 inland water transport.  The Committee is of the strong opinion that the development of the inland water transport sector will
 ultimately depend on the flow of investments, both public and private, primarily public and a multi-pronged approach in which
 the Government takes the responsibility by putting in place the necessary infrastructure for the inland waterways. Therefore,
 the Committee recommends the Department to achieve a vibrant inland water transport and endeavour should be made to
 integrate it with National Maritime Development Programme for overall development of the IWT sector.
CENTRAL INLAND WATER TRANSPORT CORPORATION

74.       The Committee was informed that the Central Inland Water Transport Corporation (CIWTC) Limited was incorporated
 on 11th February, 1967 by taking over all assets of the erstwhile River Steam Navigation Co. Ltd. and liabilities to the State
 Bank of India and Government of India under a scheme of Arrangement, approved by the Kolkata High Court on
 03.05.1967.The principal activities of the Corporation are transportation of cargo through Inland Waterways in the country and
 routes identified in the Protocol on Inland Water Transport between India and Bangladesh.
75.       The Corporation is under the administrative control of the Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways.
 CIWTC has its corporate office at Kolkata and various branch offices at Guwahati, Karimganj, Patna etc. The Corporation has
 at present 470 employees on its payroll and is headed by a full time Chairman-cum-Managing Director (CMD). There were
 two main divisions viz. River Service Division (RSD) and the Rajabagan Dockyard (RBD) headed by General Managers. The
 Rajabagan Dockyard stands transferred to Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers Limited (GRSE) w.e.f. 1
st July, 2006 as
 per decision of the Cabinet taken in its meeting held on 1.12.2005. The River Services Division is engaged in cargo movement
 in the riverine routes of NW-I and NW-2 besides export to Bangladesh. The existing fleet strength of the CIWTC is about 101
 vessels, out of which 51 vessels are operational, 23 vessels awaiting repair and 17 vessels are under repair.
76.       The Committee wanted to know the latest position about the implementation of Voluntary Retirement Scheme in the
 CIWTC, the Department of Shipping informed that the Government had decided to bring down the manpower level to 43 from
 the exiting level of 1080 by introduction of the Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS).  It was expected that by 31.3.2006 about
 323 employees would opt for VRS and the level of manpower will gradually come to the level of 43 by end of December,
 2006.  Accordingly, the provision of Rs.3.60 crore for payment of salary/wages of CIWTC during 2006-07 was made.  
 However, the VRS introduced did not yield the desired result. Hence, the amount of Rs.3.60 crore was found to be insufficient
 to meet the salary/wages. With Rs.3.60 crore, the salary/wages for only four months of 2006-07 could be met. Hence, it was
 found necessary to augment the provision by Rs.5.40 crore to meet the salary/wages for the balance period of 6 months. The
 present strength of the employees is 470.   267 workers have so far opted for VRS.  It is proposed to keep VRS open even
 during 2007-08 to bring down the manpower strength further.
77.       The Committee had received a representation from the employees of the CIWTC regarding employment protection
 through merger process, which inter-alia states that the Cabinet decision allowed merger of Rajabagan Dockyard with Garden
 Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers Limited (GRSE) with a total employees strength of 371. However, only 314 employees
 were taken over by GRSE as employees of RBD and the remaining 57 employees (371-314=57) were not taken. There is no
 denying the fact that its Head Office had been acting as the brain of RBD’s operation since its nationalization (1967) prior to
 IGN&R and RSN. Rajabagan Dockyard (RBD) was a factory and its Head Office was situated at Kolkata. The reason for
 absorption of 57 employees in GRSE arises from the fact that the 57 employees of the present Head Office were involved in
 the matters of Personnel, Administration, Finance and Accounts, legal and other related matters for the erstwhile RBD. The
 Staff were vice versa posted and transferred by its Head Office and Factory, it was directly co-related with each other, and also
 few staff were appointed at Rajabagan Dockyard (RBD) and later they were allowed to work in its Head Office. Unfortunately,
 GRSE did not take into consideration the spirit of the Cabinet decision to re-employ 371 employees in the handing over
 process by way of excluding 57 employees whose future has been dumped to utter uncertainty.
78.       The Committee has been informed that the creation of Inland Water Authority of India was a right step towards toning
 up the Inland Water Transport system but unfortunately it has failed miserably to address the situation. To facilitate the River
 Services Division (RSD), it should be amalgamated physically either with Inland Water Authority of India (IWAI), Kolkata
 Port Trust (KoPT) or Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), to create a synergy of River Services Division’s role in River
 Transport segment in the country. Therefore, it is high time to look into the earlier proposal to club the CIWTC with IWAI
 immediately so that many of the structural crisis of CIWTC are removed and existing employees are given jobs in the above
 segments. In fact, the massive thrust on IWT Sector in different Plan Period documents gives enough space to accommodate to
 strengthen the operations of IWAI, by way of taking over CIWTC operations. The RBD operations were taken over by GRSE
 to strengthen the Defence operation and in fact, taking over the Rajabagan Dockyard (RBD) with GRSE made their views as
 the best Defence Shipyard in the country. Thus, the clubbing of remaining CIWTC with IWAI, would create a solid Plinth for
 national economic development.
 
79.       The Committee notes with dismay that though the Cabinet had decided to absorb all 371 employees of Rajabagan
 Dockyard (RBD) with Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers Ltd. (GRSE), however, only 314 employees were taken over
 by GRSE. The Committee is surprised to note that GRSE has not only ignored the decision of the Cabinet but also made the 57
 employees of the headquarters of the merged entity, the worst victim of non-implementation of merger process who had been
 acting-brain of RBD's operation since its nationalization. The Committee recommends the Government to take steps to ensure
 that the remaining 57 employees are also taken into the pay-roll of GRSE as decided by the Cabinet.
 
80.       The Committee is constrained to note that inspite of its recommendation in the past, the Government has not come out
 with a complete blueprint for making full use of the existing assets of River Service Division (RSD). The Committee is of the
 opinion that CIWTC with its infrastructure and expertise can play an integral part for development and promotion of inland

 water transport through NW-I and NW-II. The Committee recommends that possibility may also be explored to physically
 amalgamate the remaining CIWTC with Inland Water Transport Authority of India (IWAI) or Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) or
 Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), so that the infrastructure and expertise of CIWTC can be utilized for development of
 waterways transport.
 
OBSERVATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS – AT A GLANCE
 
APPRAISAL OF THE 10TH PLAN AND THE ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2007-08
            The Committee is distressed to note that during the 10 th Plan, the Department of Shipping was allocated Rs.2570.89
 crore as budgetary allocation under the plan scheme which was reduced to Rs.1700.00 crore at the RE stage. The Committee
 does not see any merit therein and strongly disapproves the idea of reduction of plan outlay because once it is reduced by the
 Government at the beginning of the Five Year Plan itself it will certainly affect and jeopardise many of the plan activities of
 the Department. The Committee is further constrained to note the shortfall in utilization of funds in almost all the major
 activities of Department of Shipping i.e. Inland Water Transport, Shipping, Ports, Lighthouses and Lightships, Shipbuilding
 etc. During 2005-06, the utilization of funds was Rs.346.83 crore against RE Rs.405.00 crore, in 2006-07, the utilization of
 funds was Rs.510.21 crore against RE Rs.575.00 crore and Rs.759.00 crore has been allocated for BE 2007-08. The
 Committee is aware that the main reason for effecting reduction in funds at RE stage by the Ministry of Finance is the inability
 of the Department of Shipping to spend their allocated funds during the first two quarters of almost every  year.  The
 Committee observes that the major portions of the budgetary outlay had been utilized during the last two quarters of the
 financial year by the Department. The Committee disapproves the practice as the funds crucial for the development of
 Shipping and Port Sectors infrastructure are withheld in the process. The Committee notes that the reasons advanced by the
 Department for non-utilization are administrative in nature for which corrective action could have been taken in advance. The
 Committee, therefore, recommends the Department to plan and incur their expenditure in a proportionate manner so that it is
 evenly spread throughout the year so that the funds are utilised appropriately for the purposes and no alibi should be provided
 to the Ministry of Finance to reduce the allocations at the RE stage.                       
                                                                                              (Para 10)
            The Committee also recommends that the Department of Shipping should do away with procedural hurdles and
 maintain close liaison for the purpose of review, monitoring, implementation and co-ordination of programmes/activities. The
 Committee hopes that Department of Shipping would take all corrective steps in this regard to avoid shifting of focus from the
 shipping sector in the next plan.  (Para 11)
PORT SECTOR
The Committee notes with concern that the budgetary allocation under the Plan scheme for port sector of the
 Department during the entire five years of the 10
th Plan had been slashed down consecutively and was subjected to heavy
 reduction at the RE stage. The Committee is perturbed to note that during the 10 th Plan, the Ministry of Finance imposed a cut
 of Rs.3344.20 crore or 57%  bringing it down from Rs.5954.84 crore to Rs.2610.64 or 43% at the RE stage, on the basis of
 poor utilization pattern of the Department of Shipping. In BE 2006-07, an outlay of Rs.1364.25 crore comprising of Rs.476.12
 crore as gross budgetary support was provided to the port sector and Department of Shipping had been able to utilize
 Rs.1024.53 crore or 75% of the budgetary allocation during the year. The Committee is constrained to note that the
 Department has given reasons which are routine in nature for non-utilization of funds which do not justify the slow pace and
 under-utilization by the Department. For example, schemes to provide infrastructure facilities at Minicoy, Agatti and Amini
 Islands could not progress mainly on account of constraints of transporting materials.   The Committee also notes that in order
 to ensure optimum utilization of funds, token provision have been kept in BE 2007-08 for schemes for which approval of the
 competent authority is yet to be received. The Committee feels that the underutilization of funds would have an adverse impact
 on the ongoing and future capacity building projects in the port sector. The Committee, recommends, the Department to adhere
 to strict fiscal discipline and fix the responsibility for persistent underutilization of allocated funds and take remedial measures
 thereon for optimum utilization of allocated funds during the year and inform the Committee about the measures taken by the
 Department in this regard.                                                                                  (Para 17)
            The Committee further recommends that learning from the experience of the 10
th Plan, planning for the 11 th Plan be
 done in such a way that there will be maximum utilization of funds allocated during each year of the Plan period.
(Para 18)
            The Committee notes that during the 10 th Plan, the aggregate capacity in the major ports was 508.60 MTPA and the
 traffic handled was 463.84 MT. The Committee also notes that the Department of Shipping is hopeful of enhancing the traffic
 and capacity in the major ports from 708.09 MT to 1001.80 MT respectively by the end of the 11 th Plan. The Committee is of
 the opinion that to achieve the traffic projection targets modernization of the port infrastructure is essential in a big way.

file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/117thReport.htm[22-10-2018 12:22:07]
 However, the Committee would like to caution the Government that more than 50% investment i.e. Rs.36868 crore of total
 investment of Rs.68972 crore is projected to be contributed by private sector. The Committee feels that hospitable
 environment, good legislative support, transparent bidding procedure and selection criteria and decision making process can
 give boost to the public- private partnership in the port infrastructure sector. The Committee further desires that in order to
 achieve the projected targets of capacity expansion of the port, the Department should standardize the bidding evaluation and
 selection procedure, remove bottlenecks and procedural rigidities   and ensure transparency in selection and implementation
 process of private operators for BOT projects.             (Para 23)
            The Committee also recommends the Government and in particular to Planning Commission to act fast on the proposals
 of the Department of Shipping for commissioning of new major ports for increasing output capacity during the 11 th Plan in the
 country.                                                                                              (Para 24)
            The Committee is constrained to note that the insufficient capacity and quality of the existing rail-road connectivity is
 affecting the smooth and efficient flow of cargo in and out of the major ports. The Committee notes that of late the
 Government have taken up the matter with some seriousness and thereby Committee on Infrastructure had set up a Committee
 of Secretaries to review the rail-road connectivity and suggested that each major port should preferably have minimum four
 lane road connectivity and double line rail connectivity. The Committee agreeing with the suggestions of the Committee of
 Secretaries recommends the Government to provide better rail road connectivity as suggested by the Committee of Secretaries
 and ensure strict monitoring   for timely completion of the projects in all the major and other ports. The critical infrastructure
 gaps can be bridged under viability  gap funding scheme for augmenting larger flow of funds for development of connectivity
 projects in the major ports.                          (Para 27)
            Now, a large number of private ports have also been set up in the country. They should be asked to take over the
 responsibility of building the connectivity requirements and the Government should also explore the possibility of creation of a
 Corpus Fund to take care of the connectivity problems of all ports as suggested by the Secretary, Department of
 Shipping.                                                             (Para 28)
TSUNAMI REHABILITATION PROGRAMME
            The Committee notes with anguish that the Restoration, Rehabilitation Works as well as creation of additional facilities
 in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands under the Tsunami Rehabilitation Programme has not been given much attention by the
 Department of Shipping although an action plan for rehabilitation of port structures and creation of additional facilities has
 been initiated with an estimated cost of Rs.976.19 crore and the Government has already approved an amount of Rs.897.31
 crore. The Committee, however, is surprised to note the Department of Shipping could utilize only Rs.18.58 crore in 2005-06
 and Rs.24.15 crore in 2006-07. The Committee finds that there has been a large short fall in the utilization pattern with the
 causal pace of the progress of work. The Committee has a doubt whether any Action Plan was chalked out by the
 Government.  The Committee recommends the Department to have focused approach for providing the infrastructure facilities
 for the Andaman and Nicobar islands within the stipulated time frame and if need be a task force may be formed for
 monitoring the pace of implementation of the programme and keep the Committee informed about the progress in the
 matter.                                                                                  (Para 31)
CALCUTTA DOCK LABOUR BOARD
            The Committee notes that a proposal for release of one time grant of Rs.738.71 crore has been submitted to the Cabinet
 for financial assistance on account of payment of arrears of pensions and pensionary dues of CDLB and the  proposal is under
 consideration of the Committee of Secretaries. The Committee also notes that the Department is working out  a scheme for
 merger of CDLB with KoPT in consultation with the Department of Expenditure. The Committee is of the express opinion that
 liability on account of the payment of arrears of pensions and pensionary dues of CDLB solely lies on the Government and the
 problem of payment of pension and pensionary dues can be resolved only if, the Government approves self sustaining proposal
 for an initial corpus with appropriate policy and methodology for disbursement of pension and pensionary dues. The
 Committee welcomes the move of the Government for merging of CDLB with KoPT and financial restructuring of the KoPT
 to counter the adverse impact of the merger. The Committee recommends the Department that till the time the financial
 restructuring and merger of CDLB takes place, the Government should act upon releasing enhanced grant to CDLB for
 meeting its pensionary and other statutory liabilities.                                                                                                               (Para
 35)
TONNAGE TAX REGIME
            The Committee notes that with the introduction of the Tonnage Tax system and other fiscal incentives the Indian
 shipping companies have registered the growth of the Indian tonnage. However, the Committee is constrained to note that the
 vessels registered under the   Indian Vessels Act, 1917 and the Coastal Vessels Act, 1838 have not been included for the
 purpose of getting tonnage tax benefits. The Committee feels that Inland Water Transport and Coastal Vessel Transport in the
 country do not have the critical mass to compete with the other mode of transport on its own and for its development requires
 fiscal support from the Government. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department to impress upon the Ministry of
 Finance for extending the benefits of tonnage tax to these vessels registered under the Indian Vessels Act and Coastal Vessels

 Act so as to harness the IWT potential in the country.                                                         (Para 38)
CRUISE SHIPPING
            The Committee is constrained to note that despite the country having a large coast line, no policy for cruise shipping has
 been framed till date. The Committee notes that the Department of Shipping is formulating a cruise shipping policy for
 popularizing cruise shipping and development of infrastructure and other facilities in the country. The Committee also notes
 that in order to encourage the cruise shipping in the country, the Department has provided incentives to encourage private
 sector participation for development of cruise tourism facilities at ports on Eastern as well Western coasts. The Committee
 recommends the Department to expedite the process and bring out a comprehensive cruise shipping policy for the growth of
 the cruise shipping in the country within a time frame so that the boom in cruise shipping be tapped to the extent
 possible.                                              (Para 42)
MULTIPLICITY OF TAXES
            The Committee notes with concern that there exists a multiplicity taxes in the shipping sector due to which Indian
 tonnage is loosing out a competitive edge. The Committee is constrained to note that the Minimum Alternate Tax, Corporate
 Income Tax, Withholding Tax, Income Tax for Indian Seafarers, Custom and Central Excise Duties on Capital Investment and
 Service Tax etc. have deterring effects and are putting extra burden on the Shipowners whereas their foreign counterparts do
 not have to pay such taxes. This is hampering the growth of this vital sector in the country. The Committee, therefore,
 recommends the Department to pursue the matter of rationalization and reduction of taxes which have adverse impact on the
 growth of the Shipping Sector, with the Ministry of Finance more vigorously for suitable corrective measures to boost the
 shipping sector of the nation and inform the Committee of the outcome therefrom.                                     (Para 44)
HUMAN RESOURCES DEVELOPMENT
            The Committee is constrained to note that despite knowing fully well about the shortage of trained manpower in
 maritime sector, the Government have not taken adequate steps to meet the shortage. As per the estimates of the Indian 
 National Shipowners Association (INSA)  there was shortage of 834 officers during 2006-07 which is likely to increase by
 20% during 2007-08. Globally also as per BIMCO/ISF manpower Summary Report, there will be shortage of approximately
 27000 officers by 2015 which will further aggravate the problem of trained manpower in the country. The Government,
 however, is considering a proposal to allow foreign officers to work on Indian ships besides increasing the training facilities to
 increase the trained manpower. The Committee notes that there are four maritime training institutes being run under the
 Government sector apart from there are 124 maritime institutes  in the private sector imparting pre-sea and post-sea training in
 various disciplines. The Committee observes that since there are sizeable number of private institutes imparting maritime
 training all over the country, there is a need to provide institutional and integrated course in the country’s maritime human
 resources development. The Committee feels that the shortage of Indian officers can be made good by increasing training
 facilities in the country. The Committee recommends the Department to formulate the guidelines for affiliation of these private
 institutes and standardize the quality of such education and training through affiliation and academic supervision for achieving
 excellence in the maritime sector.                                                                       (Para 49)
RECOUPMENT OF SEAMEN’S PROVIDENT FUND
            The Committee is happy to note that as per its recommendations, the Government has approved the proposal for

 recoupment of Rs.92.78 crore with the amendment of Seamen’s Provident Fund Act. Because misappropriation of the amount

The Department of Road Transport and Highways under the Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and
 Highways has been entrusted primarily with the functions of construction and maintenance of National Highways
 (NH), administration of Motor Vehicles Act and Central Motor Vehicles Rules, formulation of broad policies relating
 to road transport, environmental issues, automotive norms, etc., besides making arrangements for movements of
 vehicular traffic with neighbouring countries. There are two Wings in the Department, namely, the Road Transport
 Wing and the Roads Wing.
 
2.         The Road Transport Wing of the Department is concerned with the formulation of broad policies related to road
 transport besides making provisions for the movement of vehicular traffic with the neighbouring countries.   The
 following Acts/Rules which embody the policy relating to motor vehicles and State Transport Corporations are being
 administered in the Road Transport Wing of the Ministry:-
 
·
        The Motor Vehicles Act 1988
·        The Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989
·        The Road Transport Corporations Act 1950
·        The Carriers Act, 1865
 
3.         The development and maintenance of National highways are being implemented on agency basis.  Out of the
 total length of 65,569 km of National Highways, 44,217 km is with the State Public Works Departments (State PWD),
 15,312 km with the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and 5,090 km with Border Roads Organisation
 (BRO).  Balance length of 950 km is yet to be entrusted to executing agencies. 
 
4.         Our country having one of the largest road networks of 3.32 million km, consists of expressways, National
 Highways, State Highways, Major District Roads, Other District Roads and Village Roads with following length
 distribution:
 
   
National Highways/Expressways : 66590 km
State Highways : 128000 km
Major and other District Roads : 470000 km
Rural Roads : 2650000 km
 
5.         The National Highways have further been classified depending upon the width formation. Generally, a lane has a
 width of 3.75 metres in case of single lane and 3.5 metres in case of multi lane National Highways.  The break-up of
 National Highways in terms of width is as under:
Single Lane                                           21674 km                                32.55%
Double Lane/Intermediate Lane        36936 km                                     55.46%
Four/Six/Eight Lane                              7980 km                                 11.98%

 for the financial year 2007-08 was considered by the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
 Transport, Tourism and Culture at its meeting held on the 10
th  April 2007.  During the meeting, the Committee took
 oral evidence of the Secretary and other officers of the Department of Road Transport and Highways.

 entrusted to various agencies, such as State PWD, NHAI and BRO. When the Committee enquired about the reasons

15.       When the Committee expressed its displeasure in submitting routine replies every year for underachievement of
 targets, the Secretary responded that:
" ..... It is true that the same reason generally applies for delay, which is land acquisition and poorly performing
 contractors. But, certainly, we are expected to address these issues more expediously and with greater
 resolution, which we will do to out best".
 
16.       The Department was asked about the impact of budget 2007-08 on the road, transport and highways sector and
 the Department was asked whether the demands made in the BE 07-08 are adequate.  The Department in its reply to the
 Committee has stated that during the year 2007-08, excise duty on petrol and diesel has been reduced from 8% to 6%
 which will stimulate the growth of road transport sector in the country.  The road infrastructure has to keep pace with
 growing requirement of the transport industry.  Further, due to introduction of service tax on work contracts at the rate
 of 2%, perhaps the cost of work would increase.   Keeping in view above two facts, necessity to increase the budgetary
 estimates may be considered at the RE stage.  It is also noteworthy that none of the incentives provided for the Road
 Sector has been withdrawn.

 transport.  The outlay for the current year for this Department is Rs.12500.00 crore.  This amount has been stepped up

23.       The Committee finds that one of the most ambitious projects launched in road sector in independent India is the

 Notification in the Official Gazette, has entrusted to the Authority stretches of National Highways. The Programme is
 being implemented in phases.  Under Phase I & Phase II of this project, 13,146 km of National Highways are proposed

 the project more than 5 years. Though the Department of Road Transport and Highways has enumerated a number of
 steps taken to ensure early completion of the NHDP, like monitoring of contracts at various level, appointing of nodal
 officers by State Governments, constitution of Committee of Secretaries, simplification of procedure of land
 acquisition, action against non-performing contractors and improving cash flow problems of contractors. However,
 when it comes to the implementation of the projects, it appears that things have not improved.   The construction of
 flyover at Delhi - Badarpur    Border can be sighted as an example as how the procedural hurdle delaying in projects
 leading to cost overrun and time escalation.  The project was approved by the Department of Road Transport and
 Highways on 31
st March, 2005, however the project is yet to be finalised for want of a number of clearances.   This
 project forms part of Golden Triangle of Agra, Delhi and Jaipur where lakh of domestic and foreign tourists visit on it. 
 The project could have been taken on priority basis particularly taking into account in the Commonwealth Games,
 2010.  The Committee recommends that the steps enumerated by the Department for the early completion of the project
 should be implemented in letter and spirit so that there is not cost overrun and time overrun.  The Committee hopes that
 the Department would take necessary precautions in future while finalizing such type of projects which require huge
 amount of investment.  In this context the Committee reiterates its recommendation made in the 102
nd Report  that
 "proper verification of bank guarantees submitted by contractors should be undertaken at the initial stage itself to avoid
 termination of the contracts at a later stage.  The Committee notes that increasing numbers of contracts are under
 implementation and being awarded.  Therefore, it is recommended that the Department should be vigilant in respect of
 each contract and should strictly enforce the compensation conditions in the contracts in respect of non-performing
 contractors.    The Committee, further, recommends that the Department should not wait for the targeted date of
 completion to initiate action but should fix short-term targets for the contractors so that the projects can be monitored
 constantly and immediate and early remedial action may be taken in case of anticipated delays.  The Committee also
 feels that the Department should draw-up a database of the performance of the contractors involved in NHDP and
 encourage outstanding contractors, who strictly comply with the construction standards and quality control and also
 complete the projects well within the targeted date, to undertake more and more projects as incentives".

49.       The Department's attention was drawn to the Committee's earlier recommendation that the Department should
 finalize uniform norms for designs of roads and bridges incorporating the international norms for new National
 Highways and was asked to furnish the action taken in this regard. The Department in its reply stated that the standards
 and specifications for design and construction of roads and bridges have been formulated by the Indian Road Congress
 and the Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways.  These standards and specifications are prepared and
 updated regularly  keeping in view the developments in other countries and international norms.  The standards
 specified by the Bureau of Indian Standards are also used for material and other works.  These documents take care of
 the local requirement and local conditions as well as the international norms.
50.       When the Committee raised specific question on the role of an inspection agency in ensuring quality of roads, be
 it on the National Highways or the State Highways, the Secretary during his evidence stated as under:
"As far as the inspection of roads and quality control mechanism goes, these are quite well laid down.  We have
 our institutes within the Ministry.  CRRI is certainly used all the time.   Some of the States have their own
 agencies.  We get independent checks conducted.  The Ministry itself has a number of very well trained
 highway engineers.  So, we feels that on quality parameters, we are generally okay, not always, and the need has
 been expressed for an independent audit of the roads that we are building.   I think this is something which we
 have requested the NHAI to consider, to have a completely independent check on their roads".
 
51.       The Committee desires that there is a need for indigenization of norms regarding designing of roads and bridges
 taking into account the local site conditions.  The Committee hopes that there should be uniform norms/guidelines in
 the country for highway projects.  The Committee recommends that an independent agency should be appointed to
 monitor and inspect the quality of all works carried out by both the Governmental and also the private agencies. There
 are reports that Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi has made third party checks mandatory by a panel of
 institutes i.e., Delhi College of Engineering,  CRRI and IIT Delhi for all road works like strengthening and resurfacing. 
 The Committee desires that the Department may also involve similar mechanism to check the quality of repair work
 carried out on the National Highways and this independent audit should be made part of the contract while awarding it
 which will also ensure that works carried out are at par with international standards or norms.

52.       The encroachments on the National Highways particularly near urban localities is a common phenomenon and
 also the removal of encroachments is a continuous process and State Government concerned is taking necessary action
 for removal of encroachments whenever these are noticed. As per the Policy, no financial assistance is provided to the

 State Government for rehabilitation of the encroachers. However, the guidelines of World Bank and Asian
 Development Bank provide for extending assistance to ‘vulnerable encroachers’, which includes SCs, STs,
 handicapped and people falling below poverty line.  The Committee enquired about the steps taken by the Department
 of Road Transport & Highways to curtail encroachments of the land under the National Highways.  The Department
 replied that efforts are made to remove the encroachments on the lands pertaining to National Highways from time to
 time with the help of district authorities. Further, the Government has enacted the Control of National Highways (Land
 & Traffic) Act, 2002, to remove encroachments on NHs.  This Act has come into force with effect from 27.1.2005. 
 Under the provisions of the Act, Government has set up 192 National Highway Administrations at various locations in
 the country. One National Highway Tribunal (NHT) each at Chandigarh, Lucknow, Jabalpur, Kolkata, Guwahati,
 Mumbai, Chennai and Bangalore has also been notified.   Appointments of Presiding Officers have been made for the
 NHT at Lucknow and Chandigarh and proposals for filling up remaining posts of Presiding Officers are under
 consideration. The Committee was also informed that National Highway Administration (an Officer of Central / State
 Government as notified in the Gazette) has been empowered to remove encroachments on NHs under its jurisdiction.
 The power of appeal vests with National Highway Tribunal, which is the Appellate Authority on all such matters. The
 district courts do not have any jurisdiction in these matters. 
           
53.       The Committee enquired from the Department regarding filling up of vacancies of Presiding Officers of National
 Highways Tribunals and increasing number of NHTs in the country. The Department replied that the control of
 National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act, 2002 has come into effect from 27.01.2005.  In order to implement the
 various provisions of the Act, 8 National Highway Tribunals have been set up.  The Presiding Officers for two National
 Highways Tribunals have been appointed.  Action has been initiated to fill the remaining posts of Presiding Officers. 
 In his connection, a meeting of the Selection Committee constituted for the purpose has already been held on
 20.12.2006, which has recommended a few candidates for appointment to the post of Presiding Officers in National
 Highway Tribunals.  The names recommended by the Selection Committee are being processed further for seeking the
 approval of the Government. As per the proposal approved by the Government in connection with the enactment of the
 Control of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act, 2002, there is a provision for setting up of 28 National Highway
 Tribunals.  At present, there is not much work-load in the National Highway Tribunals.   So, far, cases have been filed
 only in National Highway Tribunal, Chandigarh.  The present work-load does not warrant setting up of additional
 National Highway Tribunals at this stage.  As and when work-load of the National Highway Tribunals increases, the
 proposal for setting up of additional National Highway Tribunals could be considered in future, based on increased
 work - load.

 huge loss of public property, hampers the smooth development of highways and is also an irritant in the timely

 encroachments.   The Committee feels that strict enforcement of Control of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act,
