 and the Department in its reply that a Committee under the Chairmanship of Shri D Thangaraj, Principal Secretary,
 Government of Karnataka has been constituted to finalise the National Road Transport Policy on 23.10.2006.  The
 other members of the Committee are Shri B N Puri, Adviser(Transport), Planning Commission, Shri Ramendra Jakhu,
 Princiapl Secretary(Transport), Government of Haryana, Shri Guru Prasad Mohapatra, Transport Commissioner,
 Government of Gujarat, Shri Ajay Mishra, Transport Commissioner, Government of Assam, Shri Arvind Kumar,
 Adviser(TR), Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways, Shri Anand Prakash, Director(RT), Department of
 Road Transport & Highways, Shri Avadesh Choudharay, Director(TRW).   The comments received on the draft Road
 Transport Policy and various recommendations of the parliamentary Standing Committee have been sent to the
 Committee for its consideration. The Committee is yet to submit its report The Committee has been requested to
 expedite the report. 
 
96.       Rapid development is taking place in transport sector. However, the Committee is constrained to note that there
 is no policy to regulate the development of transport sector in the country.  Now the Government is in the process of
 formulating the National Road Transport Policy. The Committee hopes that the new policy would address all the core
 issues related to road transport sector.
 
Strengthening public transport system including introduction of It like Automatic Fare Collection based on GPS:
 
97.       The Committee was informed that decline of public transport has been one of the failures of our transport
 planning over the years.  The percentage of buses in the total fleet of vehicles has come down from more than 11% in
 1951 to 1.1% in 2004.  This leads to increase in personalized transport which in turn has a number of adverse
 consequences such as congestion, pollution, and accidents apart from being unfair to the poor as they get excluded from
 transport services.  This needs to be reversed.  It is proposed that in the 11
th Five Year Plan the provisions should be
 made at the central    level to provide financial assistance to help the States to strengthen their public transport system
 including application of IT like automatic fare collection system based on GPS. However, such financial assistance
 shall be restricted to those States who undertake to take measures for reforms in the public transport system. An MOU 
 between the Central Government and the State Government embodying a  number of  reform  requirements  such as 
 rationalization of  taxes in  favour of  public transport, level playing field between private and public operators,
 freedom in the matter of fare fixation,  improvement in the basic infrastructure, professional management of STUs etc.
 is to be signed. The Central Government could provide outright grant to such States by linking the achievement of the
 reform agenda measurable by verifiable indices of increased provision and usage of public transport.  It could also
 provide guarantee to resource mobilisation by the States for investment in public transport including renewal and
 augmentation of bus fleet.  B.E of  Rs. 1 crore has been  allocated for this purpose during the year 2007-08.
 
Creation of  National Road Safety Fund
 
98.       The Committee finds that the Committee on Road Safety and Traffic Management constituted under the
 Chairmanship of Shri S. Sundar, former Secretary of erstwhile M/o Surface Transport and Distinguished fellow,  TERI
 has submitted its report to Hon’ble Minister, S,RT&H on 20.2.2007.  The Committee has recommended creation of a
 National Road Safety Board under a separate Act of the Parliament.  A provision of Rs. 1.00 crore has been proposed to
 create such a body in case a decision in the affirmative is taken by the Government.
 
99.       The Committee also enquired about the status of the dedicated safety fund as approved by the Committee on
 Infrastructure and in what manner this fund is proposed to be utilized. The Department replied that the Committee on
 Infrastructure headed by Prime Minister directed that 1% of Central Road Fund (CRF) meant for National Highways be
 earmarked for a dedicated Road Safety fund.  In order to decide quantum and determine utilization of dedicated Road
 Safety Fund, the matter was referred to the Committee headed by Shri S. Sundar, former Secretary, Ministry of Surface
 Transport(MoST), which was set up to deliberate and recommend creat6ion of a dedicated by on Road Safety and
 Traffic Management..    The Committee has recommended creation of a National Road Safety Fund. It has
 recommended that (i) minimum of 1% of the total proceeds of the cess on diesel and petrol should be earmarked for
 National Road Safety fund; (ii) at least 50% of the amount to be retained by the Government of India by way of share

 their entitlement (iii) the National Road Safety Fund to the states should be released to support road safety activities

100.     The Committee hopes that the recommendations of the S.Sundar Committee may be implemented on priority
 taking into consideration the issues involved therein.     The Committee desires that the setting up of the dedicated
 national road safety fund should not be delayed due to procedural constraints and other administrative issues.   The

TOLL TAX ON BRIDGES AND NATIONAL HIGHWAYS
 
101.     During the course of the evidence, the Committee enquired about policy of the Government with regard to
 collection of fee/toll tax on bridges and National Highways.  The Committee was informed by the Ministry of Road
 Transport and Highways that as per National Highways rules, user fee on bridges is being charged since 1976.  As per
 National Highways (Fee for the use of National Highway Section and permanent Bridge-Public Funded Projects) Rules,
 1997 & Amendment Rules 2001, user fee shall be levied as below:-
(a)
                For converting existing 2 lane National Highway Section into 4 laning facilities.
(b)               All projects costing more than Rs.100 lakhs each, completed and open to traffic after 1 st May 1992 but
 before 4th December 2001 and all projects costing more than Rs.500 lakhs each, completed on or after
 4th December 2001.
(c)                All road improvement projects/bridges and bypasses taken up on BOT basis.
 
102.     It has been further stated that the rate of fee as above shall be linked to the wholesale price index of a year and
 determined on yearly basis and be rounded to the nearest rupee by the Central  Government over the rates notified.  The
 rate of fee may be reviewed after every five years based on the wholesale price index and fixed in multiple of rupees
 five by the Central Government over the rates notified.  All fee levied under rules shall be collected by the executing
 agencies concerned, departmentally or through private contractors on the basis of competitive bidding on behalf of
 Central Government.   It further states that the fee shall be collected in perpetuity by the executive agency.   The fee
 collected for the bridges are allocated to the respective States for development of National Highways.
 
103.     The Committee took note of the fact that the toll for bridges and roads was to be collected in perpetuity and
 brought to the notice of the Secretary, Department of Road Transport and Highways that the Government was already
 levying a cess on petrol and diesel for the purpose.  In response, the Secretary clarified that the cess on petrol and diesel
 is for development whereas the toll is for maintenance of roads.
 
104.     The Committee is not convinced with the reasons advanced by the Department of Road Transport and Highways
 for collecting toll on roads and bridges in perpetuity.   The Committee feels that the Government is not justified in
 burdening the common users of highways with the development as well as the maintenance of the roads in the country. 
 The Committee had also commented upon this matter in its 67
th Report on Demands for Grants 2003-04 and
 recommended that once the cost of construction of a road/bridge plus interest is recovered, the collection of toll should
 be stopped.   The Committee also feels that there exists a need for the rationalisation of the toll tax being charged on the
 National Highways.  The Committee recommends that persons travelling on smaller stretches of the National Highways
 where toll is being collected should be charged a lower amount than the persons using the entire length of that National
 Highway.   The Committee also recommends that a one time revolving fund should be set up for all the major road
 projects in which share of road projects from CRF should be kept.  The Committee also expresses its concern over the
 multiple  taxation on the vehicle owners by way of tax on the time of purchase of vehicle, cess on purchasing of
 petrol/diesel and collection of toll when he uses tolled highways.  The Committee sees no logic behind such multiple
 taxation on vehicle owners.  The Committee recommends that on BOT Annuity basis contracts, the concessionaire

OBSERVATIONS/CONCLUSIOINS/RECOMMENDATIONS AT A GLANCE
 
THE TENTH PLAN PROVISIONS AND ANNUAL PLAN 2006-07
The Committee notes that trend of fund utilization pattern of the Department has been fluctuating as is evident
 from the above that Department utilized 98.16% of allocated fund whereas it could utilized only 52.08% of fund during
 2004-05.  This in turn has bearing on the performance of the Department of Road Transport and Highways.  The
 Committee hopes that the Department will take corrective measures to utilise the funds to the maximum extent possible
 during the Eleventh Five Year Plan.   The Committee also strongly recommends that the Department should evolve a
 mechanism to   monitor the utilization of funds periodically so that any shortcoming could be noticed and solved
 immediately.   The Department may also set up a coordination unit with all its Units and also with the State
 Governments, so that the funds earmarked for a particular year are spent timely.
(Para 9)
The Committee observes that the budgetary allocation of the Department of Road Transport and Highways was
 substantially increased from 2005-06(Revised Estimates) of Rs.13293.25 to Rs.14995.21 crore during 2006-07 and for
 2007-08(Budget estimates) the allocation has again been increased to Rs.16193.70 crore.  The Committee, therefore,
 reiterates its earlier recommendation that the Department should devise strategies in such a way that they are able to
 fully utilize the funds placed at their disposal.  They should also evolve some mechanism to identify bottlenecks
 causing delays and work towards resolving all such hindrances in coordination with the all concerned agencies.   This
 would help them to avoid time overrun and consequential cost overrun of the projects to be executed by them.   The
 Committee desires that the State Governments may be requested to send their plan for road projects well in time in
 order to spend the allocated outlay within the particular year.  The Committee also feels that since a large number of
 roads are being identified for up- gradation or inclusion in the NHDP, the Department should ensure that funds are
 utilized well in time for better road connectivity and also to generate good revenue by completing the projects in time.
(Para 22)
NATIONAL HIGHWAY DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME (NHDP)  
The Committee expresses concern over the fact that there are 7 stretches of Golden Quadrilateral still pending
 out of these 4 stretches are of more than 50 kms. length.   It indicates a sorry state of affairs that Golden Quadrilateral
 project which was scheduled to be completed by the end of 2003 have extended over four more years and now stretched
 upto 2007-08.  Still the Department has not chalked out strategies to deal with contract defaulters or legal wrangles. 
 The Committee also notes that 5 road stretches of N-S corridor and E-W corridor are also pending.  The Committee
 strongly recommends that all these works should be completed at the earliest.
The Committee notes that 94.77% of the Golden Quadrilateral Project has been completed by February, 2007. 
 The Committee expresses its concern over the slow progress of this project and rescheduling of target of completion of
 the project more than 5 years. Though the Department of Road Transport and Highways has enumerated a number of
 steps taken to ensure early completion of the NHDP, like monitoring of contracts at various level, appointing of nodal
 officers by State Governments, constitution of Committee of Secretaries, simplification of procedure of land
 acquisition, action against non-performing contractors and improving cash flow problems of contractors. However,
 when it comes to the implementation of the projects, it appears that things have not improved.  The construction of
 flyover at Delhi - Badarpur    Border can be sighted as an example as how the procedural hurdle delaying in projects
 leading to cost overrun and time escalation.   The project was approved by the Department of Road Transport and
 Highways on 31
st March, 2005, however the project is yet to be finalised for want of a number of clearances.   This
 project forms part of Golden Triangle of Agra, Delhi and Jaipur where lakh of domestic and foreign tourists visit on it. 
 The project could have been taken on priority basis particularly taking into account in the Commonwealth Games,
 2010.  The Committee recommends that the steps enumerated by the Department for the early completion of the project
 should be implemented in letter and spirit so that there is not cost overrun and time overrun.  The Committee hopes that
 the Department would take necessary precautions in future while finalizing such type of projects which require huge
 amount of investment.   In this context the Committee reiterates its recommendation made in the 102
nd Report that

ROADS OF INTER-STATE CONNECTIVITY AND ECONOMIC IMPORTANCE
            The Roads of Inter State connectivity and economic importance as evident by its projects are very crucial for
 interstate connectivity and should be handled with good spirit.  The Committee again finds that two important projects
 could not be taken-up for want of completion of one or the other formalities.   However sufficient fund should be
 allocated therefor.  The Committee hopes that the projects sanctioned under this head in the year 2005-06 and 2006-07
 are completed as per their scheduled dates of completion as these roads are vital in giving connectivity to destinations
 of economic and tourist importance.  (Para 48)
QUALITY CONTROL
The Committee desires that there is a need for indigenization of norms regarding designing of roads and bridges
 taking into account the local site conditions.  The Committee hopes that there should be uniform norms/guidelines in
 the country for highway projects.  The Committee recommends that an independent agency should be appointed to
 monitor and inspect the quality of all works carried out by both the Governmental and also the private agencies. There
 are reports that Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi has made third party checks mandatory by a panel of
 institutes i.e., Delhi College of Engineering,  CRRI and IIT Delhi for all road works like strengthening and resurfacing. 
 The Committee desires that the Department may also involve similar mechanism to check the quality of repair work
 carried out on the National Highways and this independent audit should be made part of the contract while awarding it
 which will also ensure that works carried out are at par with international standards or norms.(Para 51)
ENCROACHMENT
The Committee feels that the encroachment of land under National Highways is a serious issue as it involves
 huge loss of public property, hampers the smooth development of highways and is also an irritant in the timely
 completion of various projects.   The Committee recommends that suitable action should be taken to prevent
 encroachments.   The Committee feels that strict enforcement of Control of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act,
 2002 will play a major role in removing encroachments upon national highways.  The Committee hopes that the
 Department will fill up the vacancies on priority in National Highways Tribunals to ensure that the law regarding
 removal of encroachments on national highways is implemented in both letter and spirit.(Para 55)
 
 
 
CENTRAL ROAD FUND
The Committee notes that the issue of release of previous fund accruals to the Central Road Funds due to
 additional cess since 1.4.2003 still remains unresolved. The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation that the
 Department should take up the matter immediately with the Ministry of Finance to resolve the impasse in the non-
accrual of previous fund allocations from the CRF in view of high cost implementation of NHDP and also the inclusion
 of a large number of new roads which are being included in this project. The Committee desires that the Department
 should impress upon the State Governments to spend the allocated amount under this head optimally and periodically
 monitor the projects under taken by State Governments.
(Para 59)

 externally funded projects are completed within the stipulated period so that cost overrun do not occur on these
 projects. The Committee also desires the Department to ensure proper monitoring of these projects which carry a huge
 amount of overseas loan.(Para 74)

            The Committee notes that the number of road accidents in India are quite large in number and human and
 property on account of road accidents is also colossal.  In this context, the Committee is constrained to note that out of
 the allocated amount of Rs.14.80 crore for National Highways Accident Relief Scheme, the Department was able to
 spend an amount of Rs.6.58 crore till 31
st March 2007 which is less than 50% of the allocated amount.  The Committee
 in its earlier recommendation had asked the Department to pursue the matter with the Ministry of Health and Family
 Welfare for enhancing the financial assistance for hospital/trauma centres located on the National Highways to upgrade
 their facilities.  The Committee recommends that the Department should coordinate with all the State governments to
 ensure the availability of trauma centres and ambulances within reachable limits on all national highways so that
 fatality is checked to the extent possible. 
(Para 80)
NATIONAL DATA BASE NETWORK
The National Data Base Network project aims to bring about uniformity in Driving Licenses and Vehicle
 Registration documents issued by RTOs across the country.  The Committee however expresses its concern over the
 delay in implementation of this project even though there is no cost overrun in this project.   The Committee
 recommends that Department of Road Transport and Highways to persuade the States to implement the project in a
 time bound manner.  The use of smart cards can be useful only if all the DL & RC issuing authorities are covered under
 National Data Base Network. It will also ensure the transparency, responsiveness and e-governance in the transport
 sector through application of information technology.(Para 83)

 during 2006-07.  The Committee is convinced that “importance of accurate data and well-researched insight to aid
 informed policy-making can not be overstated” accepted by the Department as a mere rhetoric and not supported by
 concrete actions.  The Committee is of the view that the unorganised sector of road transport has remained a neglected

 sector which will be useful in research and development activities also. (Para 88)

            The Ministry of Tourism is the nodal agency for overall policy planning and coordination of programmes of
 various activities of the Central Government agencies, State Governments/Union Territories and the Private Sector
 for the development and promotion of tourism in the country.  The Ministry plays a crucial role in coordinating and
 supplementing the efforts of the States/Union Territories Governments, catalyzing private investment, strengthening
 promotional and marketing efforts and in providing trained manpower resources. The activities of the Ministry
 mainly consists of the following functions:-
 
·
        Framing of policy matters on development of tourism

·        Encouragement of Public Private participation in tourism infrastructure development
·        Promotion and marketing of Tourism Products within the country and abroad
·        Providing incentives in the accommodation sector
·        Regulation of tourism industry
·        Investment facilitation
·        Human Resource Development and Training
·        Research, analysis, monitoring and evaluation
·        International Cooperation of promotion and development of India Tourism
 
2.         The administrative head of the Ministry is the Secretary (Tourism).  The Secretary also acts as the Director
 General (DG) Tourism. The office of the Director General of Tourism {now merged with the office of Secretary
 (Tourism)} provides executive directions for the implementation of various policies and programmes.  Directorate
 General of Tourism has a field formation of 20 offices within the country and 13 offices abroad and one sub-ordinate
 office/project i.e. Indian Institute of Skiing and Mountaineering (IISM)/Gulmarg Winter Sports Project (GWSP).
 The activities of IISM/GWSP have been revived and various ski and other courses are conducted in the J&K valley. 
 In addition to the Headquarters Organization at New Delhi, the Directorate General of Tourism has 20 India tourism
 Offices in the country (including 5 Regional Offices), situated at New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Guwahati
 and other offices are located at Agra, Bhubaneswar, Aurangabad, Bangalore, Kochi, Hyderabad, Imphal, Jaipur,
 Khajuraho, Naharlagun, Panaji (Goa), Patna, Port Blair, Shillong and Varanasi.  There are 13 India tourism Offices
 Overseas, which include 5 Regional Offices at, New York, Frankfurt, Dubai, Sydney and Tokyo.  The other India
 tourism Offices are located at Los Angeles, Toronto, London, Paris, Amsterdam, Milan, Johannesburg and
 Singapore. The overseas offices are primarily responsible for tourism promotion and marketing in their respective
 areas and the field offices in the country are responsible for providing information service to tourists and to monitor
 the progress of field projects.

DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM INFRASTRUCTURE AND DESTINATIONS
 
23.       The Committee has been informed that during the 10 th Plan, a paradigm shifts in tourism planning and
 development have yielded quantum increases in tourist footfalls.  The Ministry of Tourism has focused on
 infrastructure development in certain key destinations–Ajanta-Ellora, Bodhgaya-Rajgir-Nalanda, Kurukshetra,
 Mahabalipuram.  An integrated approach with all backward-forward linkages was adopted in these destinations. 
 This has yielded larger tourism volumes and revenues, thereby contributing significantly to the national economy
 and the rural sector in particular. This thrust for infrastructure development has been achieved in combination with
 care for the carrying capacity of destinations, visitor satisfaction and local community sensibilities.
 
24.       In the 10
th Five Year Plan, the eight schemes providing Central assistance for tourism infrastructure
 development from previous plan period were merged into two schemes, i.e., Integrated Development of Tourist
 Circuits; Product/Infrastructure and Destination Development.  Recognizing the need to regulate tourism product
 development, these two schemes were further merged into one scheme for Product/Infrastructure Development for
 Destinations and Circuits with the following components, namely, Major Destinations and Circuits development;
 Rural Tourism infrastructure development.
 
25.       The Committee was informed that at the beginning of the 10
th Plan the Central Financial Assistance to the
 States had not been able to create a major impact in terms of creation of world-class tourism infrastructure. 
 Therefore, in order to provide quick and substantial impact, the revised scheme was taken up  to identify key tourism
 circuits in the country on an annual basis, and develop them to international standards, with the objective of
 providing all infrastructure facilities required by the tourists within these circuits.  The circuits prioritized/sanctioned
 for development during the 10th plan period are given at Annexure-IV.
 
26.       In the 9 th Plan, destination development had tended to be somewhat ad hoc, with inadequate prioritization. 
 During the 10 th plan period, limited destinations in the States / UTs were identified on yearly basis for integrated
 intensive development. While developing the destinations, the strategy followed, was to ensure that the
 developments take place in a regional planning framework that is not restricted to the immediate environs of the site

 but extends to the ‘region of influence’ of the attraction or cluster of attractions including the primary staging area
 and travel nodes.  It was ensured that all development work was based on professionally prepared master plans,
 ideally using the best expertise and contained components that are conceived, to satisfy the preferences and
 requirement needs of a clearly identified target market.  Efforts were made to see that the master planning approach
 included all stakeholders in the planning process – all levels of government and administration, various government
 agencies and Ministries, the local community, elected representatives, and members of the tourism industry or
 related industries. Destinations were carefully selected in consultation with the State Governments, based on the

 Tourism to take remedial action to ensure the optimum utilization of allocated funds.        The Committee also recommends
 the Ministry to develop a system of skill assessment and certification provider without any formal training or
 education.                                                                                                      (Para 38)
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
            The Committee notes that the hospitality and service sector has been accorded priority with the growth and
 diversification of tourism activities. The Committee further notes that there are five institutes of repute being run in the
 private sector apart from there are 125 institutes of hotel management in the country offering hospitality programmes in
 private sector.  The Committee observes that as a sizeable number of private IHMs have emerged in the country to offer
 courses in hotel management programme there is a need to provide a institutional and integrated course in development of
 the country’s human resources programme. The Committee is pleased to note that although the guidelines for affiliation of
 these private institutes have been put-in place spelling out the eligibility requirements for affiliation though these institutes
 are lacking in training and other infrastructural facilities. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to grant a
 statutory/deemed university status to NCHMCT for achieving excellence in the tourism sector and to standardized the
 quality of education and training through affiliation and academic supervision through an Act of
 Parliament.                                                                        (Para 44)
            The Committee is constrained to note that there is huge demand-supply mismatch of manpower servicing the tourism
 industry resulting in poor quality of service offered to the tourists. The Committee feels that there is a need to develop the
 required human resources in various segments of the tourism industry consequent upon the rapid growth in the tourism,
 rapidly changing technology and a more demanding competitive market. The Committee recommends the Ministry to
 address the issues related to human resources development in the tourism sector with particular emphasis on qualified
 tourists guides, involving the quality of human resources, their condition of works, training and opportunities, the role of
 private sector for efficient administration and successful operation of the quality of manpower.                                          
                                       (Para 48)
PROMOTION OF DOMESTIC TOURISM
            The Committee notes that the request of the Ministry of Tourism for budgetary allocation of Rs.188.75 crore has not
 been accepted by Government and a provision of Rs.165 crore has been made for the year 2007-08 which is similar to that
 of last year’s allocation. The Committee feels that it will dampen the spirit of the Ministry and also put them in difficulty to

18
file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/119threport.htm[22-10-2018 12:24:10]
 continue their efforts sincerely. The Committee expects that the cut in budgetary allocation will be restored at the RE stage.
 The Committee notes that the infrastructure development and destination management is the backbone for sustained growth
 of tourism in the country as it provides critical connectivity between the tourism product and target source market for both
 domestic and international tourists. The Committee finds that the creation of tourism infrastructure has multiplier effect in
 terms of overall economic growth, employment generation, preservation of art, culture and heritage. The Committee,
 therefore, urges upon the Ministry to have proper planning for development of tourism infrastructure in economically
 backward States but having abundant tourism potential by creation of assets viz. roads, telecommunication, medical
 facilities, sanitation, removal of garbage from these tourists sites etc. Integrated approach with all backward and forward
 linkages along with mass awareness campaigns in domestic market should be adopted in these destinations for getting larger
 tourism volumes and revenues, thereby contributing significantly to the national economy.                                       (Para 54)
OVERSEAS PROMOTION
            The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism through its overseas offices, attempts to promote India as a
 preferred tourist destination and to increase the number of foreign tourists arrivals in the country. The Committee observes
 that there is strong competition in the tourist generating markets for attracting foreign tourists to their countries. The
 Committee recommends the Ministry to review the functioning of the overseas marketing offices and, if need be relocate
 some of them in view of the emerging tourism requirements of the prospective tourists besides revamping the India tourism
 website to make it more user friendly. The Committee appreciates the work done by the Ministry in the form of Incredible
 India campaign and recommends the Ministry to reinforce the campaign in the global tourist market with more vigor and
 zeal.  The Committee also recommends that Incredible India campaigning should also be done in various regional languages
 to boost domestic tourism.                                 (Para 57)
            The Committee is constrained to note that our country lags behind several other less endowed countries in terms of
 attracting tourists although the  foreign tourists and foreign exchange earnings through tourism (in US Dollars), have
 registered a growth of 53.1% and 69.8% respectively. The Committee also notes that the major constraints for growth in
 foreign tourists arrivals in the country are inadequate budgetary support for promotion and marketing, non-availability of
 accommodation at the major ports of entry and other major tourist centres in the country during season, fear about health
 and hygiene conditions, perceptions relating to safety and security and expensive packages as compared to many South East
 Asian countries. The Committee recommends the Ministry to lay emphasis on safety, security and hygiene aspects along
 with other promotional activities through all major print and visual media at overseas markets and ask for adequate
 budgetary support from the Ministry of Finance and inform the Committee of the outcome
 therefrom.                                                            (Para 60)
NATIONAL TOURISM PROMOTION BOARD
            The Committee notes that tourism is not single but involves multi-sectoral activities requiring close coordination
 with various agencies viz., the Ministries of Civil Aviation, Culture, Textiles, Environment and Forests, Railway, Home,
 Finance, Shipping & Road Transport and Highways and External Affairs etc.  The Government has brought the subject of
 tourism under the scope of the Committee on Infrastructure (COI) for initiating policy on creation of world class
 infrastructure in a time bound manner. The Committee is of the opinion that inspite of the efforts, the tourism is still in the
 appalling state of coordination. The Committee is not satisfied with the replies of the Ministry on the issue of the setting up
 of a National Tourism Promotion Board for better coordination with all agencies/ stakeholders and expand its scope towards
 inter-sectoral convergence of resources and policy integration and desires that the whole issue be re-examined and
 Committee be informed of the outcome thereof with reasons for conclusions.
     (Para 63)
SHORTAGE OF HOTEL ACCOMMODATION
            The Committee observes that the Ministry of Tourism has assessed the requirement of hotel rooms in Delhi and NCR
 in the wake of the Commonwealth Games 2010 and taken a series of steps and incentives to augment the
 accommodation/infrastructure in this region. The Ministry of Finance has also declared a Tax Holiday for 5 years for setting
 up new hotels in Delhi and NCR region w.e.f. 1
st April 2007. The Committee also notes that the Ministry of Tourism has
 taken up the matter of creation of infrastructure with the State Governments and other land owning agencies like Ministries
 of Civil Aviation, Railway and DDA for creation of land banks, allocation of hotel sites on revenue sharing basis and
 granting extra FSI/FAR for hotels, permitting extra commercial usage in the hotels and a capital subsidy scheme as an
 incentive for accommodation infrastructure upto 3 star hotels, which have now yielding results. The Committee 
 recommends the Ministry to impress upon all the land owning agencies and the State Government for allotting land on
 annual rental basis for promotion of hotels in the country and Ministry of Finance be pursued for extending Tax Holiday
 scheme for construction of budget hotels under 3 star category all over the country so as to promote the tourism in a big
 way.

18
file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/119threport.htm[22-10-2018 12:24:10]
                                                    (Para 68)
RATIONALIZATIONS OF TAXES ON THE TOURISM INDUSTRY
            The Committee notes with concern that there exists multiplicity of taxes and the quantum of each levied by different
 States and Union Territories does affect the growth of tourist traffic to the country by making tourist packages more
 expensive as compared to other neighbouring countries. The Committee is also constrained to note that the luxury tax on
 hotels and VAT on food and beverages and on Airline Turbine Fuel (ATF) and high rate of taxation on tourist transport
 vehicles have deterring impact on the growth of tourism. The Committee notes that the issues related to very high and
 variable rate of luxury tax and taxation on transport sector have been referred to Empowered Committee of State Finance
 Ministers for looking into the implementation of VAT all over the country and Ministry of Tourism has mooted a proposal
 regarding introduction of Zonal Permits for a minimum of 3 States in order to rationalize the tax on tourist transport and to
 facilitate smooth movement of inter-state travel. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to pursue the matter
 of rationalization of taxes on the tourism industry more vigorously with the Ministry of Finance for suitable
 recommendation so that the taxes are rationalized appropriately to promote the tourism sector in the country in a big
 way.                               (Para 71)
INTRODUCTION OF VISA ON ARRIVAL SCHEME
            The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism has mooted a proposal regarding introduction of visa on arrival
 and electronic visa scheme for selected countries but due to the prevailing global security scenario and present security
 concerns in the country, the same was not agreed to by the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Committee agrees to the fact that
 security reasons are the prime concern and cannot be compromised but at the same time it also feels that granting visa-on-
arrival to the foreign tourists at airports will certainly boost the global tourist arrivals in the country. The Committee is of the
 opinion that the scheme should first be introduced with certain friendly countries on experimental basis and then it can be
 extended to other countries as well. The Committee recommends the Ministry of Tourism to further pursue the matter with
 the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Civil Aviation for desired results.
                                      (Para 76)
SPECIAL TOURISM POLICE
            The Committee notes with concerns that incidents of cheating, fleecing criminal acts and harassment of foreign
 tourists bring a bad name to country and have an adverse impact on the foreign tourists arrival. The Committee feels that
 the issue related with safety and security is vital in creating goodwill and the Union Ministry of Tourism cannot wash its
 hand off stating that policing is a State subject. The Committee is of the view that the role of media, travel agents and tour
 operators is paramount in establishing goodwill even in the critical situation. The Committee welcomes the steps taken by
 Government of Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Rajasthan,
 Uttar Pradesh and Delhi for deployment of Tourism Police for ensuring safety and security of the tourists. The Committee
 recommends the Ministry to take initiatives in other States as well for deployment of special Tourist Police so as to address
 the safety and security related issues properly.
                                    (Para 81)
DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM IN ANDAMAN & NICOBAR AND LAKSHADWEEP ISLANDS
            The Committee notes that as per its recommendations the Ministry of Environment and Forests has reduced the No
 Development Zone to 50 mtrs. instead  of 200 mtrs. in Andaman and Nicobar islands.  The proposals for relaxation in No
 Development Zone for Lakshadweep islands upto 5mtrs. is under finalisation. The Committee feels that this move will
 definitely facilitate the development of world class tourism infrastructure in the islands and coastal areas besides attracting
 high value and low volumes tourists traffic in these islands.
                                                                                              (Para 90)
            The Committee notes that the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep islands have the potential of growing
 as unique tourist destinations for Eco-Tourism and Island Tourism but due to variety of limitations particularly the
 inadequate connectivity, the tourism in these islands has not grown as required both in the scale and quality.  At Andaman
 the tourists have to largely depend on the infrastructure at Port Blair whereas the facility created at the other islands remains
 unutilized for want of poor inter-islands connectivity. The Committee is constrained to note that inspite of the limited
 resources, the Administration of these islands have not sent any proposals to the Ministry of Tourism for release of the
 central financial assistance for development of the infrastructure as well the connectivity. It clearly shows the lackadaisical
 attitude of the Administrations of these islands. The Committee, therefore, urges the Administrations of these islands to
 prepare concrete proposals complete in all respect for release of central financial assistance under different schemes of the
 Ministry of Tourism for promotion and development of infrastructure as well as connectivity. In this way they could

18
file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/119threport.htm[22-10-2018 12:24:10]
 encourage the growth of hotel accommodation and mitigate connectivity problems between different islands. The
 Committee recommends the Department of Tourism  to take up the matter with Administration of these islands for sending
 the proposals so as to create conducive environment of investment to seek larger flow of funds from private sector
 participation in developing the necessary infrastructure and accommodation and then privately manage it through a
 transparent process.                             (Para 92)
The Committee notes that in order to revive the domestic tourists traffic, the Ministry of Tourism has requested the
 DoPT for extension of LTC facility by air for the central government employees for a further period of 2 years beyond
 24.11.2005. The Committee recommends the Ministry to pursue the matter for extension of LTC facility in the Andaman
 and Nicobar Islands for the central government employees with the DoPT and Ministry of Tourism should introduce
 attractive LTC packages for these employees visiting Andaman and Nicobar Islands.                              
                                                                                 (Para 93)

2.         The Ministry of Culture has six Subordinate Offices, two attached Offices and thirty three Autonomous Bodies and
 two Missions under its purview.  The major areas of activities of the Ministry are Archaeology, Museums, Anthropology
 and Ethnology, Libraries, Archives and Archival Libraries, Dissemination of Art and Culture, Memorials, Centenaries and
 Anniversaries, Buddhist and Tibetan Institutions and International Cultural Relation. The programmes undertaken by the
 Ministry can broadly be classified as, activities of North East Region, Archaeology, Museums, Anthropology and
 Ethnology, Archives and Archival Libraries, Tibetan/Buddhist Studies, Libraries, Akademies and National School of
 Drama, Promotion and Dissemination of Culture, Memorials, Centenaries and Anniversaries, Cultural Relations and
 Festival of India, IGNCA and Secretariat.

5.         The Committee notes that while comparing B.E. 2006-07 and B.E. 2007-08, it is observed that most of the major
 schemes under the Ministry of Culture have got  increased allocations.  The Committee feels that preservation and
 protection of vast cultural resources of the country is a task gigantic in nature and requires huge investments.  But, the
 Committee is at dismay that the Government has always treated it as non productive sector thereby inviting apathy of the
 Finance Ministry which is always reducing the allocations made for the Ministry of Culture at Revised Estimates stage.  
 The Committee strongly feels that this sector is catalytic for economic growth and not only that but also preservation of our
 culture means preserving our national identity which should not be compromised at any cost.  The Committee, therefore,
 recommends that the allocations made for the year 2007-08 should not be reduced at RE stage by the Finance Ministry and
 the Ministry of Culture should try to spend the allocations to the fullest extent. 
 
6.         Transition from the 10
th Five – year Plan to the 11th Five Year Plan is an occasion for deep retrospection.  It is also
 an opportunity to learn valuable lessons from past successes and failures.  The new strategies for the 11 th Plan should be
 built on the already demonstrated strengths and successes during the past decades of planned development, while avoiding
 the pitfalls. Before embarking upon the new Plan it is necessary to compare the past performance as well as the future Plans
 undertaken by the Ministry. In this context the Ministry informed the Committee that “the Culture Sector has been classified
 as non-developmental sector.  It is not surprising that this sector has got neither the profile nor the priority it deserves in the
 Nation’s overall agenda for development.  It may be relevant to mention here that Art and Culture got a share of only 0.02%
 of the total 10
th Plan Allocations.”
 
7.         During the Tenth Plan Period, major institutions under the Ministry like the Sangeet Natak Akademi, Sahitya
 Akademi and Lalit Kala Akademi completed 50 years of their existence and organised Golden Jubilee Celebrations.  It was
 an occasion of not only to celebrate the achievements of decades but also to re-orient their activities by re-focussing their
 objectives.
 
8.         An allocation of Rs.1720.00 crore was approved by the Planning Commission for the Central Sector – Art and
 Culture for the Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07).  Of this, an amount of Rs.1168.43 crore constituting about 68% was
 utilized by the Ministry of Culture during the year 2002-06.  An Annual Plan outlay of Rs.470 crore was allocated by the
 Planning Commission for the various activities of the Ministry of Culture during 2006-07.  It is pertinent to mention that
 many of the Plan activities in respect of the Ministry and its organisations were to be deferred during the Tenth Five Year
 Plan period as there was reduction of Annual Plan outlay of each year at the stage of Revised Estimates.
 
9.         Consequent upon the identification of the major thrust areas for the Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-12) keeping in
 view the vision for Eleventh Plan by the Ministry, the following new schemes are proposed to be implemented from 2007-
08 for which token budgetary provisions have been made.  The details of the schemes are being worked out by the Ministry,
 namely:-
 
(i)         Scheme for the Safeguarding and Other Protective Measures in the area of Intangible Heritage and Cultural
 Diversity (arising out of UNESCO Convention);
(ii)        Awareness creation in the area of Intellectual Property Right(IPR) and Setting up of a National IPR Cell for
 Creative Artists and Artisans;
(iii)       Plan Scheme for promotion and Dissemination of Awareness about Indian Cultural and Heritage.\

Pending finalisation of the schemes and approval from Planning Commission of the above schemes, token provision has
 been provided for the schemes under B.E. 2007-08.
10.       Our culture is the most vibrant and rich culture in the world.  The Committee feels that culture has to be harnessed
 together with tourism and showcased to the world.  The right modal mix between culture and tourism would yield valuable
 foreign exchange by inviting more and more tourists; promote our artists and artisans many of whom are at the verge of
 starvation; preserve our local/ regional culture, art and craft ; last but not the least, it will also enthuse private sector to
 invest more and more in these activities.  The Committee strongly recommends that the approach of the Ministry of Culture,
 Ministry of Finance and Planning Commission should change during the 11
th Five Year Plan and all of them should
 together take adequate care and ensure that none of the Plan activities in respect of Ministry of Culture and its organizations
 is deferred due to reduction in Annual Plan outlay at the stage of Revised Estimates. 
 
11.       The year 2007-08 being the first year of the Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007-12), the Planning Commission has
 allocated a sum of Rs.557.00 crore for various developmental activities of the Ministry of Culture.  Even though, this
 Ministry had proposed an outlay of Rs.905.41 crore for the first year of the Eleventh Plan, on the basis of the
 recommendations of the Working Group constituted by the Planning Commission and also receipt of proposals for the
 Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007-12) including Annual Plan 2007-08, from various cultural organizations/divisions under the
 Ministry of Culture, the allocation for the Annual Plan 2007-08 has been pegged only at Rs.557.00 crore.  As regard Non-
Plan funds, a sum of Rs.375.61 crore has been provided during the year 2007-08.  The Plan provision for the Annual Plan
 2007-08 includes Rs.50.00 crore for the building Projects of the attached and subordinate Bodies of the Ministry of Culture.
 
12.       The Ministry has been allocated only a sum of Rs.400.00 crore under Plan at R.E. 2006-07 level, thereby effecting a
 reduction of Rs.70.00 crore from the original allocation.  On the basis of the recommendations of the Standing Committee
 for reviewing of budgetary allocation in the month of December instead of the month of September, the matter was taken up
 with the Ministry of Finance for their views/comments.  In this regard, they have shown their inability to alter the reviewing
 system of budgetary allocation, since preparation of budget documents for presentation of annual budget on 28
th February
 starts from December and it is, therefore, necessary to complete their R.E. exercise before this which is done during
 October-November every year. The  Planning Commission is of the opinion that inadequacy of resources under Non Plan
 Activities does not justify conversion of such activities to the Plan side.  It has been therefore, desired that the requirement
 of funds for the regular upkeep and maintenance activities and for protection and conservation activities may realistically be
 assessed and sought from the Ministry of Finance.
 
13.       The Committee strongly recommends its earlier observations with regard to budgeting pattern of the Ministry of
 Culture and reiterates its recommendations made at para 11 of the 103
rd Report on the Demands for Grants for the year
 2006-07 wherein it was stated that :-
 
"The Committee is of the view that fixing of the Revised Estimates ceiling by the Ministry of Finance on the basis of
 the level of expenditure attained upto the month of September/October creates problem for the Department of
 Culture.   The Committee observes that most of the cultural functions and festivals take place in the month of
 October and November, after the monsoon.  The Archaeological Survey of India also incurs major expenditure after
 the monsoon.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that Government must review the budgeting procedure and
 evolve some mechanism to ensure that the Plan allocation for the Department of Culture is not reduced.  The
 Committee recommends that if the review of the budgetary allocation is done in the month of December, instead of
 the month of September then the cut in the budgetary provision could be avoided.  "

14.       The Committee took note of the fact that a large number of vacancies are existing in various cadres in different apex
 institutions/bodies functioning under the Ministry of Culture.  When the Secretary was requested to explain the position
 thereon he stated that in the ASI there were sixteen vacancies of Deputy Superintendent Archaeologist Surveyors, out of
 which they have advertised for eight posts and these are going to be filled.  The Secretary also informed the Committee that
 ASI does not have single museologist on its roll to look after 41 site museums working under it.  It also does not have single
 conservation architect and even conservation engineers are also not there in its panel resulting major problem in various
 activities.  Now, the Ministry is deciding to outsource these posts.  Particularly, when the Committee asked about the reason
 for not appointing a museologist, the Secretary, informed that there is a ban on creation of posts as well as filling up of
 posts.  The Secretary admitted before the Committee that out of thirty-three there are six organization which do not have an
 executive head at present.  The Committee had earlier recommended for appointment of Director-General, National
 Archives immediately and till now the said post is lying vacant.  The Director-Generals post is actually under the purview
 of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC).  The UPSC advertised for this post and subsequently interviews were
 held on 21.2.2006, but none was suitable for the post.  The Ministry again requested UPSC to re-advertise this post. 
 Subsequently the post was re-advertised by the UPSC on 27.7.2006 but, till now no interview has been held.   Similarly, in
 the Anthropological Survey of India a person was selected and the proposal was sent to the ACC for appointment, but when
 the ACC was deliberating on   the process of approving the appointment of the selected person, the UPSC withdrew the
 recommendation that it had made for the candidate because of the reason that the qualification of the selected person was
 not adequate.   In the case of Indian Museum, Kolkata, the Ministry has completed the process of selection and it has gone
 to the ACC for approval and the appointment will take place very soon.  As far as the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute
 of Asian Studies, Kolkata is concerned the post for the head of the executive was re-advertised twice.  The last time UPSC
 had recommended two candidates. Out of these two, when Ministry started selecting one, it was found that certain
 guidelines laid down by the Department of Personnel and Training for the Constitution of the Search Committee had not
 been followed. So the Search Committee had to be reconstituted to confirm to the guidelines given by the DoPT and now a
 person has been selected and will be appointed very soon.  In the Rampur Raza Library, the post of Director is lying
 vacant.  An interview was held on 30
th June 2006 by the Selection Committee but no suitable candidate was found. 
 
15.       Regarding the reason for non-filling up various key posts the 
 Secretary, Ministry of Culture expressed concern and helplessness and submitted before the Committee that UPSC
 generally takes about nine months to one year for filling up these posts.  Secondly, the Government have imposed a ban on
 recruitment;  there is a circular to this effect saying that only one percent of the total strength could be filled, and that too,
 through a Screening Committee, from year to year basis, and accordingly meeting will be held for filling up the direct
 recruitment posts.  The Screening Committee, however, has not met even for the year 2001-02 and 2002-03.   Meetings of
 the Screening Committee for both these years have been held recently and the Ministry of Culture has allowed some of the
 institutions to fill-up the vacancies arising in the year 2001-02 and 2002-03. The Meeting of the Screening Committee for
 the year 2003-04 has not yet been held.  The instructions of the Government are that apart from the posts which are there
 and which are not recommended by the Screening Committee, the rest of the posts have to be abolished.  So every year, the
 Ministry is actually abolishing the posts.  The Secretary informed the Committee that during Special Investigation Unit
 inspection at the National Library, Kolkata, it was recommended for abolition of certain posts, to which the National
 Library has not agreed, and these posts have not been abolished so far, thereby creating major problem. 
 
16.       The Committee notes the sorry state of affairs prevailing in various premier institutions of art, culture and literature
 and several of them are functioning headless.  The Committee takes strong exception to the fact that Screening Committee
 is not meeting regularly.  The Committee is also surprised to notice the lethargic approach of UPSC towards filling up these
 vacant posts which should have been done rather without any loss of time.   The Committee therefore, recommends that the
 Ministry should propose an amendment to the rules and a composite method of recruitment should be followed instead of
 direct recruitment method.  The Committee strongly feels that these key posts should be taken out of the purview of the
 UPSC and appointment should be made out of a panel of persons of the institutions having requisite experience and such
 other persons having eminence in various concerned fields.  As regards the posts of Deputy Superintendent Archaeologist
 Surveyors in the ASI is concerned the Committee expresses its displeasure in advertising the posts in peacemeal instead of
 in one go and recommends that all the vacant posts should be filled up without further loss of time. The Committee finds
 that despite the earlier recommendations of the Committee to appoint a person who is an expert in archaeology or eminent
 historian as the Director-General of ASI the Ministry of Culture continues to appoint civil servant from IAS as the Director-
General of ASI which is resulting in the neglect of this premier institution. The Committee reiterates its earlier
 recommendations to appoint eminent archaeologist or historian as the Director General of ASI.

17.       The Archaeological Survey of India, the biggest attached office under the Ministry of Culture has been provided with
 a major step up in the plan as well as non-plan outlay for the year 2007-08 for sustaining its various activities.  ASI has
 envisaged certain new schemes to address the issue of preservation and conservation of monuments.  It proposes to take up
 the conservation of at least 800 monuments/sites.  Besides, ASI proposes to implement a new scheme to provide visitor’s
 amenities at all World Heritage Monuments and those monuments visited by large number of tourists.  Another major
 initiative is to assist state protected monuments and unprotected monuments through the State Governments.  Modernising
 archaeological exploration by state of the art technologies is another area of priority of the ASI in the Eleventh Plan.  On
 account of these major and much needed initiatives, the Annual Plan Allocation of ASI has been kept at Rs.98.00 crore
 which includes Rs.8.00 crore for externally aided project/scheme of conservation and development of Ajanta- Ellora
 Complex through Japan Bank of International Corporation.  In case of Non-Plan provision for 2007-08 crore has been made
 to provide adequate funds to meet the committed liability such as salaries, D.A. etc. of all organisations under Ministry of

(a)        Conservation and Preservation of Monuments
 
18.       Conservation, preservation and maintenance of the centrally protected monuments and sites are the prime
 responsibilities of ASI.  The total number of individual structures being maintained by the ASI is over five thousand. 
 During the year 2006-07, 700 schemes under plan and 500 schemes under non-plan for conservation, preservation,
 environmental development and providing tourist amenities at monuments were taken up.
 
19.       During 2006-07, more than eight hundred monuments were taken up for conservation and structural repairs,
 chemical preservation and environmental development besides day-to-day maintenance of three thousand six hundred sixty
 seven monuments. ASI has been extending services and expertise to State Governments and other agencies by undertaking
 Civil Deposit Works of ancient structures other than the protected ones.            Public-private partnership is encouraged and
 some important corporate houses have contributed funds to the National Culture Fund for the developmental activities of
 Protected Monuments.  MOUs have been signed with Indian Oil Corporation, Steel Authority of India, World Monuments
 Fund, Indian Hotels Company Ltd.   The agreement for phase-II of Ajanta Ellora Conservation and Tourism Development
 Project with loan from JBIC, is finalised and ASI’s component being 901 Million Yen (Rs.36.87 crores) Conservation of
 monuments is multidisciplinary in nature.  ASI has entrusted scientific studies and investigations of some of the monuments
 to the specialized agencies in the country.
 
(b)        Excavations & Explorations

 the following programmes of ASI.

                  Jufardih, District Nalanda, Bihar and Bangarh, District South Dinajpur West Bengal (both Excavations to be
 executed by Patna Excavation Branch).
 
2.
                  Barabati Fort District Cuttack, Orissa (excavation) by Bhubaneswar, excavation branch.
 
3.
                  Daultabad Fort, district Aurangabad Fort, Maharashtra (excavation) by Aurangabad Circle.

(d)        Encroachment of Monuments
 
29.       The Committee inquired from the Ministry about the number of monuments which have been encroached upon in an
 unauthorized manner and remedial action taken by the Ministry to remove these encroachments.  The Secretary replied to
 the Committee that there were 249 monuments where there were encroachments, out of which the Ministry have cleared 70
 in the last five years.  Now, so far as encroachments are concerned, under the Act itself, the Superintending Archaeologist
 has the power to ask somebody to remove the encroachment.  But if the person who has been asked does not remove the
 encroachment, then, under  the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971 powers have been given to
 the Superintending Archaeologist to actually evict encroachers.  But the actual eviction has to be done only with the
 assistance of the State Government and District Collector.  So, unless the Collector does not provide for the Police and other
 things, it is not possible to remove these encroachments.

 agencies. There are 294 CISF attendants guarding the Red Fort and about 165 guarding the Taj Mahal.   The Secretary
 submitted before the Committee that "There is an urgent need for creation of manpower at the Archaeological Survey of
 India to guard these monuments."

(e)        Other issues
 
32.       Air Pollution Monitoring Laboratory at Agra is continuously monitoring the ambient air quality in and around Taj
 Mahal to study possible impact of air pollutants on the monument and to formulate conservation measures accordingly.  In
 addition, weather parameters such as wind velocity and direction, temperature, relative humidity and rainfall are being
 recorded continuously as these parameters have a bearing on the behaviour and distribution of pollutants in the
 environment.  It has been found by this laboratory that the level of air pollutants i.e., sulphur-di-oxide and Nitrus Oxide
 gases are generally within the permissible limits whereas the suspended particulate matter is always at a very high level
 except during the rainy season.  The deposition of Suspended Particulate Matter (SPM) on the shimmering white marble of
 the Taj Mahal imparts yellow tinge to the marble surface.  To restore the pristine glory of the Taj Mahal, as a conservation
 measure, the clay pack treatment which is non-corrosive and non-abrasive is carried out for the removal of the acretionary
 deposits.

 11.9.2005 and is under the jurisdiction of Delhi Circle of the Archaeological Survey of India.  The Northern Railway has
 made a proposal for realigning the railway tracks passing through Salimgarh Fort in view of their proposed project for a
 new Yamuna Bridge (in lieu of the existing bridge) on Delhi-Shahdra section on Northern Railway. The realignment of the
 railway track passing through Salimgarh Fort would involve making two deep cuts on the ancient Salimgarh Fort wall.  As
 this would constitute a violation of the provisions of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act,
 1958 and rules made thereunder, the ASI has regretted that it has issued NOC for realigning the railway line passing
 through Salimgarh Fort.  The Salimgarh Fort along with the Red Fort has been proposed for inclusion in the list of World
 Heritage Sites in 2007.  ASI has appointed a Consultant for preparing a Comprehensive Conservation Management Plan for
 Red Fort (including Salimgarh Fort).  The Consultant has finalized the draft report which is under discussion.  Conservation
 works would be initiated after the plan is finalised.

 other persons having eminence in various concerned fields.  As regards the posts of Deputy Superintendent Archaeologist
 Surveyors in the ASI is concerned the Committee expresses its displeasure in advertising the posts in piecemeal instead of
 in one go and recommends that all the vacant posts should be filled up without further loss of time. The Committee finds
 that despite the earlier recommendations of the Committee to appoint a person who is an expert in archaeology or eminent
 historian as the Director-General of ASI the Ministry of Culture continues to appoint civil servant from IAS as the Director-
General of ASI which is resulting in the neglect of this premier institution. The Committee reiterates its earlier
 recommendations to appoint eminent archaeologist or historian as the Director General of ASI.
(Para 16)
 
Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)
 
(a)   Conservation and Preservation of Monuments:
(b)   Excavations & Explorations
 
            The Committee recommends that conservation preservation work undertaken by ASI including phase II of Ajanta
 Ellora project should be completed within a definite time frame and in a targeted manner.  The details and outcome of these
 may be provided to the Committee separately. As regards exploration and excavations, the Committee feels that selection of
 new sites is a welcome step but this should also be done in a systematic and time bound manner.  Moreover, findings of
 excavations should also be recorded simultaneously so that the report is finalized by the end of the excavation work itself. 
 The Committee strongly recommends that the pending reports on excavations undertaken by ASI should be finalized and
 published without any loss of time.
            The Committee notes that conservation of our heritage is important, both for encouraging tourism as well as for
 attracting visitors from overseas.  The importance of cultural tourism in the context of development of both culture and
 tourism cannot be overemphasized.  Archaeological Survey of India, which is a flagship organization of the Ministry of
 Culture is engaged in conservation, preservation and maintenance of monuments.  Unless and until substantive allocation of
 funds is made to ASI towards undertaking the massive task of maintenance and conservation of heritage, ancient
 monuments and historical sites, the heritage preservation in a sustained manner and promotion of ancient cultural heritage
 could not be achieved.  Unfortunately, this aspect of heritage preservation/promotion has received very little attention it
 deserves.  This is due to meagre Plan budget of the Ministry which acts as a constraint to step up its activities.  Therefore,
 the Committee recommends that more funds allocation should be made to ASI and number of monuments under its
 protection should also be increased taking into account the total number of unprotected monuments in the country which are
 languishing and dithering due to neglect.
(Paras 22 & 23)
(c)  National Mission on Monuments:
            The Committee recommends that the National Mission of Monuments and   Antiquities is an important Mission and
 has a laudable goal to achieve but however, the modalities for the Mission should be clearly planned and targets should be
 fixed for achieving the stated objective so that the allocation made for this purpose is not wasted.    The Committee also
 recommends that in addition to the four States chosen initially for the purpose activities of the Mission should also be
 extended to other States which are economically backward but culturally very rich. 
(Para 28)
(d) Encroachment of Monuments

            The Committee expresses its anxiety over the incidents of encroachments upon the land of Centrally Protected
 Monuments.  The Committee is more concerned about the failure of Archeological Survey of India to get back the land
 from the encroachers.  Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that a complete assessment should be made
 regarding encroachment of monuments/sites under the protection of Archaeological Survey of India all over the country. 
 Prompt action ought to be taken against the encroachers with the help of State Governments/Local Administrations and the
 matter should be pursued at the highest level i.e. Chief Minister.    The Committee also recommends that number of
 monuments attendants should be suitably increased by recruiting more personnel on urgent basis to check the incidents of
 encroachments as well as thefts. 
(Para 31)
 
 
(e)  Other issues
 
            The Committee expresses its concern that Taj Mahal, the world famous monument at Agra is becoming yellowish
 due to deposition of Suspended Particulate Matter (SPM).  The Committee recommends that while undertaking any
 conservation activity at Taj Mahal abundant cautions should be taken to retain the original glory of the shimmering white
 marble used in this.  
 
            The Committee takes exception to the fact that ASI without assessing the consequences issued No Objection
 Certificates (NOC) for realigning the railway line passing through Salimgarh Fort, which the Ministry is proposing to be
 included in the list of World Heritage Sites in the year 2007 in a routine manner.  This shows the apathy and callousness of
 the Organization which now regrets for issuing NOC and admits that realignment would involve making two deep cuts on
 the ancient Salimgarh Fort Wall.    The Committee strongly recommends that the NOC issued by ASI should be revoked
 forthwith and this kind of incidents should not be repeated in future.   
(Paras 34 & 35)
 
Observing Centenaries and Anniversaries of Important national personalities and events
 
            The Committee observes that in comparison to the total plan and non-plan outlay i.e. Rs.932.61 crore of the whole
 Ministry, the allocation made for the purpose of observing centenaries and anniversaries of the important national
 personalities and events is quite substantial amount i.e., 65.92 crore.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that it should
 be spent carefully and such events and occasions should also be used optimally for the promotion of tourism.
(Para 37)
 
National Archives of India
 
            The Committee recommends that the allocation for National Archives which has been almost doubled in the BE
 2007-08 in comparison to the RE 2006-07 should be utilized for the purpose of acquiring more and more documents from
 the States.  The Committee also recommends that activities like, reference, digitization of rare and precious archival
 records, conservation of archival records of national importance and translation thereof should be done in committed
 manner. 
(Para 40)
Sahitya Akademi
 
            The Committee desires that the allocation to the tune of Rs.1.25 crore made for the activities of the Sahitya Akademi
 will be spent by the Akademi meaningfully. 
(Para 43)
Sangeet Natak Akademi
 
            The Committee notes with unhappiness that out of Rs. 9.00 crore allocated in RE 2006-07, the Akademi could spend
 only Rs.6.41 crore.  The Committee recommends that the increased allocation made this year for the Sangeet Natak
 Akademi in the BE 2007-08 should be used meaningfully for promotion of performing arts.  The Committee also
 recommends that the work relating to Museum of performing arts should be initiated at the earliest.
(Para 46)
 
National School of Drama

The Committee is happy to note that National School of Drama has got Rs.11.00 crore for undertaking various
 activities but simultaneously cautions that the amount should not remain under spent as it is made clear by the Ministry that
 out of theRs.11.00 crore available to the School at RE 2006-07, it could spend only 7.42 crore by 28th February, 2007. 
(Para 49)
Lalit Kala Akademi
 
            The Committee is distressed to point out that this premier institute which is engaged in promotion of visual and
 plastic arts in India like painting, graphic, sculpture and ceramic, etc. is not being able to spend even the meager allocation
 made to it during 2006-07 which is quite clear from the fact that it has spent even less than fifty per cent of its allocation. 
 The Committee recommends that functioning of the Akademi should be strengthened and non-utilisation of the allocated
 funds should be viewed seriously by the Ministry for which corrective measures should be initiated in a time bound manner.
 The Committee should be informed of the measures taken in this regard at the earliest.
(Para 51)
Raja Rammohun Roy Library Foundation 
 
The Committee recommends that in accordance with the recommendation made by the Knowledge Commission at
 least one library should be opened at the level of District Headquarter and since Raja Rammohun Roy Library Foundation is
 the nodal organization for undertaking such task adequate budgetary provision should be made for the purpose. 
(Para 54)
Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts
 
            The Committee takes strong note of the fact that planned allocation made for Indira Gandhi National Centre for the
 Arts at the stage of B.E. 2006-07 was just Rs.50 lakh whereas at the RE stage it was increased to Rs.3.00 crore and out of
 this amount the Centre could spend only Rs.30 lakh.  The Committee does not find any satisfactory explanation for non-
utilization of the allocated funds and the reasons for the vast increase at the RE stage during the year 2006-07.  The
 Committee also notes that there is a major increase in the allocation for the IGNCA again in the BE 2007-08.  The
 Committee hopes that this year the increased allocation will be utilized by the Centre optimally. The Committee also notes
 that there is some adverse report of CAG on the functioning of IGNCA and complaint has been lodged in the CBI against
 some IGNCA Trustees.  The Committee therefore, desires that copies of all these reports may be furnished to the
 Committee for its perusal at the earliest and inform about the action taken thereon.    
(Para 56)
Budgetary provision for the North Eastern States
 
            The Committee notes that the major portion of the plan allocation of the Ministry is released through various
 autonomous and subordinate organizations under the Ministry of Culture, most of which are scattered all over the country
 and their location is far away from the North-East.  This becomes an inhibiting factor in the implementation of the
 programmes in the North-East.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that efforts should be made to find suitable local
 partners such as Universities, local academies etc. in the North-Eastern Region itself, which will go a long way in
 improving utilization of the funds earmarked for the North-East.
