            The Committee notes that one of the reasons for underutilization of allocation is unspent balances with the States
 and also non-submission of utilization certificates by most of the States on time.  The Committee observes that most of
 the time the Central Government delay release of funds to the State or releases it at the fag end of the financial year
 and expect the States to utilize it in a very short time.  The Committee criticize  this practice as obviously the States are
 not in a position to spend the entire amount and have unspent balance lying with them.  The Committee, therefore,
 recommends that the release of the funds to the States should be made on time so that they could utilize the amount
 rationally under proper monitoring of expenditure.  The Committee also desires that there should be proper
 coordination with the States Government, so as to obtain utilization certificates and to safeguard that money released is
 spent only on approved infrastructure development projects.
(Para 22)
            The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism is making efforts to develop quality tourism infrastructure at
 major tourist destinations and circuits for developing tourist products and providing better services to both domestic
 and international tourists.  The Committee observes that tourism is one economic sector in the country that has the
 potential to grow at high rate and can ensure consequential development of the infrastructure of the destinations and
 circuits.   The Committee feels that the infrastructure development holds the key to India’s sustain growth in the
 tourism sector,   therefore, tourist sites and destinations needs to be carefully selected on the basis of their potential to
 provide all infrastructural  facilities  requires by the tourists within such destinations and circuits.    The Committee is
 of the opinion that, if, India has to exploit its vast inherent potential  in tourism, then it must provide exclusive quality
 tourism product and destinations comparable with other Asian countries like Singapore, Malaysia, Maldives, Thailand
 and China. As tourism cannot develop independent of other infrastructure, therefore, a lot of information
 dissemination is required in addition to hospitality and the scope and reach of the domestic tourism should also be
 broadened through development of these competitive destinations and circuits.   The Committee, therefore,
 recommends the Ministry to develop quality tourism at identified tourist circuits and destinations with focus on mega
 destinations and circuits that match international standards and satisfy the domestic and international tourists.   The
 aggressive marketing and publicity of these destinations and circuits should also be done to generate a niche market of
 Indian tourism products.   The Committee also urges the Ministry that while selecting a destination or a circuit they
 should attached priority for harmonious growth and development of all the Regions and States. 
(Para 23)
            The Committee also recommends that in order to maximize the impact of investment on tourism infrastructure,
 the Ministry should make efforts for convergence of these mega destinations and circuits and projects with Jawahar
 Lal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) for integrated development of infrastructure services, urban
 renewal, asset management and urban governance. 
(Para 24)
RURAL TOURISM
            The Committee notes that the rural tourism projects promoted under the scheme for Product/Infrastructure
 Development of Destinations/Circuits targets rural artisans, artists and service providers as primary beneficiaries for
 increase of tourist traffic to these rural destinations.  The Committee is of the view that Rural Tourism has great
 potential and prospects in the country as it helps to provide boost to local performing arts and help conserve the local
 culture apart from preventing rural urban migration.   The Committee feels that the Rural Tourism needs to be given
 impetus by allocating funds for the Rural Tourism projects for each State and the villages should be identified for
 priority development involving the local bodies in the management.  The Committee, therefore, recommends the
 Ministry to focus development of rural tourism infrastructure involving local community in order to promote tourism
 in rural area and percolate its socio-economic benefit. 
(Para 30)
SHORTAGE OF ACCOMMODATION
            The Committee notes that to meet the shortage of about 40,000 rooms during  the Commonwealth Games 2010 in
 Delhi and NCR, the Ministry has mooted a proposal to Central and States Governments for augmenting the
 accommodation infrastructure for growth and quality of the tourist facilities and to create   infrastructure  by
 converting selected Government properties into heritage hotels and making use of the vacant land in Government
 premises including surplus land available with the Ministry of Civil Aviation, Railways and D.D.A. for creation of land
 banks and development of hotels sites on revenue sharing basis and granting extra FSI/FAR for hotels.  The Committee

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/136.htm[28-08-2018 13:33:28]
 also notes that a capital and interest subsidy schemes for accommodation infrastructure upto 3 star and heritage basic
 hotels and a tax holiday for five years to budget and upto 4 star category hotels have been introduced as a incentive to
 combat crisis besides finalization of guidelines for the home stay programme under “Incredible India Bed and
 Breakfast Scheme”.  The Committee observes that there is steep escalation of room tariffs in India which is an
 indication of increasing demand for tourist accommodation. The Committee feels that if such a condition prolongs, the
 tourists being priced out and may opt for an alternative destination in another country.  The Committee of the view
 that the migration of the tourist might have long-term implications in terms of potential loss of future stream of tourists
 in favour of competing tourist destinations.  The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to explore the
 possibility of constructing of hotels on surplus land with Airport Authority of India, surplus and Ministry of Railways
 to meet the demand for additional rooms in the wake of the Commonwealth Games 2010.    The Committee also urges
 the Ministry to impress upon the Central and States Governments for implementation of single window clearance
 system for tourism projects in order to encourage the private players to build hotels in the country.  This would not
 only optimize the utilization of infrastructure facilities but also make the future investment viable. 
(Para 37)
            The Committee also recommends the Ministry to take steps for facilitating additional hotel accommodation
 through “Incredible India Bed & Breakfast Scheme” and consider extending of tax concession benefits to budget home
 stay accommodation so as to facilitate availability of rooms at affordable costs for the tourists who desires to stay with
 Indian families and experience Indian culture and cuisine. An integrated publicity campaign in domestic and overseas
 markets should also be carried periodically.
(Para 38)
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
            The Committee notes that India has positioned itself as a major human resources supply nation in the hospitality
 industry.  The Committee is, however, concerned about the continuing shortage of about 191000 trained manpower per
 annum in the tourism sector.  The Committee is of the view that the problem of trained manpower in the country may
 further aggravate, if the Government does not come forward with concrete plan /policy.   The Committee notes that in
 view of the shortage of trained manpower in the tourism sector, the Ministry is setting up of more Institutes of Hotel
 Management in the States and providing financial assistance for the modernization and capacity enhancement of the
 existing ones as also of the Food Craft Institutes.
(Para 51)
            The Committee is of the view that the shortage of trained manpower in the tourism sector can be better
 addressed by augmenting the infrastructure of existing training institutes in the country besides opening more such
 training institutes in the private hands.   The Committee, however, urges the Ministry to provide institutional and
 integrated curricula for creation of trained manpower in the tourism sector and the NCHMCT should be granted
 regulatory status to regulate, co-coordinate, monitor, control and standardize quality of the educational institutions
 affiliated to it.  This may help to achieve excellence in the growing demand of trained manpower in the tourism sector. 
(Para 52)
CRUISE TOURISM
            The Committee is perturbed to note that despite its recommendations in the earlier reports on Demands for
 Grants urging the Government to bring out a comprehensive cruise tourism policy, the Government has not
 formulated the cruise tourism policy till date.  The Committee feels that in the absence of a comprehensive cruise
 tourism policy the Ministry will not be able to popularize the cruise tourism and address all the aspect of facilitating
 creation of infrastructure, encourage investments from the private sector and create a congenial and hospitable
 environment for growth of cruise tourism in the country.  The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to
 pursue vigorously the matter of finalization of cruise tourism policy and development of dedicated cruise terminals at
 important ports with the Department of Shipping without further delay. 
(Para 54)
MEDICAL TOURISM
            The Committee notes that the concept of Medical Tourism is gaining momentum in the country as it offers
 competitive cost and quality.  The Committee also notes that the Government is facilitating promotion of Medical

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/136.htm[28-08-2018 13:33:28]
 Tourism and has introduced a new category of medical visa for foreign tourists visiting India for medical treatment. 
 The Committee feels that if, the country has to become a major medical hub it must prepare a road map incorporating
 all possible challenges and solutions for achieving recognition of the Medical Tourism and a synergy between the
 hospital and tour operators should be ensured promote this sector.   The Committee, therefore, recommends the
 Ministry to prepare a blue print to tap latent potential, quality and standardization of medical services besides
 promoting India as holistic health destinations globally.  An integrated publicity campaign should also be launched in
 the overseas markets.
(Para 58)
ADVENTURE TOURISM
            The Committee notes that the Adventure Tourism is India’s relatively new segment although it offers a perfect
 playing ground for development  of adventure sports like white water river rafting, paragliding, hot air ballooning,
 skiing, mountain biking, scuba diving, hiking-trekking and rock climbing-rappelling etc..   The Committee also notes
 that Ministry of Tourism has formulated a guidelines on safety and quality norms for adventure tourism activities and
 is providing financial assistance to various States/U.T’s for development  of adventure Tourism projects and
 infrastructure facilities required for trekking, rock climbing, mountaineering, aero- sports, winter/ water related
 sports, trekker huts, wildlife viewing facilities, etc..  The Committee recommends the Ministry to attach priority to this
 special interest tourism and promote it with renewed zeal and vigour across the globe.
(Para 61)
RELAXATION OF THE RAP/PAP/ILP REGIME
            The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism is in constant touch with Ministry of Home Affairs to
 relax/abolish the requirement of permit system in the country as the growth of international tourism to a reason is
 based on development of tourism in that destination.   The Committee is of the view that foreign tourists constitute an
 important component of tourists who wish to visit the country specially the North Eastern States and Andaman &
 Nicobar and Lakshadweep  Islands.  The restrictions on foreigners to stay beyond permitted period and visiting only
 selected islands/regions/destination has discouraged the foreign tourists arrival in the country.  The Committee,
 therefore, recommends that in order to optimally exploit the potential of tourism in these islands/regions/destination,
 the restrictions on the foreigners on visiting the islands/regions may be removed and they may be permitted to
 stay/enjoy the beauty of the islands/regions/destination for a longer periods.  The Committee also feels that opening up
 new islands/regions/destination for foreigners also needs to be given priority.  The Committee recommends the
 Ministry of Tourism to vigorously pursue the matter of review of liberalisation of the entire RAP/PAP/ILP regime at
 the highest level in the Ministry of Home Affairs which act as a hindrance to the growth and development of domestic
 and international tourism to those regions.  The Committee may be apprised of the outcome in the matter from time to
 time.
(Para 69)
DOMESTIC CAMPAIGNS
            The Committee notes that the Ministry is launching a multi-pronged promotional campaign in the domestic
 markets under Incredible India Campaign.  The nation wide campaigns “Sare Jahan Se Achcha” and “Atithi Devo
 Bhava” aroused interest among the masses to travel within the country besides sensitization and educating the public of
 preservation of monument and places of tourist interests.  The Committee feels that despite “Incredible India
 Campaign” there still persists a gap in information dissemination among middle class domestic travelers especially
 from rural India about the places of tourist interests in the country.  The Committee, therefore, recommends the
 Ministry to print the information brochures in all regional languages including Hindi and English containing all minute
 details about tourist accommodation, unit rates, bus/taxi fares, climate, seasons and must see places details etc. and
 these are distributed to the tourists with the help of the States Tourism Departments so that the domestic travellers
 could largely be encouraged.   The Committee also recommends the Ministry to continue to focus on the diverse and
 varied tourism product of the country and create awareness about varied attractions amongst domestic travelers to tap
 and achieve the tourist potential available in the country.
(Para 73)
            The Committee also desires the Ministry to design integrated tour packages to suit to the budget and need of the
 tourists in collaboration with the Tour and Travel Operators to make domestic tourism a viable, popular and

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA

 comfortable mode besides strengthening tourists’ facilities at the tourist destinations, viz. transport, accommodation,
 catering, hygiene and sanitation etc. 
(Para 74)
OVERSEAS CAMPAIGNS
            The Committee notes that the allocation for overseas publicity and promotion has been increased substantially
 for the 2008-09.  The Ministry through its Overseas Offices endeavours to position India through “Incredible India”
 campaign as a  preferred tourism destination in the major source markets to increase India’s share in the international
 tourist arrivals. The Committee observed that the India with its rich cultural and history, has vast and varied in-built
 tourism potential and it should be exploited by the Ministry to its full potential.    The Committee, therefore,
 recommends the Ministry to promote India as a round the year destination through a 360 degree communication
 strategy, both in domestic and overseas market through a unique brand line “Incredible India” and reinforce
 Incredible India campaign as a unique and preferred tourism destination in the tourists generating countries.   The
 Committee also urges the Ministry to regularly review and monitor the functioning of the Overseas Offices in order to
 ensure effecting marketing and positioning of India as preferred tourist destination in the global markets. 
(Para 80)
            The Committee also recommends the Ministry to take initiatives to promote and market ‘India’ overseas
 targeting consumers directly through electronic and print media and internet based marketing and dissemination of
 information.   The Committee urges the Ministry to produce publicity material in various foreign languages and
 regularly launch awareness campaigns to sensitize/educate stakeholders in the tourism industry and general public on
 various issues pertaining to tourism such as tout menace, sanitation, preservation of monuments and tourist places,
 treatment of tourists etc.
(Para 81)
ROAD CONNECTIVITY
            The Committee notes there are a number of destinations and circuits have huge tourist potential.  The
 Committee is deeply concerned over the poor road connectivity of these tourism destinations and circuits including
 cultural heritage sites.  It observes that many of tourist destinations are away from the National Highways and lack
 road connectivity of desired standard.  However, the Committee notes that an Inter-Ministerial Group of Secretaries is
 looking after the road connectivity projects to identify the road links to tourist destinations, assess their present
 condition and suggests measures to improve connectivity to all major destinations/heritage sites with the National
 Highways.  The Ministry of Tourism has provided a list of 11 roads to the group for improvement and upgradation
 which connects the tourist destinations and circuits including heritage sites.    The Committee is the aware that
 improvement and upgradation of States roads, is the responsibility of States Government.  Therefore, the Ministry of
 Tourism should impress upon the respective States Government/U.T’s to improve the condition of such roads.  The
 Committee also recommends that the Government of India Should consider the proposals for improvement of States
 roads under Central Road Fund Scheme.
(Para 87)
            The Committee is perturbed to note that lack of connectivity is the major impediment for the growth of tourism
 in India.  The Committee feels that there exists a large domestic tourist movement in the country but in the absence of
 poor access to the places of tourist interest, the tourist cannot be encouraged to visit such places.   The Committee is of
 the view that domestic tourism cannot be promoted unless air, rail and road links across the country and especially the
 places of tourist interest are improved to desired level.   The Committee recommends that tourist destinations in the
 country should be well connected with the rail, road and air to ensure the easy accessibility to these places.  In order to
 improve the connectivity to tourist sites, the Ministry of Tourism should have done coordination with Ministry of
 Railways and Civil Aviation for promotion of tourism in the country.  The Ministry of Railways should provide better
 quality of rail services to encourage tourists to travel by train.  The basic amenities like drinking water, toilets, tea-
coffee, parking facilities and well-maintained clean waiting rooms and potters with trolleys   should also provided at the
 railways stations connecting these mega destination.   The Ministry of Civil Aviation should develop infrastructure
 facilities at Airports to meet the rising air traffic requirements and quality of service at the airports connecting mega
 destinations.  The domestic and foreign carriers should also be encouraged to increase air seat capacity from overseas
 markets.  The helicopter services for remote areas, like Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and North-eastern
 region  may also be initiated by the Ministry of Civil Aviation as a measure to promote tourism in a big way.

(Para 88)
MULTIPLICITY OF TAXES
            The Committee is constrained to notes that luxury tax on hotel, VAT on food and beverages and on Airlines
 Turbine Fuel (ATF) and higher rate of taxes on tourist transport vehicles in the States have adverse affect in the
 growth of tourism.   The Committee, however, is perturbed to note that even after repeated recommendations of the
 Committee, the Government has not been able to do much to rationalize tax regime, which is ailing the tourism sector
 at large.  The Ministry of Tourism has forwarded two proposals for consideration of  Empowered Committee of State
 Finance Ministers and Department of Road Transport and Highways respectively, in this regard and a decision is
 awaited.  The Committee strongly criticizes the lackadaisical approach of the Government in the matter which have
 adversely affected the growth of tourism and hospitality sector in the country.   The Committee reiterates that the
 Government must provide a level playing field to the tourism and hospitality sector including tourist transport by
 attempting to rationalize taxes or eliminate the disparity in tax treatment as levied by the different States and Union
 Territories.  The Committee recommends the Ministry to pursue vigorously the matter of rationalization of taxes with
 the Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers till the matter is favourably resolved.  The Committee also
 recommends the Government to set up an Empowered Group for rationalization of roads and transport taxes on
 tourist vehicles.  
(Para 91)
VISA-ON-ARRIVAL SCHEME
            The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism has taken up the matter of the issue of visa on arrival facility
 on pilot basis  to tourists with the Ministry of External Affairs and Ministry of Home Affairs for 18 select countries. 
 The Committee welcomes that the Ministry of Home Affairs has taken a decision to grant long term tourist visas 5 years
 duration with Multi - entry facilities to the nationals of the 18 countries and introduction of Advanced Passenger
 Information System (APIS).  However, the step is not sufficient to achieve the objective.  The Committee feels that with
 the liberlisation of visa regime and introduction of multiple entry long term tourist visa for tourist and implementation
 of APIS would facilitate tourist arrival in the country and will increase India’s share in global tourism markets.  The
 Committee recommends the Ministry to purse the matter with the Ministry of Home Affairs for expediting introduction
 of multiple entry long term tourist visa, provide visa on arrival facilities on pilot basis to the nationals of 18 countries
 and implementation of APIS.  The Committee also cautions the Ministry that in no way the security considerations of
 the country be compromised. 
(Para 97)
SPECIAL TOURISM POLICE
            The Committee is constrained to note that incidents of cheating, fleecing, criminal acts and harassment of foreign
 tourists including gender abuse mar the image of the country and have an adverse impact on the foreign tourists
 arrival. The Committee feels that the issue related with safety and security is paramount and needs to be looked into
 seriously.  The Committee is aware the linkages between Centre and States in the federal set-up and appreciates the
 efforts of the Ministry in persuading the States for creation of tourist police force for ensuring the safety and security of
 the tourists.   The Committee also notes that the Ministry of Tourism is formulating guidelines regarding formation of
 tourist police force and has taken several steps to curb the menace of cheating, over charging and victimization of
 tourists.  The Committee feels that in the critical situation, the role of media, travel agents and tour operators is crucial
 in establishing goodwill and image of that country. The Committee recommends the Ministry to take initiatives for
 deployment of special Tourist Police in the reamining States and bring out a guide lines on the formation of tourism
 police so as to address the safety and security related issues in a big way.    The Committee also desires that the police
 personnel of the States should also be provided special tourist oriented training.
(Para 102)
COORDINATION WITH VARIOUS DEPARTMENTS
            The Committee notes that the tourism is multi-disciplinary activity and cannot be developed at its own. The
 Committee also note that there exists a Committee of Secretaries for effective coordination and making decision on the
 policy matter amongst different Ministries.     The Committee feels that there is a need to strengthen the system for
 effective function and close coordination amongst various Department and Ministries of the Government i.e. Railways,
 Urban Development, Civil Aviation, Shipping and Road Transport and Highways, Home, Finance etc. The Committee,

 therefore, recommends the Ministry to set in place institutional arrangement for better linkages, interface and
 coordination amongst various Departments and Ministries so as to increase awareness about tourism and its social and
 economic impact of the society.

REPORT
India is one of the few nations in the world having a developed culture and a fast
developing economy. Its culture is deeply rooted in a pluralistic society. Development of culture
should be considered as a catalyst to the economic development. As such culture cannot be
confined to the boundaries of any particular sector. However, it could be recognized that there
are certain sectors wherein presence and contribution of culture and creativity are much more
dominant and visible. Elements of culture encompass media, films, music, handicrafts, visual arts,
Performing Arts, literature, heritage management, cultural and creative industries etc. The Cultural
development inter-alia  includes areas of Culture both in tangible and intangible fields.
2. The mandate of the Ministry of Culture is to preserve and promote all forms of art and
culture. To this end, the Ministry of Culture undertakes the following activities :
• The maintenance and conservation of the country’s heritage, ancient monuments and
historic sites;
• Promotion of the literary, visual and performing arts;
• Administration of libraries, museums and anthropological institutions;
• Maintenance, preservation and conservation of archival records and archival libraries;
• Research and development in the conservation of cultural property;
• Observation of centenaries and anniversaries of important national personalities and
events;
• Promotion of institutions and organizations of Buddhist and Tibetan studies;
• Promotion of institutional and individual initiatives in the field of art and culture;
• Entering into and implementation of cultural agreements with foreign countries;
3. The functional spectrum of the Ministry ranges from generating cultural awareness at the
grassroots level, to promoting cultural exchanges at an international level. Along with programmes
for the preservation of India’s ancient heritage, the activities of the Ministry encourage and
disseminate a variety of contemporary creative arts as well. The Ministry’s aim is to develop
ways and means through which the basic cultural and aesthetic sensibilities of the people remain
active and dynamic. The activities are carried out through the two attached offices, i.e. ,
Archaeological Survey of India and National Archives of India; seven subordinate offices and
thirty-three autonomous institutions working under the Ministry.
The following are the subordinate offices under the Ministry of Culture:
• Anthropological Survey of India, Kolkata
• National Museum, New Delhi
• National Gallery of Modern Art, New Delhi
• National Library, Kolkata

8. The Committee notes that the expenditure trend during 2007-08 is not very
satisfactory. For the plan allocation, expenditure of Rs. 370.39 crore has been incurred out

9. Regarding low utilization of funds, while considering the A TNs, the Committee was
informed by the Secretary that the Ministry has a very large number of small and diverse
activities which is probably causing the underutilization of funds. During the RE exercise in the
month of November by the Finance Ministry, the BE of Ministry of Culture has been reduced
invariably. The Secretary, Ministry of Culture has expressed its constraints:

3
‘‘One is that, about a quarter of our expenditure is done by the ASI which is not a
CPWD type but nevertheless of a work related expenditure which can only happen after
the monsoon and, therefore, gets into the second half of the year... Secondly, cultural
activities do come in, in an odd way because of cultural season which is really winter
and thereafter. Therefore, we have this second half of the year type of expenditure.
Usually the Ministry is able to spend 53% by December, however, the Ministry of Finance
desires that only 33 per cent of the allocation can be spent in last quarter. Thus, the
Ministry of Culture finds itself at a disadvantage.’’
10. The Committee in its 120th Report, had recommended to the Ministry of Culture that the
review of budgetary allocation by Government in the month of December may be taken up
instead of the month of September of the financial year. Subsequently, this matter was taken up
with the Ministry of Finance for their views/comments. In this regard, the Ministry of Finance
have shown their inability to alter the reviewing system of budgetary allocation, since the
preparation of budget documents for presentation of Annual Budget on 28th February starts from
December and it is, therefore, necessary to complete their R.E. exercise before this, which is
done during October-November every year.
11. The Ministry of Culture informed the Committee that the reduction in the budgetary
provision at RE stage from the original provision for the Ministry every year affects important
ongoing activities as well as proposed activities included in the Plan allocation made to cultural
organizations of the Ministry of Culture. This reduction in the budgetary provision hampers the
growth of cultural organizations especially development of infrastructural facilities including
building component, application of modern techniques and IT related techniques in their
functioning. Therefore, it is felt that the cultural organizations including autonomous organizations
need to be funded adequately to meet their developmental activities.
12. The Committee is unhappy to note that despite its concern and considered
recommendation, the Ministry of Finance has refused to review the budgetary allocations
in the month of December instead of in the month of September thereby subjecting the
Ministry of Culture to financial cuts at RE stage. The Committee observes that there is
a greater need and scope for scrutiny of entire exercise of Budgetary Process beginning
from budgetary proposals in September by the Ministry of Finance in respect of Ministry
of Culture because of its special needs. The Committee feel that the entire budgetary
process and procedure involving about eight months has actually given both to the evil of
mis-utilisation of funds in a hurried manner and apprehension of losing valuable but
scarce financial resources made available to them by Ministry of Finance at the fag end
of the financial year. It appears that given the rigidity in budgetary exercise the Ministry
of Finance has failed to assess actual requirements of the Ministry of Culture for funds
to be utilized for various developmental purposes. The Committee is of the firm belief
that the underutilization to a great extent in the Ministry of Culture is the result of rigid
financial practices and procedures. The Committee therefore, recommends the Planning
Commission and Ministry of Finance for giving an active consideration through a rigorous
and rational scrutiny for reforming and rescheduling of the present Budgetary procedures
and practice as far the Ministry of Culture is concerned, so that the final plan and non-
plan allocations are conveyed to the Ministry and to respective Institutions/organizations
by the month of December every year for effective and fruitful utilization of scarce
financial resources. Alternatively, the Committee recommends that the possibility may be
explored for provision of budget allocations for various activities may be converted as non-
Iapsable fund taking into account the seasonal nature of work and activities undertaken
by various institutions under the Ministry of Culture.

ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA (ASI)
17. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) was established in 1861. It is an attached
office of the Ministry of Culture. The major activities undertaken by ASI are: maintenance,
conservation and preservation of centrally protected monuments/sites and remains. In addition to
the above activities, it conducts archaeological exploration and excavation and underwater
archaeology regularly. Since its inception, the ASI has grown into a large organization having its
network of 24 circles throughout the country. There are 3667 monuments of National importance
in the country which are Centrally Protected Monuments, which include 21 properties inscribed
on the World Heritage List by UNESCO. ASI is also engaged in developing epigraphically
research, setting up and reorganization of site museums, imparting training programmes in
Archaeology, strengthening of the Chemistry Branch and Horticulture Branch. Publication
programme of ASI encompassing the fields such as academic, informative and awareness
generation is one of the important activities of ASI. This programme will be strengthened further
during the year 2008-09 so that more publications relating to archaeology could be brought out
for the general public, particularly for students.
18. In the BE 2008-09 the ASI has been provided with Rs. 312 crore consisting of plan
component of Rs. 111.00 crore. While emphasizing the importance of ASI, the Ministry of
Culture has informed the Committee that the increase in the budgetary allocation will benefit
mainly the Archaeological Survey of India and the building projects of National Gallery of
Modern Arts. The Committee drew attention of the Ministry of Culture to the problem vanishing
of centrally protected monuments. In the reply, the Secretary, Ministry of Culture during the
course of evidence submitted to the Committee:
‘‘... regarding the monuments which appear to be vanishing and which do not seem to
find trace. There are about 30-odd such monuments which we ourselves are now trying

5
to see where exactly and when they went out of the book. But, Sir, it is not easy
because some of these are not available for quite some time. It is not a recent
phenomenon per se . Some of them, I am given to understand by my Archaeologist
colleagues, are, actually, available. They know where it is but, maybe, it is covered by
water. They know that it is there but it is not protected in that sense. Since there is a
need to go into all these in detail, we have set up recently an internal committee within
the ASI to study this and come back with the factual position and, perhaps,
recommendations in this area. It has been recently done. That is something we would be
looking at.’’
19. The Committee notes that the cases of vanishing of our monuments is a dangerous
process which if not controlled in time, may lead to a situation where we will be left with
only a few monuments as symbols of our culture and tradition. The vanishing of
monuments should be stopped with all the resources at our disposal. The Committee notes
that the Ministry has already taken appropriate measures to prevent it. The Committee
may be apprised about the findings of the internal Committee to study the problems and
the steps taken to implement the findings with the result it achieved.
20. The Committee notes that the allocation for ASI has been reduced from BE 2007-08 of
Rs. 98.00 crore to Rs. 89.00 crore at RE stage. The main reason for reduction of allocation
at RE 2007-08 was that Rs. 10.00 crore under Sub-head 03 00 50 (other charges) was
earmarked in the BE 2007-08 for the National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities. Since the
NMMA is yet to be fully operationalized and State level implementation committees are not yet
formed, projects to be approved by them are yet to take off. Consequently, the allocation for
NMMA had to be reduced drastically at RE stage. Other sectors in which provision was
substantially reduced (in percentage terms) at RE Stage are Archaeological Site Museums and
externally aided programme. This work is now in advanced stages and the projects will take off
during 2008-09. In externally aided projects (JBIC project at Ajanta-Ellora) the low expenditure
level is due to time taken in completion of certain formalities. The increased allocation of
Rs. 111.00 crore under Plan for the financial year 2008-09 will be utilized to increase IT
applications in ASI, increased provision for publications, celebration of heritage awareness weeks
at various Monuments/Museums and greater participation of school students; to take up more
Conservation projects and to complete ongoing works; and for providing better facilities at
protected monuments (toilets, drinking water etc.).
21. The Committee hopes that ASI will learn from its past experience on the reasons
for underutilizations of allocated funds and take appropriate steps to utilize the allocated
resources. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should take immediate steps to
operationalise NMMA and expedite formation of State level implementation Committees so
that funds are utilized within the financial year. The Committee may be apprised about

25. The Ministry has informed that 249 centrally protected monuments have been encroached
illegally. Steps proposed to be taken to solve the problem of encroachments at protected
monuments are as under:—
(i) The monuments prone to encroachments shall be fenced on priority basis.
(ii) Secu rity at the monuments will be strengthened to avoid encroachments by
deploying regular watch and ward staff, private security guards.
(iii) To ensure better coordination and liaison with State Government District and Police
authorities to take immediate preventive action against the encroachers.
(iv) Arrange frequent inspections of the monuments by the officers.
(v) Make fresh appeal to various courts wherein status-quo  orders have been passed
against the removal of encroachments.
(vi) State/District level committees to be formed with members drawn from Revenue
Police, ASI, State Department of Archaeology, etc.
(vii) Rehabilitation policy will be put into effect for eviction of encroachers from the
centrally protected monuments.

29. The Committee recommends that to preserve the National Heritage from

NATIONAL ARCHIVES OF INDIA
35. Set up as an Imperial Records Department in 1891 in Calcutta, this Department was
shifted to Delhi in 1937 and renamed as National Archives of India after independence in 1947.
The National Archives of India is the custodian of non-current records of enduring value of
Central Government Ministries/Departments/offices and their predecessor bodies. National
Archives of India has one Regional Office at Bhopal and three Record Centres at Jaipur,
Pondicherry and Bhubaneswar. The main functions of National Archives of India include
accession of Public Records for permanent preservation, care and conservation of records in its
custody for posterity, preparation of reference media, dissemination of information, acquisition of
microfilm copies of records of Indian interests from abroad, regulation of access to records for
research and other purposes. Besides, National Archives of India is the Nodal Agency for records
management activities of the Central Government Ministries/ Departments/Offices as also of
Public Sector Undertakings, Statutory Bodies, Corporations, Committees and Commissions set up
by the Union Government and ultimate transfer of records of enduring value to National Archives
of India for permanent preservation and use by the posterity.

suffer for reduction in allocation.
INDIRA GANDHI NATIONAL CENTRE FOR THE ARTS
38. Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) is a premier National Institution
engaged in the pursuit of knowledge on arts and culture and in the exploration of relationships

10
of arts and culture with various disciplines of learning and diverse aspects of life. Established
in 1985 in the memory of the Late Prime Minister Smt. Indira Gandhi, it has multifarious
activities such as research, publication, training, documentation, dissemination and networking and
is poised to grow into a large repository of information pertaining to the arts in India. The
IGNCA seeks to place the arts within the natural and human environment by providing a forum
for creative and critical dialogue between the diverse arts, between the arts and sciences,
between the arts and the traditional and current knowledge systems. The IGNCA promotes
interaction and understanding between diverse communities, regions, social strata, and between
India and other parts of the world.

40. The Committee notes that IGNCA was allocated Rs. 45.00 crore in BE 2007-08 that
was reduced to Rs. 37.00 crore at RE stage. Out of this the IGNCA could utilize only
Rs. 33.00 crore. The Committee has time and again expressed its displeasure on non-
utilisation of funds even at the reduced RE level. Some initiative is needed on the part
of the Ministry to take corrective action and utilize the resources. The Committee may
be apprised about the steps taken to utilize the entire budget allocation.
MUSEUMS
(a) National Museum
41. National Museum set up in 1960 is a subordinate office under the Ministry of Culture.

activities of National Museum pertain to Acquisition of artifact, art objects organizing of

organizing exhibitions; both in the country and abroad; computerized documentation/digitization of
the art objects; publication of books, catalogues, bulletin, picture, postcards etc., and
strengthening of educational programme through its two mobile vans mounted with exhibition.

Manuscripts; Installation of Security Gadgets; Restoration/binding of rare and fragile Manuscripts

11

44. Indian Museum, founded in 1840, is the oldest and largest institutions of its kind in the

45. In the year 2007-08, plan allocation of Rs. 8.50 crore has been drastically reduced to

(vi) Development of Library including computerization of library holdings; (vii) Organizing
exhibitions and museum workshops.
46. The Committee is distress to note plan outlay of Rs. 8.50 crore was reduced to
Rs. 3.98 crore at RE stage because of non-implementation of some schemes like
modernization and reorganization of gallery; restoration and maintenance of museum
building; strengthening & modernization of security; and programme of education & mass
communication. The Committee recommends that corrective measures should be taken by
the Ministry for utilization of allocated amount in BE 2008-09 with proper planning and
putting monitoring mechanism in place. The Committee may be apprised of the efforts
made in this regard.

47. Victoria Memorial Hall (VMH) is a museum of contemporary art which is engaged in
collection of material and data relevant to a period depicting art history during the freedom
struggle. This Museum is also working as one of the Centres of the project of restoration of
oil painting of non-Indian origins, being coordinated by the National Museum, New Delhi. Major
activities undertaken under Plan by VMH are: modernization of galleries and storage of art objects
and installation of lighting, climate control, etc. organizing domestic Exhibitions, providing
assistance to organizations for preservation, restoration and conservation of art objects; work of
documentation, catalouging and photo documentation; acquisition of art objects; educational
programmes; and strengthening/modernization of security in VMH.

Administrative Block.
49. The Committee is perturbed to note that Victoria Memorial Hall could incur expenditure

SECURITY OF IMPORTANT ART ITEMS
50. To a specific query regarding priceless treasures like antique statues of Gods and
Goddesses, invaluable sculpture being regularly smuggled abroad under the grab of replicas from
villages of Rajasthan, Orissa, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Tamil Nadu, the
Ministry informed the Committee that the available data is not indicative of any regular smuggling
activity of antiquities. The premier investigating agency Central Bureau of Investigation have also
informed that during the period between 2005 and 2007, no case has been registered by them
relating to smuggling of antiquities. There are number of smuggling cases reported before this
period. Of these, the bronze images of Nataraja from Tamil Nadu, terrocotta Yakshi, Tamluk
(West Bengal), Stone pillars from Amin (Haryana), Terracotta figures from Bhitargaon (U.P.),
Image of Lakulisa from Jageshwar (Uttarakhand) have been retrieved after due legal process in
the respective Courts of different countries and through the Indian diplomatic channels. Constant
interaction takes place between ASI, CBI and Custom authorities to share information on
smuggling of art objects and to contain these activities.
51. The Committee notes that drawing any conclusion that no regular smuggling
activity of antiquities is taking place on the basis of available data with regard to cases
registered, is misleading. The Committee feels that smuggling activities are taking place
systematically in connivance of the local people. Therefore, the Committee recommends
that the Ministry should take measures to generate sufficient awareness amongst the
public as well as the custodians of law to strengthen the mechanism available in the
public domain to punish the culprits of smuggling activities. The Committee recommends
that Museum security is an important area and it should be given adequate attention.
Moreover, stealing and pilferage of important items kept in the museum should also be
taken care of by installing latest gadgets and by framing suitable policies in this regard
as museums are the treasure of our culture.
SCHEME OF PROMOTION AND STRENGTHENING OF REGIONAL AND LOCAL MUSEUMS
52. Under this grants-in-aid scheme, financial assistance is given for professional development
of museums, managed by voluntary organizations, institutions, societies, trusts, local bodies, etc.
including universities and colleges registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (XXI) or
under any law at present in force as well as those managed by the State Government, for the
purpose of (i) renovations/repairs/extension/modernization of galleries/augmentation of reserve
collections (ii) Publication programme, (iii) strengthening of Conservation laboratories/
Conservation projects (iv) Museum libraries (v) Equipments and (vi) Documentation programme.
53. Plan allocation in BE 2007-08 was Rs. 9.00 crore which was reduced to Rs. 7.00 crore
at RE stage. The expenditure incurred upto February, 2008 was Rs. 4.09 crore. In order to

13
provide more grants to eligible Musuems during 2008-09, the allocation has been increased to
12.00 crore this year as against the 7.00 crore (RE) of the last year.
54. The Committee observes that it is a welcome step and the scheme of promotion
and strengthening of regional and local museums need to be implemented with right
earnest. The Committee hopes that all the necessary steps for running the scheme should
be planned in advance and the allocation should be utilized judiciously.
NATIONAL GALLERY OF MODERN ART, NEW DELHI
55. The National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), founded in 1954, is the one and only
institution of its kind in the country representing evolution and pictorial transformation in Visual
Arts over the last 150 years. The main objectives of the NGMA are, to create an understanding
and sensitivity among the Indian public towards the visual and plastic arts in general and to
promote the development of contemporary Indian Art in particular. The NGMA has established
a functional branch at Mumbai to cater to the art loving public, particularly in the Western region
of the country. Another branch of NGMA in the Southern region, a premises called Manikyevelu
Mansion, has also been established at Bangalore. The collection of NGMA presently comprises
of 17813 works of art representing about 1742 contemporary Indian Artists, which include
Paintings, Sculptures, Graphics and Photographs.
56. During 2008-09, NGMA proposes to take up the work of modernization of galleries at
New Delhi and Mumbai at par with international standards, operationalization of new branch at
Bangalore and new wing at New Delhi by augmenting additional display and improvement of
facilities for the visitors; organizing 8 special exhibitions of eminent contemporary Indian artists
and holding of 4 exhibitions in various countries; organizing tr aveling exhibitions at Ahmedabad,
Patiala, Jaipur, Guwahati and Shillong; strengthening of the restoration laboratories; strengthening
of activities in the field of photographic documentation of art works, cataloging, computerization
and application of IT; conducting of educational programmes, seminars; etc.
57. The Plan allocation in BE 2007-08 of Rs. 4.50 crore was reduced to Rs. 4.00 crore at
RE stage. The Ministry informed that reduction at the RE is due to non-procurement of art
works during the current year. The Ministry also stated that the allocation in BE 2008-09 of
Rs. 5.00 crore is due to the opening of the new extension wing of the NGMA, New Delhi and
opening of the new branch of NGMA at Bangalore. There is also proposal to establish additional
galleries, provide better visitor facilities and organize special exhibitions with State of the-art
display technique etc. both at New Delhi as well as Bangalore.
58. The Committee appreciates the decision of the Ministry to open National Gallery at
Bangalore and hope that this will help in spreading the modern art culture of our country.
However, the Committee is concerned over the tendency of reduction of the allocation at
RE stage and even that allocation remains unutilized as the expenditure upto 29.2.2008 is
Rs. l.66 crore only. This shows the lackadaisical approach of the Ministry. The Committee
recommends that the allocated amount should be fully utilized by NGMA so that the
Government may not impose cuts in outlays at RE stage.

programmes such as science demonstration lectures, Astronomy related programmes, Taramandal

14
shows, Science Quiz, Popular Lectures, Science film shows, etc. NCSM has developed a

and Ranchi; setting up of three Sub-Regional Science Centres; and development of new 10
traveling exhibitions including Mobile Science Exhibition.
61. The Committee notes that out of the total plan allocation of Rs. 17.00 crore,
National Council of Science Museums could spend only Rs. 13.60 crore by February, 2008.
The Committee is of the view that proper planning for utilization of resources and
monitoring of the expenditure is the need of hour. The Ministry should take remedial
steps accordingly.
62. The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Ministry for popularizing science and
technology and the course being run on science communication. The Committee may be
apprised of the success of the two-years Post Graduate course on Science Communication.
MANAGING TREASURE AT LALIT KALA ACADEMY AND NATIONAL GALLERY OF
MODERN ART
63. Over the years, the Lalit Kala Academy and the National Gallery of Modern Art have been
buying art works from various artists. The Ministry informed the Committee that the Akademi
has already restored a majority of the paintings and prints in its collection from the normal
deterioration due to aging and temperature variations. The Akademi is also in the process of
making a world class storage facility for its collection. In addition to the storage facility, a
Restoration Lab for the works of art is also being conceived and executed for the New Delhi
office.
64. The Ministry further stated that the National Gallery of Modern Art has over 16500 art
works in its collection. These works of art are preserved properly under climate controlled
environment and the works of art, both in display and under storage, are periodically inspected

65. The Committee is of the view that the art works valuing hundreds of crore should
be preserved in an effective manner. Hence it recommends that there is more scope for
managing the treasures since a large number of paintings are still to be preserved/
restored. State of the art facility may be used for this job and expert guidance from other
countries can be sought and if need arises voluntary organizations may also be engaged
to preserve the art works.
INTER-MINISTERIAL COORDINATION
66. Taking notes of cultural events being organized abroad, the Committee desired to know
the extent of inter-Ministerial coordination between Ministries of Culture, Tourism and External

15
Affairs, the Secretary, Ministry of Culture informed the Committee that there is no formal
mechanism for Inter-Ministerial coordination between Ministry of culture, Tourism, External
Affairs, etc. The Secretary further stated that—
‘‘When programmatic requirements come up, we work together. For example, there was
Incredible India Programme in the US last year. There is a programme in China to come

PROMOTION AND DISSEMINATION OF  CULTURAL ACTIVITIES:
ZONAL CULTURAL CENTRES (ZCCs)
68. Seven Zonal Cultural Centres (ZCCs) were set up for the creative development of Indian
Culture in various regions. The essential thrust of these Centres has been to create a cultural
awareness among people and to identify, nurture and promote the vanishing folk art traditions in
the rural and semi urban areas of the States. The objectives of these centers are to provide local
creative support to folk and traditional artisans. They are:—
(a) Promotion of various art forms especially the folk art of the Zone.
(b) Setting up of Shilp Grams in each Zonal Cultural Centre to provide promotion and
marketing facilities to craftsman.
(c) National Cultural Exchanges Programme, exchange of artists, musicologists,
performers and scholars from one region to another within the country.
(d) Development of Infrastructural Facilities.
69. Two more activities have been entrusted to the Zonal Cultural Centres from the year 1993
viz. Republic Day Folk Dance Festival and Craft Fair; and Documentation of vanishing Folk Art
Forms. The zonal cultural centres will continue its major ongoing schemes during 2008-09 which
inter alia  includes national cultural exchange programme, documentation and publication, national
folk dance festival, shilpgram , guru-shishya parampara , theater rejuvenation, scheme for
recognition to young talented artists, crafts fare on republic day, Kurukshetra Utsav, training of
street children and slum area children and north-east festival. Plan allocation for Zonal Cultural

16
Centres in BE 2007-08 was kept at Rs. 13.00 crore. However, at RE stage Rs. 11.00 crore has
been allocated and expenditure upto February, 2008 is Rs. 10.88 crore.
70. The Committee is of the view that protection and promotion of vanishing folk art
tradition. is a very important mandate and in order to implement the mandate Zonal

2008-09 may be fully utilized and if possible allocation may be enhanced next year for the
purpose. The Committee also recommends that the Zonal Cultural Centres should expand
their activity to include the use of culture as an effective tool of national integration.
SETTING UP OF MULTI PURPOSE CULTURAL COMPLEXES INCLUDING THOSE FOR
CHILDREN
71. Under the scheme, financial assistance is provided to an autonomous body created by
State Governments to set up art complexes. The objectives of the schemes are that the quality
of life of young people be made sensitive to what is aesthetically and morally good in our
society. This can be done by exposing them to the finest forms of creative expression from an
early age. Cultural complexes for children will provide these avenues for our young people.
Multipurpose cultural complexes of general nature foster and coordinate activities in the State in
the different cultural fields such as music, drama, dance, literature, fine arts etc. and promote
through them the cultural unity of the country. Under the present terms and conditions, there
will be two categories of MPCC.
Category I:  It will be an integrated complex consisting of auditorium, with green rooms and
toilets, library/documentation centers, museum, exhibition gallery, storage space, conference hall/
seminar room, guest room/dormitory, children’s activity corner, cafeteria etc. (It is only an
indicative list of facilities). The project cost shall be limited to Rs. 5.00 crore and only one
MPCC will be allowed in each State under this category.
Category II: It will be a smaller version which may include any or all of the facilities like
auditorium, library/reading hall, workshop facilities etc. The project cost of this category shall be
limited to Rs. 2.00 crores and there can be more than one such MPCC in a State.
72. From the year 2007-08, the scheme of Multi Purpose Cultural Complexes was
discontinued at the instance of Planning Commission. It was desired that by the Planning
Commission that the MPCC Scheme may be restructured as a central sector scheme. For the
Tenth Five Year Plan, tentative allocation of Rs.80.00 crore has been made and in RE 2007-08
Rs.3.60 crore has been provided and expenditure incurred is Rs. 2.25 crore. For 2008-09,
allocation of Rs. 2.00 crore has been made.
73. The Committee notes that ceiling of the project cost fixed for single cultural
complex of Category-I is Rs. 5.00 crore and for Category-II smaller version cultural
complex is Rs. 2.00 crore. Whereas, the total allocation made for MPCC in the BE
2008-09 is only Rs. 2.00 crore. The Committee is at a loss to understand the rationality
behind this less allocations as even for a Category II MPCC an amount of Rs. 2.00 crore
is required. The Committee feels that this kind of approach will promote only adhocism.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the modalities for running the scheme may
be worked out and the scheme may be widely publicized for utilization of allocated
resources. The Committee may be apprised about the details of the number of MPCCs
already established till the last financial year and the details of the proposed MPCCs. The
Committee would also like to know the benefits of converting it into a Central Sector
Scheme.

77. The National Mission for Manuscripts (NMM) is the first consolidated national effort for

records. They represent the collective wisdom and experience of generations of thinkers. The
Mission was established in 2003 with the objective of creating a national resource base for
manuscripts, scattered across the country. The Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts is the

construction of the proposed museum would be taken up soon after and would be completed
within 2-3 years.
92. The Committee hopes that efforts for securing land will be taken up with Delhi
Development Authority in a time bound manner and if need be the issue may be taken
up at Ministerial level. The Committee recommends to the DDA that they should speed
up the process of land allotment to the Sangeet Natak Akademi at the earliest. The
Committee may be apprised about any procedural or administrative delay in the allotment
of land and construction of the building.
LALIT KALA AKADEMI
93. Lalit Kala Akademi (the National Academy of Arts) was established in 1954 for promotion
of visual and plastic arts in India like Painting, Graphic, Sculpture, Ceramic, etc. The Akademi
organizes Regional, National and International exhibitions regularly and also participates in various
Biennial and Triennial being organized by other countries abroad. In the past 50 years of its
existence, the Akademi has provided invaluable contribution to the Promotion of visual arts in
India by organizing exhibitions artists camps, Kala Melas and bringing out art publications.
94. The Committee notes that the plan allocation of Rs. 5.50 crore was reduced to
Rs. 5.00 crore at RE stage and further step up to Rs. 6.00 crore in BE 2008-09. The
expenditure reported upto 29 February, 2008 is Rs. 5.57 crore.
95. The Committee hopes that with the enhanced allocation in BE 2008-09, the Lalit
Kala Akademi will be able to spread its activities in more effective manner and will utilize
all its available resources.

96. National School of Drama (NSD) is one of the foremost theatre training institutions in the
world and the only one of its kind in India. It was set up by Sangeet Natak Akademi in 1959
as one of its constituent units. In 1975, it became an independent entity and since then it is
functioning as an autonomous organization under Ministry of Culture. Since its inception, the
School has not only made great strides in the area of theatre training but has also diversified
its activities. Besides the training programme, which is of 3 years duration, the School has
explored new vistas in the areas of Children Theatre and decentralization of theatre training
through organizing workshops.
97. The Plan allocation of Rs. l1.00 crore in BE 2007-08 was enhanced at RE stage to

Region by augmenting the scheme of National Theatre Festival and North East Region Theatre
Development. NSD proposes to organize Theatre workshops, to assist 15 theatre groups and to
organize part time courses during 2008-09, NSD will organize its Golden Jubilee Celebrations
during 2008-09. NSD also proposes to open 5 Drama Schools in different regions during
2008-09.
98. The Committee is pleased to note that National School of Drama is planning to
undertake lot of activities in the year 2008-2009. The Committee hopes that National
School of Drama will be able to fulfill its commitment in 2008-09 by planning its activities
in phased manner.
NEHRU MEMORIAL MUSEUM AND LIBRARY (NMML)
99. The Nehru Memorial Museum and Library was established in 1966 as a memorial to
Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of Independent India. Besides maintaining a
personalia museum focussing on the life and times of Jawaharlal Nehru, the major objectives of
this autonomous institution which is under the Ministry of Culture are to acquire, maintain and
preserve the personal papers and other historical material pertaining to nationalist leaders and
institutions of Modern India; to establish and maintain an advanced library on the history of
Modern India in all its aspects and to promote research in the fields of Modern Indian History
and Society. The Nehru Memorial Museum and Library (NMML) all through these years has been
successfully pursuing the aims and objectives set out in its Memorandum of Association and in
the process has continued to sustain and improve upon a tradition of excellence and commitment
to historical scholarship.
100. Plan Allocation for Nehru Memorial Museum and Library in BE and RE 2007-08 was
Rs. 3.50 crore. Additional provision of Rs.20.00 crore was provided for development and
modernization of NMML in accordance with the Finance Minister’s Budget Speech. Expenditure
of Rs. 22.45 crore was made upto 29.2.2008. Allocation in BE 2008-09 is Rs. 4.00 crore.
101. The Director, Nehru Memorial Museum and Library informed the Committee that—
‘‘The main focus of this proposal, and half the money, Rs. 20 crores, is allocated for
a massive digitisation programme for the archival resources of the Nehru Memorial
Museum and Library. We have about Rs. 90 lakhs of archival documents. We have about
1000 collections of what are called private papers, beginning from Nehru to lot of
business papers, to Salim Ali and Mohammed Bashir. It is really now the largest non-
official archives in India. And this is really frontier work and it has not even happened
in many parts of the world. We plan to digitise this entire collection, put it on Internet
and hopefully, if there are no legal and other difficulties about certain papers, put it right
on to the Net and make it searchable down to the last word. That is the kind of
technological up gradation that we have been working on. So, I have been working with
people at various levels, technological and others, to put together this whole project. We
have done pilot studies and done the research. We have really put together what we
know. This would cost us about Rs. 3 crores and 50 lakhs to digitise about 35 lakh
documents in the first stage. Then, coming to newspapers, we have about 110 lakh pages
of newspapers in all Indian languages. Beginning with English and Hindi, we would like
to digitise 20 lakhs of pages out of these 110 lakhs and that would take us another
Rs. 5 crore. To set up the digital archival management system, the hardware, etc. it
would cost another one crore rupees and the personnel, etc. would cost us about half
a crore of rupees. So, we have a Rs. 10 crore budget for this. We will try to do most
of this over the next year, beginning now, but some of it may necessarily spill over. The
second part of this is the modernisation of the existing library and we have allocated
Rs. 2 crore for that.’’

SCIENCE CITIES
104. Science Cities, at selected centres in the country were proposed to be set up during the
Ninth Five Year Plan. The Science Cities will be comprised of a Science Exhibition Hall, the
mass Science Area and a Science Park, The location of Science City should be either the State
Capital or one important city of the State having a sizeable population. Moreover, the state
Governments may provide the infrastructure facilities to these Centres free of cost. The total
cost of setting up of a Science City may be between Rs. 65-70 crores. The State Governments
and Societies/authorities promoting the setting up of Science Cities are eligible for financial
assistance from the Central Government under its Plan funds.
105. W ith the available funds during 2008-09, it is also proposed to set up Science Cities at
Ahmedabad, Allahabad, Hyderabad and Mangalore. Funds are also allocated for Regional Science
Centres at Raipur, Ranchi, Dharwad, Mangalore, Coimbatore, Jaipur and Science City, Bangalore
and sub-regional centres at Solapur and Kalimpong.
106. Plan allocation of Science Cities in BE 2007-08 was 13.00 crore which was reduced to
Rs. 10.89 crore at RE stage. The expenditure incurred upto February, 2008 was Rs. 7.89 crore.
Allocation in BE 2008-09 is Rs. 12.00 crore.
107. The Committee recommends that adequate plan outlay should be provided in the
Budget to ensure that science cities are set up in all the state capitals of the country and
while fixing priority every year parity should be drawn amongst the regions.

countries, with a view to projecting India’s culture and promoting bilateral cooperation between

countries should be selected where these festivals should be held continuously for some

114. The Ministry of Culture informed that an 18 member Committee has been constituted to

NATIONAL CULTURE FUND
118. The National Culture Fund (NCF) was set up in November, 1996 as a trust under
Charitable Endowment Act, 1890 with the aim of inviting the participation of the corporate
sector, NGOs, State Governments, Public/Private Sectors and individuals in the task of
promoting, protecting and preserving India’s cultural heritage as well as creation of new galleries,
museums and imparting of training in cultural activities. The donations to the National Culture
fund are eligible for 100 per cent tax exemption under Section 10 23C (iv) and 80 G (ii) of
the Income Tax Act. The NCF is managed and administered by a Council and an Executive
Committee. NCF is required to propagate its objectives in a big way through advertisements and
massive public relation efforts to mobilise sufficient funds.
119. At the time of constitution of NCF, it was decided that a corpus of Rs. 19.25 crore
would be provided by Ministry of Culture.

122. The States in the North Eastern Region are often considered to be at disadvantageous

124. On the recommendation of the Parliamentary Standing Committee under Para 61 of
120th Report many autonomous organizations under the Ministry of Culture have tied up with

are largely unexplored, and sites still lesser excavated, chiefly owing to non presence of a

it is largely engaged in activities like preservation and conservation of archaeological monuments.

east remain unrealized. The multitude of diverse ethnic tribes of these states are a major source

OBSERV ATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS — AT A GLANCE
BUDGET ALLOCATION AND OVERALL ASSESSMENT OF THE FINANCIAL
PERFORMANCE FOR THE YEAR 2007-08
The Committee notes that the expenditure trend during 2007-08 is not very
satisfactory. For the plan allocation, expenditure of Rs. 370.39 crore has been incurred out
of the RE of Rs. 520.00 crore. In the non-plan also, expenditure of Rs. 298.00 crore has
been incurred out of Rs.460.00 crore upto 29th February, 2008. Thus, Rs. 149.61 crore
in plan and Rs. 161.28 crore in non-plan remained to be utilized in the month of
March, 2008. (Para 8)
The Committee is unhappy to note that despite its concern and considered
recommendation, the Ministry of Finance has refused to review the budgetary allocations
in the month of December instead of in the month of September thereby subjecting the
Ministry of Culture to financial cuts at RE stage. The Committee observes that there is
a greater need and scope for scrutiny of entire exercise of Budgetary Process beginning
from budgetary proposals in September by the Ministry of Finance in respect of Ministry
of Culture because of its special needs. The Committee feel that the entire budgetary
process and procedure involving about eight months has actually given both to the evil of
mis-utilisation of funds in a hurried manner and apprehension of losing valuable but
scarce financial resources made available to them by Ministry of Finance at the fag end
of the financial year. It appears that given the rigidity in budgetary exercise the Ministry
of Finance has failed to assess actual requirements of the Ministry of Culture for funds
to be utilized for various developmental purposes. The Committee is of the firm belief
that the underutilization to a great extent in the Ministry of Culture is the result of rigid
financial practices and procedures. The Committee therefore, recommends the Planning
Commission and Ministry of Finance for giving an active consideration through a rigorous
and rational scrutiny for reforming and rescheduling of the present Budgetary procedures
and practice as far the Ministry of Culture is concerned, so that the final plan and non-
plan allocations are conveyed to the Ministry and to respective Institutions/organizations
by the month of December every year for effective and fruitful utilization of scarce
financial resources. Alternatively, the Committee recommends that the possibility may be
explored for provision of budget allocations for various activities may be converted as non-
lapsable fund taking into account the seasonal nature of work and activities undertaken
by various institutions under the Ministry of Culture. (Para 12)
The Committee is happy to note that for the first time, allocation for the Ministry
of Culture has reached to four figures. The Committee feels that it is a good beginning
for this vital sector which has huge potential but yet to be explored. The Committee
hopes that all the new schemes and projects taken up by the Ministry during the financial
year 2008-09 will be completed in a time bound manner. (Para 13)
The Committee also recommends that possibility of organising off-season festivals
and organizing Dance/Cultural programmes throughout the year may be explored. The
Ministry should also explore for decentralization of some of the schemes which can help
the Zonal Centres in expediting their work. This will certainly help in providing much
needed relief to the Ministry. The Committee also recommends that in spite of the
