regard as museums are the treasure of our culture.
Reply of the Government
72. Ministry of Culture has instructed all the protected monuments and site museums under ASI
and museums directly under the Ministry of Culture and its autonomous bodies for appropriate
security measures. They have adopted measures for adequate protection by way of deploying CISF
and Private Security Agencies, installation of CCTV, Metal detector, fire smoker etc. wherever
necessary.

13
73. In order to ensure the safety of cultural heritage under its protection, the ASI uses private
security guards, State police and home guard personnel and also the CISF at selected monuments.
Constant interaction takes place between ASI, CBI and Custom authorities to share information on
smuggling of art objects and to contain these activities.
74. There exist suitable provisions in the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act, 1972 for regulation
of export in antiquities and art treasures and for prevention of their illicit trafficking, such as
registration of dealers, registration of specified categories of antiquities, prosecution of offenders
etc. The ASI deploys officers at the various international exit channels to assist the Custom
authorities in identifying the objects of antique nature and art treasures so that the smuggling
activities could be curbed.
75. ASI has initiated action for preparation of data base on antiquities that are available in the site
museums, sculpture sheds, loose sculptures available within the premises of protected monuments,
stores and those kept at temporary shelters. A consolidated data base will be helpful in containing the
smuggling of antiquities and retrieval of stolen objects. In order to ensure the security of museums
and important objects kept therein, ASI has provided gadgets such as CCTV, metal detectors, security
and fire alarm systems in many of its site museums and will soon cover the remaining ones as well.
Proposals are being formulated for increasing security staff at all monuments.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee

of the Museums and recommend that security need to be updated on regular basis to be a
step ahead of the culprits.

134. Recommendation of the Committee has been noted. During the operation of the ‘Science
Cities’ scheme certain bottlenecks were experienced. Under the existing norms, for setting up of
the Science City the total financial cost is between Rs. 65-70 crore to be shared by the State
Government, Central Government and Private Entrepreneurs in the ratio of 13:13:74. However, it
was found that 74% share to be raised through private entrepreneurs or any other agency by the
State Government was not forthcoming. This necessitated changes in the existing norms and
accordingly the Ministry is in the process of revising the ‘Science Cities’ Scheme. Under the
revised norms, the total cost of setting up of a Science City has been reduced to Rs. 50.00 crore
out of which State Government’s contribution will be of Rs. 20.00 crore to be raised either
by themselves or by a private/co-operative agency or a combination of both. A provision of
Rs. 90.00 crores for Science Cities scheme has been made in the Eleventh Five Year Plan.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
135. The Committee hopes that the modification in the existing norms will be taken up
at the earliest so that the allocated amount is spent and Science Cities reaches all the
States in a time bound manner.

(Recommendation at Para 108)
136. The Committee appreciates the efforts in spreading Indian culture abroad by holding seminars,
fairs and festivals. The Committee recommends that the festivals should be highly focused and
highlights every region of the country so as to promote tourism and culture of all the States. The
Committee also recommends that some countries should be selected where these festivals should be
held continuously for some years so as to make an impact on the population there.
Reply to the Government
137. Recommendations of Committee have been noted, and shall be implemented suitably subject
to availability of funds.

23
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
138. The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry and recommends that additional
requirement of funds should be communicated to Ministry of Finance well in time so that
the scheme does not suffer.

(Recommendation at Para 111)
139. The Committee notes that in spite of Ministry’s attention being drawn to the fact of delay
in appointing administrative heads, no significant achievement has been made in most of the
organizations under the control of the Ministry. And in many cases some of the officials of the

Reply to the Government
152. Out of the amount of Rs.47.00 crore allocated for NE region at RE stage, during 2007-08,
an amount of Rs.34.44 crore was utilized upto 31.3.2008, by the Ministry and its various

organizations and Divisions to augment the expenditure in North East area from the very beginning

issues involved in establishing the Excavation Branch in the North East.

155. To ex pand the archaeological excavation programmes in the north-eastern region of the

ASI, Guwahati Circle, Guwahati exclusively for archeological exploration in the N.E. region.

156. The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry and recommends that full-fledged
Excavation Branch should be set up in the North-East to give more concentration in the
North-East States.

present this One Hundred and Forty-seventh Report on “Action Taken by the Government on the
Recommendations/Observations of the Committee contained in its One Hundred and Thirty-eighth
Report on Demands for Grants 2008-09 of the Ministry of Civil Aviation”.

Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture was presented to the Parliament on the
28th April, 2008.
3. The Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained on its
One Hundred and Thirty-eighth Report were received from the Ministry of Civil Aviation on the
12th December, 2008.

1
REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Civil Aviation
on the observations/recommendations as contained in its One-Hundred and Thirty-eighth Report on
Demands for Grants (2008-09) of Ministry of Civil Aviation, which was presented to both the
Houses of Parliament on 28th April, 2008.
2. Action Taken Replies have been received from the Department on the 12th December, 2008
in respect of all the observations/recommendations contained in the Report, which have been
categorised as follows:—
(i) Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Department:
Para Nos. 6,
 11, 21, 41, 48, 52, 55, 66, 69, 70, 72, 76, 80, 81, 82, 83, 85  Total-17

of the Department replies:

been accepted by the Committee:
Para Nos. 30, 62 T otal-2

still awaited:
Para No. NIL
Total-19
ANNUAL PLAN 2007-08
(Recommendation at Para 6)
3. The Committee notes that Ministry of Civil Aviation has failed to fully utilize the outlay
approved during 2007-08. This looks something strange at a time when the civil aviation sector is
witnessing an unprecedented growth for past few years. The Ministry anticipates to utilize an
amount of Rs.11211.61 crore only out of the approved allocation of Rs.12347.09 crore during the
year 2007-08, which exemplifies the poor financial management in the Ministry of Civil Aviation.
The Committee feels that there is a lack of proper planning in the various organisations of Ministry
of Civil Aviation, as a result of which the Ministry was unable to utilize optimally the approved
outlays at its disposal. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Civil Aviation
should impress upon the concerned agencies to make a realistic assessment of their financial
requirements so that the allocations made do not remain unutilized.
Reply of the Government
4. The details of approved outlay and actual expenditure is as under:
(Rs. in crores)
Approved Plan Outlay Actual Expenditure % of outlay
(a) – IEBR 12187.09 1 1059.52 90.75
(b) – GBS (Revised) 160.09 152.09 95.05
T
OTAL: 12347.09 11211.61 90.80

2
5. The reasons for less expenditure are as under:
(i) Airports Authority of India
AAI had proposed to incur expenditure of Rs.1961.41 crores during the year 2007-08 which
was revised to Rs.1980.95 crores at RE stage. Against this, AAI had incurred an expenditure of
Rs.1980.23 crores during 2007-08. Further AAI has drawn the full amount of budgetary support
projected in RE 2007-08 amounting to Rs.55 crores. Keeping in view the progress of works and
expected clearances for modernization of Kolkata and Chennai airports, AAI has projected an
expenditure of Rs.3377.10 crores during 2008-09.
(ii) National Aviation Company of India Limited (NACIL)
At the time of formulation of the Annual Plan 2007-08, it was estimated that a total of 15
aircraft shall join the fleet of NACIL (erstwhile IAL : 9 aircraft and erstwhile AI : 6 aircraft). As
against 15 aircraft, 19 aircraft have joined the fleet (erstwhile IAL : II aircraft and erstwhile
AI : 8 aircraft) during 2007-08. However, in spite of the delivery of additional 4 aircraft during
2007-08, reduction in outgo is mainly due to:—
(a) Favourable exchange rate and lower escalation factor in respect of erstwhile Air India
as compared to the escalation estimated in the Plan Projection.
(b) Saving due to delay in delivery schedule of aircraft, resulting in deferment of advance
payment in respect of B-787 - 8 aircraft.
Aircraft acquisition comprises almost 97% of the “total plan outlay allocation” of NACIL. The
remaining outlay is in respect of “Other Capital Project” which mainly caters to the expenditure on
Other Supporting Facilities such as ground support equipment, miscellaneous equipment and assets,
corporate computerization etc. Expenditure under this head is undertaken only when it is essential
and operationally required without compromising operational efficiency.
(iii) Air India Charters Limited (AICL)
As per the Annual Plan for the year 2007-08, 5 B-737-800 aircraft were to be received and
the same have been reeeived during 2007-08. The shortfall of Rs.197.69 crore is on account of:—
(a) Exchange variation due to reduction in exchange rate.
(b) Lower escalation factor as compared to the Plan Projection.
(c) Only essential operational projections are being undertaken without affecting the
operational efficiency of the Company.
As such, the shortfall in expenditure in 2007-08 works in NACIL’s favour.
(iv) Pawan Hans Helicopters Ltd.
The approved plan outlay for 2007-08 of PHHL was Rs.246.50 crores which included
acquisition of 7 new helicopters during the year at an estimated cost of Rs. 190 crores. Board of
Directors of PHHL have decided that acquisition of 20 helicopters projected during Eleventh Five
Year Plan period be processed together at one go instead of the proposed year-wise induction plan
projected earlier, keeping in view the prevailing long delivery schedules of helicopters upto 24
months after advance payments and market demand for helicopters, time required for tender
process and Government approval each time. Accordingly, advance payment of Rs. 91.20 crores
towards acquisition of entire 20 Nos. helicopters is now proposed by PHHL in their Annual Plan
2008-09. Earlier in Eleventh Five Year Plan Projections, an amount of Rs. 160.50 crores was
provided towards payment for acquisition of 6 Nos. helicopters during Financial Year 2008-09.

3
The Annual Plan for the Financial Year 2008-09 of PHHL has been reviewed keeping in view
the above. The approved Plan Outlay of Rs. 123.80 crores includes acquisition of new fleet
(advance payment of Rs. 91.30 cores, towards 20 helicopters) midlife upgradation of Dauphin fleet,
import of capital equipment, creation of Maintenance Centre and Heliport, building and other
projects, IT Plan and other Civil/Electric work etc.
(v) Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA)
A provision of Rs. 87 crore was made in BE 2007-08 and during RE 2007-08 this provision
was reduced to Rs. 56 crores in respect of DGCA. An expenditure of Rs. 52.99 crores was
incurred in 2007-08, which amounts to 95% (approx) w.r.t. RE 2007-08. As for the financial year
2008-09, steps have been initiated to utilise optimally the funds allocated to DGCA.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
6. The Committee notes reply of the Ministry.
BUDGET 2008-09 AND ANNUAL PLAN FOR 2008-09
(Recommendation at Para 11)
7. The Committee feels that reduction in Budgetary support of the Ministry will definitely have
a negative impact on the expansion of aviation sector in North-Eastern region as the approved
budgetary support component does not include the outlay of Rs.45.00 cores proposed to be given
as a grant for the setting up of Greenfield Airport at Pakyong, Sikkim. The Committee recommends
that the Ministry may take this issue with the Finance Ministry at RE stage and prevail upon them
to grant more money to ensure that works for project start well in time. The Committee expects
that the Government will ensure that the targets set for internal and extra budgetary resources as
well as external commercial borrowings from foreign banks/financial institutions for bridging the
gap in budgetary support will materialize. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should take
adequate steps during 2008-09 also to ensure optimum utilisation of the enhanced allocations made
to various organisations.
Reply of the Government
8. A greenfield airport at Pakyong, Sikkim is proposed to be constructed by AAI at an
estimated cost of Rs.358.94 crores (on completion costs basis). Eleventh Finance Commission had
awarded an amount of Rs.50 crores to Government of Sikkim for this project, out of which
Rs.13.30 crores were released during the award period. Subsequently, the 12th Finance
Commission has made an award of Rs.1 00 crores to the State Government for the airport project.
An amount of Rs.50 crores has been released to the Government of Sikkim, till now, against the
12th Finance Commission award. State Government has assured that they would transfer this
amount of Rs.113.30 crores to AAI for execution of project. The balance amount of Rs.245.64
crores shall be funded as 90% grant by Central Government ( i.e. Rs.221.08 crores) and 10% from
the internal resources of AAI ( i.e. Rs.24.56 crores). This Ministry had requested for the release
of an amount of Rs.45 crores as Central Grant (out of the total amount of Rs.221.08 crores)
during 2008-09, which was not accepted at BE stage. The demand will be taken up again at the
RE stage depending upon the fund position.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
9. The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry and hopes that the Ministry will
impress upon the Planning Commission to release the additional amount of Rs.45 crore for

4
the airport project at Pakyong, Sikkim so that the project is not delayed for want of funds
as with the construction of the new airport in Sikkim, the north-eastern sector will get
boost in tourism and trade sector.
NATIONAL A VIATION COMPANY OF INDIA LIMITED
(Recommendation at Para 21)
10. The Committee notes that profit of both the erstwhile Air India and Indian Airlines has gone
down substantially due to varied price of A TF, rapidly declining passenger revenue yields on
account of intense competition and deployment of excess capacity in the market, etc. The
Committee hopes that merger process of both these carriers will be completed in time and this
process will help the national carrier in long run in consolidating its position in domestic and
international market. The Committee hopes that the synergisation process would help to improve
the operational efficiency of both the carriers. However, the Committee is of the view that NACIL
should adopt an aggressive marketing strategy to face the stiff competition at global level as well
as domestic level in order to have a level playing field with that of competitors. The Committee
appreciates the steps taken by NACIL to increase the market share of Air India with the fleet
strength of around 110. The Committee desires that the number of bilateral agreements which were
signed during the last year should be materialized to the maximum possible extent. The Committee
hopes that with the induction of new aircrafts in its fleet, Air India can regain its glory and
Maharaja status. The Committee desires that the NACIL will soar to new heights by optimally
utilizing its man power and available resources which is not available with any of its competitor.
The Committee hopes to see that NACIL will come out of the red and make profits in near future.
The Committee recommends to the Government that they may commission a study to know how
the private airlines are functioning including the financial freedom they are enjoying, their efficiency
and customer service. The findings of the study may be used for the improvement of NACIL. The
Committee may be apprised about the findings of such a study and the steps taken to improve the
performance of NACIL.
Reply of the Government
11. NACIL has been continuously implementing various marketing initiatives keeping in view the
demand of the market as well as to provide attractive options for its customers. These comprise
of promotional offers and schemes, which provide value addition for the passengers and also enable
the airline to retain its competitiveness in the market as well as assist in increasing the revenues,
capacity utilization and market share. These measures, taken from time to time, comprise of pricing
initiatives, short term and long term schemes. The launch of these schemes depend upon various
market factors like seasonality, market presence and strength of the airline vis-a-vis its competitors,
supply and demand equation etc. These schemes also seek to stimulate the market by creating new
market segments and to provide value-enhanced services to our passengers.

Andhra Pradesh in reducing the Sales Tax on ATF from 32% to 4% recommends that the Ministry
pursue this long standing issue with other State Governments so that uniformity of tax on ATF can
be maintained. Since the Cost of fuel is an important component of cost structure, reduction in
taxes on A TF will definitely have a positive impact on the airfares. The Committee once again
recommends that Ministry of Finance should sympathetically consider and give approval to the
proposal of Ministry of Civil Aviation regarding notifying ATF as ‘Declared Good’ under Section

73. State Government had been requested to consider moderation of the rate of sales tax

rules relating to the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committees, the Hon'ble Chairman,
Rajya Sabha, referred** the Bill to the Committee on the 31st December, 2008 for examination and
report on or before 15th February, 2009.
3. The Committee took oral evidence of the Secretary, Department of Road Transport and
Highways and Chairman, National Highways Authority of India at its meeting held on the
19th January, 2009.
4. The Committee considered the draft Report on the subject and adopted the same on
13th February, 2009.
6. The Committee wishes to express its thanks to the Secretary and other officers of the
Department of Road Transport and Highways, Chairman, National Highways Authority of India and

1
REPORT
The National Highways Authority of India (Amendment) Bill, 2008 was introduced in the
Lok Sabha on the 22nd December, 2008. The Bill was referred to the Department-related
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture for examination and report.
Under the mandate, the Committee has examined the Bill and finalised the Report after hearing the
views of the nodal Department i.e. Department of Road Transport and Highways. The Bill seeks
to further amend the National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988.
2. The reasons for introduction of the Bill, as informed by the Department of Road Transport
and Highways have been enumerated in the succeeding paragraphs.
3. The National Highways Authority of India was established as a statutory body under the
National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) Act, 1988, and was operationalized in February, 1995
with the appointment of a fu ll-time Chairman . NHAI’s initial mandate in 1996 was the projects
undertaken with the assistance of Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Japan Bank for International
Cooperation (JBIC). Subsequently in 1998, the Government of India announced the National
Highways Development Project (NHDP) comprising mainly the Golden Quadrilateral and other
projects in Phase-I and the North-South and East-West corridors in Phase-II. The Government of
India (GoI) has now entrusted NHAI the responsibility of implementing a greatly expanded National
Highways Development Project (additional Phases III to VII) with an investment of about
Rs.2,20,000 crore. The new phases of NHDP are to be implemented mainly through Public Private
Partnership (PPP), either as Build, Operate and Transfer (BOT) (Toll) projects or as BOT (Annuity)
projects.
4. The proposed Bill focuses on building up the institutional capacity of the NHAI by
expanding its membership to ensure focused attention to all PPP policy issues, appraisal and
implementation of PPP projects.
5. The Committee on Infrastructure (COI) under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister had
taken following decision in respect of the institutional strengthening of NHAI in its meeting held
on 13.01.2005:
“In order to provide autonomy and delegate more powers to NHAI for approval of
individual projects within the overall programme including the financing structure approved
by CCEA, it is necessary to build institutional capacity of NHAI by making it a
multidisciplinary professional body with high quality financing management and contract
management expertise.”
6. In pursuance to the decisions of the COI as mentioned above and suggestions of the
Planning Commission, an Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) was constituted under the
Chairmanship of Secretary, Road Transport and Highways and members from Department of
Economic Affairs, NHAI, Planning Commission and experts in the field of highways. IMC
considered various drafts prepared by NHAI as well as by Planning Commission and carefully
examined the need of restructuring, in view of the mandate being given to NHAI particularly in the
context of paradigm shift in project implementation from civil works contract with full Government
funding to project implementation mainly through Public Private Partnership (PPP).
7. IMC recognized that within the broad policy framework set by the Government of India,
NHAI has to act as a professional, commercially-oriented organization and has to focus on cost-
effective and timely delivery. For this, the key approaches and underlying considerations for the
new organizations structure are:

2
• A structure designed to improve decision making efficiency in a transparent manner
ensuring responsiveness to changes taking place in the environment.
• A lean organization structure continuing the tradition of significant outsourcing and
leveraging the skills and resources available from the private sector.
• An organization with high dependency on technology and a proper system of ensuring
accountability.
• Achieving improved retention of experience and staff within the organization so as to
maintain the level of expertise and organizational competence.
• Inculcating multidisciplinary skills within the organization for better project appraisal
and monitoring.
8. IMC recommended following vision statement for NHAI:
“To meet the nation’ s need for the provision and maintenance of National Highways
network to global standards and to meet user’ s expectations in the most time-bound and
cost-effective manner, within the strategic policy framework set by the Government of
India and thus promote economic well being and quality of life of the people.”
9. NHAI has adopted a business model that rests on outsourcing of specific tasks related to
design, construction and supervision of works and the subsequent management of corridors. IMC
was of the view that for managing such a large programme within the prescribed time-frame, there
is no alternative to the model of outsourcing. NHAI should, therefore, continue with the
outsourcing model which also has the advantages of keeping the organisation relatively lean,
harnessing private sector efficiencies, and providing flexibility in execution of works.
10. NHAI, nevertheless, remains accountable to the NH users and the Government of India for
the quality of service/output provided by contracted service providers, hence, NHAI need to have
in-house capacity for efficient procurement and monitoring of contract outputs and services.
11. IMC considered strengthening of the NHAI Board, its organizational structure, the human
resources management and strengthening of systems and processes as the key areas for
strengthening NHAI.
12. Currently, Chairman, NHAI is nominated by Government of India, from among serving civil
servants. IMC has recommended that the selection of candidates for the post of Chairman, NHAI
should be done by a search committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary comprising the Secretary,
Department of Road Transport and Highways; Secretary, Planning Commission and one of the
Directors of the IIMs and one CMD/MD of a financial institution. To ensure continuity of the
Chairman for effective management, the Chairman should be given a minimum tenure of three years
extendable by another two years. The age limit may also be relaxed upto 62 years in case it is
necessary to provide the minimum tenure of three years.
13. As per the provisions of the NHAI Act, 1988, the Authority consists of a Chairman, not
more than five full time members; and not more than four part time members. At present, the full
time Members include Member (Administration), Member (Finance) and three Members (Technical),
while the four part time Members include Secretary, Department of Road Transport and Highways;
Secretary, Planning Commission; Secretary, Department of Expenditure and Director General (Road
Development), Department of Road Transport and Highways.
14. Keeping in view the vastly increased mandate for NHAI and also the greatly enhanced
participation envisaged for the private sector, it is proposed to increase the full time Members from
five to six and part-time Members from four to six, to allow induction of professionals of repute

3
in the fields of financial management, transportation planning and other relevant areas. Induction
of outside professionals will enhance the capacity of the Authority to take strategic decisions,
widen its perspective, bring in best management practices, and assist in achieving the goal of
higher private participation.
15. The Cabinet in its meeting held on 5th July, 2007 approved the proposal for restructuring
of NHAI which includes:—
(i) NHAI to have six full time members (against five at present) – one each for finance,
administration, public private partnership (PPP), two Members (Projects) and one
Member (Technical).
(ii) Increase in the number of part-time Members by two (from 4 to 6), who would be
from the non-Government sector, one from IITs/IIMs and the other from financial
institutions.
(iii) Amendment to NHAI Act, 1988 (to effect the revis ed strength of the Board).
16. Amendment will be required in sub-section (3) of section 3 of the NHAI Act, 1988 for
increasing the number of full-time Members from five to six and part-time Members from four to
six. Subsequent to the amendment in the NHAI Act, 1988, the National Highways Authority of India
(the term of office and other conditions of service of Members) Rules, 2003 will be amended
accordingly.
17. The expenditure on salary, allowances, other remuneration and facilities provided to the
members will be met from the National Highways Authority of India Fund as provided under
Section 18 of the Act.
18. The Committee in its meeting held on the 19th January, 2009 heard the views of the
Secretary and other officials of the Department of Road Transport and Highways, Chairman,
National Highways Authority of India and Ministry of Law and Justice on the Bill and sought replies
to the queries on the subject. The Committee in its meeting held on 13th February, 2009 considered
the Bill and the Committee’s consideration/recommendations have been given in the succeeding
paragraphs.
19. Clause 2 of the Bill reads – In the National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988, in
section 3, for sub-section (3), the following shall be substituted, namely:—
“(3) The Authority shall consist of:-
(i) a Chairman;
(ii) not more than six full-time members; and
(iii) not more than six, but at the least four, part-time members,
to be appointed by the Central Government by the notification in the Official Gazette:
Provided that the Central Government shall, while appointing the part-time members, ensure
that at least two of them are non-government professionals having knowledge or experience
in financial management, transportation planning or any other relevant discipline”.
20. When the Committee specifically asked about the need for induction of additional members
through the amendment, the Secretary replied that
“...sometime in 2006, the Committee on Infrastructure had reviewed the capacity of the
NHAI to implement such a large programme. It was felt that the institutional capacity of
NHAI needs to be strengthened, both by way of giving additional manpower and also by

4
creating posts for experts. The areas which were found to be strengthened, particularly
were the areas of say financial management, legal expertise and, of course, managerial
expertise, in general...”
21. The Department while submitting the detailed background note to the Committee as
mentioned in earlier paragraphs of the report substantiated the need for this amendment. The
Department has further stated that the NHAI which was operationalized in February, 1995 with the
appointment of full-time Chairman has come a long way from implementing projects with the
assistance of international agencies to have the responsibility of implementing the greatly expanded
National Highways Development Project (additional phases III to VII) with a large investment of
about Rs. 2,20,000 crore at present. The National Highways Development Project announced by
the Government of India in the year 1998 has really changed the functioning of the NHAI. The
NHAI started off with only ten projects in certain stretches of the Golden Quadrilateral in its earlier
days, has now projects spread all over the country. Funding pattern of the projects undertaken by
NHAI has also changed during the course of time. Earlier the projects were financed through
Government funding and aid from international financial institutions, but the new phases of NHDP
are to be implemented mainly through Public Private Partnership (PPP), either as Build, Operate and
Transfer (BOT) (Toll) projects or as BOT (Annuity) projects.
22. The institutional strengthening process of NHAI which started in the year 2005 by the
decision of Committee on Infrastructure (COI) under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister was
finally approved by the cabinet in its meeting held on the 5th July, 2007. During the deliberations
of the Committee, the Secretary, Department of Road Transport and Highways and the Chairman,
National Highways Authority of India placed their views on the necessity to bring this amendment.
23. The Committee is of the view that this Bill appears to be a piece-meal effort on the
part of the Government that does not really address the basic issues highlighted in the
decision of the Committee on Infrastructure (COI) particularly those relating to greater
autonomy and delegation of more powers to NHAI for approval of individual projects. The
Committee feels that the Bill has been used as a contingent legislative tool. The
Government should avoid such attempt so that the dignity and importance of the Parliament
is maintained. The Committee appreciates the Government’s attempt for strengthening the
NHAI by adding professionals of repute in the fields of financial management and
transportation planning, it, however, feels that merely by adding numbers in the Board will
not yield the desired results as expected in the new vision statement of NHAI. The
Committee is of the opinion that having road projects worth Rs. 2,20,000 crore, NHAI would
certainly require much more than that, such as delegation of more powers to NHAI for
approval of individual projects; strengthening of its organization structure; improving its
human resource management and systems and processes of NHAI.
24. The Committee also finds that the amendment is silent on the issue of fixed tenure
for the Chairman, NHAI. The Committee notes the recommendation of the Inter-Ministerial
Committee (IMC) that to ensure continuity of the Chairman for effective management, the
Chairman should be given a minimum tenure of three years extendable by another two
years. The IMC also recommended that the age limit may also be relaxed up to 62 years
in case it is necessary to provide the minimum tenure of three years. The Committee
expresses its disappointment over the non-inclusion of such important recommendations
which will have a longstanding effect on the functioning of NHAI in this amendment.
25. The Committee finds discrepancy in this amendment on the inclusion of additional
part-time members. The Statement of Objects and Reasons of the Amendment Bill states
that in order to increase the efficiency, the number of part-time members of the Board has
been increased from four to six but the formulation of the Bill in Clause 2 reads ‘not more

5
than six but not less than four’ thus defeating the objective of increasing the numbers from
four to six. Section 8 of the original Act and Section 3 of the present Bill are not in
harmonious construction. Section 8 says no vacancy will invalidate the decisions of NHAI
Board, whereas Section 3 says there will be minimum four and maximum six part time
members in the Board of NHAI. It means, if the number is less than four, the Board cannot
take any decisions. This might create confusion which needs to be looked into for removing
possible ambiguity. The Committee therefore, urges upon Government to carefully consider
all the points mentioned above and recommends that the Government should come up with
a comprehensive legislation incorporating all the suggestions made by IMC and covering all
the issues concerned with the strengthening of NHAI.
26. The Committee adopted the Clause of the Bill without any amendments.
27. The enacting formula and the title are adopted with consequential changes.
28. The Committee recommends that the Bill may be passed after incorporating the
suggestions made by it.

OBSERV ATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS — AT A GLANCE
The Committee is of the view that this Bill appears to be a piece-meal effort on the
part of the Government that does not really address the basic issues highlighted in the
decision of the Committee on Infrastructure (COI) particularly those relating to greater
autonomy and delegation of more powers to NHAI for approval of individual projects. The
Committee feels that the Bill has been used as a contingent legislative tool. The
Government should avoid such attempt so that the dignity and importance of the Parliament
is maintained. The Committee appreciates the Government's attempt for strengthening the
NHAI by adding professionals of repute in the fields of financial management and
transportation planning, it, however, feels that merely by adding numbers in the Board will
not yield the desired results as expected in the new vision statement of NHAI. The
Committee is of the opinion that having road projects worth Rs.2,20,000 crore, NHAI would
certainly require much more than that, such as delegation of more powers to NHAI for

The IMC also recommended that the age limit may also be relaxed upto 62 years in case it
is necessary to provide the minimum tenure of three years. The Committee expresses its

longstanding effect on the functioning of NHAI in this amendment. (Para 24)
The Committee finds discrepancy in this amendment on the inclusion of additional
part-time members. The Statement of Objects and Reasons of the Amendment Bill states
that in order to increase the efficiency, the number of part-time members of the Board has
been increased from four to six but the formulation of the Bill in Clause 2 reads ‘not more

four to six. Section 8 of the original Act and Section 3 of the present Bill are not in

take any decisions. This might create confusion which needs to be looked into for removing
possible ambiguity. The Committee therefore, urges upon Government to carefully consider
all the points mentioned above and recommends that the Government should come up with
a comprehensive legislation incorporating all the suggestions made by IMC and covering all
the issues concerned with the strengthening of NHAI. (Para 25)
The Committee adopted the Clause of the Bill without any amendments.
(Para 26)
The enacting formula and the title are adopted with consequential changes.
(Para 27)
The Committee recommends that the Bill may be passed after incorporating the
suggestions made by it. (Para 28)

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS
Section 3 of the National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988
provides for constitution of the National Highways Authority of India. As
per sub-section (3) of the said section, the authority shall consist of
(i) a Chairman; (ii) not more than five full-time members; and (iii) not
more than four part-time members. Keeping in view the vastly increased
mandate for National Highways Authority of India and also the greatly
enhanced participation envisaged for the private sector, it is proposed to
amend sub-section ( 3) of section 3 to increase the strength of full-time
members from five to six and part-time members from four to six to
allow induction of professionals of repute in the fields of financial
management, transportation planning and other relevant areas. Induction of
outside professionals will enhance the capacity of the Authority to take
strategic decisions, widen its perspective, bring in the best management
practices, and assist in achieving the goal of higher private participation.
2. The Bill seeks to achieve the above objects.

Sub-section ( 3) of section 3 of the National Highways Authority of

seeks to amend sub-section ( 3) of section 3 of the said Act to provide for
not more than six full-time Members and not more than six, but at the
least four, part-time Members.

of India (NHAI).

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport,
Tourism and Culture, having been authorised by the Committee, do hereby present on its behalf
this One Hundred Forty-ninth Report on ‘Development of Tourism Infrastructure and Amenities for
the Commonwealth Games 2010’,
2. Delhi is hosting 2010 Commonwealth Games from 3rd October, to 14th October, 2010. It
is expected to attract one lakh foreign tourists to Delhi during this period. As the Commonwealth
Games is expected to have large scale impact on India's tourism Sector, the Committee decided
to take stock of the preparedness and efforts of the Government and various stakeholders for
providing the tourists all the facilities including infrastructure development, transport infrastructure
and connectivity, conservation and preservation of monument, hotel accommodation and human
resource development etc. for making the event successful.
3. The Committee in its meeting held on 12th and 27th November, 2008 and 19th January, 2009
discussed the subject with the representatives of Union Ministries of Tourism, Culture and Urban
Development; Archaeological Survey of India, Indian Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC);
Government of Delhi, INTACH, the recognized Tour, Travel and Hoteliers Associations namely
Hotel Association of India, Travel Agents Association of India, Indian Tourist Transporters
Association, Tourist Guides Federation of India, Adventure Tour Operators Association of India and
Indian Association of Tour Operators and Federation of Hotels Restaurants Association of India
with a view to ascertaining their views/suggestions on the subject and to know the details of the
preparation and progress of works of tourism infrastructure projects for the Commonwealth
Games, 2010. In this context, the Committee visited the world heritage sites maintained by ASI
namely the Qutab Minar and Humanyu Tomb on 6.1.2009 to assess the state of affairs of these
monuments.
4. The Committee during its study visit to Udaipur, Jaipur and Agra from 4th to 8th February, 2009
discussed the subject with the representatives of Union Ministry of Civil Aviation, Tourism and
Culture, Archaeological Survey of India, Airports Authority of India (AAI), National Aviation
Company of India Limited (NACIL), Government of Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Haryana. During
the visit, the Committee selected four major areas for discussions: schemes/efforts made for
developing tourism infrastructure and amenities for the tourists during Commonwealth Games, 2010
per se ; availability of hotel accommodation; increasing air connectivity and expansion/modernization
of airports and; protection and preservation of ancient monuments and world heritage sites in the
States of Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Haryana.
5. The Committee expresses its gratitude to the officers and representatives of the Ministries
of Tourism, Culture, Urban Development, Civil Aviation, Archaeological Survey of India, India
Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC); Airports Authority of India (AAI); National Aviation
Company of India Limited (NACIL), Governments of Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Haryana;
INTACH and recognized Tour, Travel and Hoteliers Associations namely Hotel Association of India,
Travel Agents Association of India, Indian Tourist Transporters Association, Tourist Guides
Federation of India, Adventure Tour Operators Association of India and Indian Association of Tour
Operators and Federation of Hotels Restaurants Association of India for their cooperation in
furnishing the required feedback and information in connection with the examination of the subject

and also for making valuable suggestions for improving the tourism infrastructure for the
Commonwealth Games.
4. The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on the
19th February, 2009.
SITARAM YECHURY
NEW D ELHI; Chairman,
February 19, 2009 Department-related Parliamentary Standing
Magha 30, 1930  (Saka) Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture.

1
REPORT
INTRODUCTION
India has always been an attractive tourist destination from far and wide since ages.
Importance of tourism as an instrument of economic development and employment generation has
been well recognized all over the world. Tourism plays an important and effective role in achieving
the growth with equity. During the last few years, tourism has been experiencing substantial
growth in terms of international tourist arrivals and tourism earnings. World tourism accelerated in
2007 posting a higher growth rate (6.6%) as compared to the previous year’s growth rate (5.5%).
The growth of tourism measured in terms of Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTAs) and Foreign
Exchange Earnings (FEE) in India during 2007 were higher than those in the World and Asia and
Pacific. With the FTAs of 5.08 million and FEE of US$ 10.73 billion in 2007, India
achieved growth rate of 14.3% in FTAs and 24.3% in FEE in 2007. FTAs in India during January
- October, 2008 were 4.32 million, with a growth of 9.4% as compared to FTAs of 3.95 million
during January - October, 2007. FEE during January - October, 2008 were US$ 9.70 billion as
compared to US$ 8.29 billion during January - October, 2007, registering a growth of 16.9%. The
key factors driving the tourism boom include India’s sustained economic growth, strong foreign
direct investment inflows, increased air network, the availability of affordable air travel, a strong
domestic market, aggressive marketing campaigns, etc.
2. Delhi is hosting 2010 Commonwealth Games and like all events big or small, this mega
event too is expected to have significant impact on India’s economy. Around one lakh foreign
visitors are estimated to visit Delhi during the Games period. For creating various infrastructural
facilities for those tourists, a number of projects have been undertaken. In view of little time left,
the Committee decided to take stock of the preparedness of the Government and various other
agencies that are responsible for providing tourists all the facilities mainly relating to such areas
as safety and security, transport, air connectivity, hotel accommodation including conservation and
preservation of our ancient monuments, human resource development, etc. for making this event
successful.
3. The Committee discussed various aspects relating to development of tourism infrastructure
and other amenities for tourists during the Commonwealth Games, 2010’ with different
stakeholders in this regard. Apart from the representatives of Union Ministries of Tourism, Culture
and Urban Development, Archaeological Survey of India, Indian Tourism Development Corporation
(ITDC); Government of Delhi, it also interacted with representatives of INTACH, the recognized
Tour, Travel and Hoteliers Associations, namely, Hotel Association of India, Travel Agents
Association of India, Indian Tourist Transporters Association, Tourist Guides Federation of India,
Adventure Tour Operators Association of India, Indian Association of Tour Operators and
Federation of Hotels Restaurants Association of India. The Committee noted their views/suggestions
on different aspects of the subject and received non-official feedback from them on the preparation
and progress of tourism infrastructure projects for the Commonwealth Games, 2010.
4. The Committee notes that during the Commonwealth Games a large number of
tourists are expected into India besides the participants. The Committee feels that the
Commonwealth Games would provide us good opportunity to showcase our rich cultural
heritage and achievements of the contemporary India to the International community, that
would act as catalyst for development of infrastructure and capacity-building. The success
of Commonwealth Games will not only position India as a multifaceted destination but will
bring economic returns through business and tourism. The Committee, therefore, calls upon

2
the Government and all the stakeholders to make concerted efforts for creating best of the
facilities and infrastructure, renovation and better up-keep of our tourism and ancient sites,
improving road and air connectivity and safety and security of the tourist and providing
adequate accommodation at reasonable prices. The Committee also recommends that Delhi
being the Centre of important literary and cultural activities, should refurbish its Libraries,
Museums, Art Galleries, H aats, etc., for showcasing its rich and varied cultural and
intellectual heritage.
TOURIST INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT
5. With the Commonwealth Games 2010 drawing closer, the host city Delhi is gearing itself
up for the mega event. The Committee was informed that various plans were underway for
providing/creating adequate facilities for the tourists expected during the Commonwealth Games.
The city was set to undergo a major facelift while building adequate and modem infrastructure
by 2010. The tourist infrastructure development involved the upgradation as well as the growth of
hotel accommodation in Delhi and the NCR Region. For example, under the Central
Financial Assistance (CFA) Scheme, the Ministry of Tourism has sanctioned projects amounting
Rs.6123.36 lakh in Delhi under the Tenth Plan. Further, under the Eleventh Plan, projects
amounting to Rs.1780.68 Lakh have also been sanctioned during the year so far. During the
year 2008-09, an outlay of Rs.552 crore had been sanctioned to the Ministry of Tourism for
infrastructure development projects for all the States and Union territories of the country. Out of
the sanctioned amount, the Ministry has spent only 63 per cent of the budgeted outlay till
November 2008. The projects sanctioned for Delhi include:
(a) Development works at the Red Fort;
(b) Development of the Old Fort;
(c) Illumination of Humayuns Tomb;
(d) Illumination of Qutab Minar;
(e) Development of Dilli Haat at Pitampura;
(f) Special repairs and Reconditioning of Colonial Building at Red Fort etc.
6. Besides, the Ministry of Tourism has sanctioned the tourism projects and released funds
under CFA for holistic development of golden triangle circuit. The following tables shows the

7. On being enquired about State-wise allocation of funds for different projects, the Ministry
informed that there was no State-wise allocation; the layout was for the infrastructure sector for
whole of the country. There is a different Head under which, assistance is given by the Ministry
of Tourism as and when a proposal came. It was also stated that there was no shortage of funds
at present and there was no proposal pending from any State/UTs. The representative of the
Ministry assured the Committee that they could spare Rs.l00 crore or more depending upon the
proposals of the Delhi Government under infrastructure upgradation of tourism destination schemes
for infrastructure development for the Commonwealth Games.
8. The Committee notes that there are adequate funds available with the Ministry of
Tourism under infrastructure upgradation of tourism destination schemes. However, the
Committee notes with concern that no proposals from the Delhi Government for
development of infrastructure and capacity building including creation and renovation of
hospitality facilities, modernization of tourism sites, etc., was submitted/pending with the
Ministry of Tourism till November, 2008. The Committee feels that since the Commonwealth

5
Games are drawing closer, so many projects have yet to be initiated, let alone completed.
In such a situation, absence of any proposal from the NCT of Delhi surprises the
Committee. The Committee therefore, recommends the Ministry of Tourism to impress
upon the Government of Delhi and also the Government of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and
Rajasthan for submitting projects proposals for developing tourism infrastructure including
hotel accommodation for the Games and release the funds at the earliest for implementing
the development works on time.
9. In view of the fact that most of the tourists coming to Delhi shall also visit important
towns in Rajasthan and Agra, the Committee decided to see for itself the arrangements and
amenities at these places. The Committee, therefore, visited Udaipur, Jaipur and Agra from 4th to
8th February, 2009 alongwith the representatives of Union Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Civil
Aviation and ASI. Discussion was held with the officials of Government of Rajasthan, Uttar
Pradesh and Haryana with a view to ascertaining their views/suggestions on the issue of
connectivity and amenities to tourists during the CWG-2010.
10. During the discussion the Principal Secretary, Tourism, Government of Rajasthan informed
the Committee that the Rajasthan Government was making efforts for promoting tourism in the
State. It was closely associating the private sector also for launching attractive packages during the
Games. The State Government had already launched Tourism Policy, Golf Tourism, Resort
Tourism, Spa Tourism etc. to tap the tourist. During 2007-08, the Rajasthan received 25920529
domestic and 1401042 international tourists. The Principal Secretary further emphasized that hotels
which were under construction, may be provided financial assistance. As regards the financial
assistance from the Ministry of Tourism, it was informed that all the projects including Nahargarh
Fort and Amer Fort pending for Central Finance Assistance (CFA) have been cleared and as of date
no project in Rajasthan was pending for want of CFA.
11. About the connectivity issue, the Principal Secretary informed the Committee that with the
commissioning of new international airport terminal in Jaipur, there is a need to introduce more
international flights. There is also a need for air connectivity to Ajmer and Kota. The Rajasthan
Government was willing to provide land free-of-cost for development of airport infrastructure at
these places. The Principal Secretary demanded that the speed of Shatabdi train from New Delhi
to Jaipur, that takes five hours, may suitably be increased to reduce the travel time. The route also
demands double line for smooth passage of trains, he said.
12. As regards the security and safety of the tourists in Rajasthan, the Principal Secretary
replied that the state Government was organizing workshops for police personnel and the hotel
guards will be trained by the police personnel. Tourist police was also available throughout
Rajasthan to help tourists in a better way.
13. The Committee notes that the Government of Rajasthan is utilizing the opportunity
for promotion of tourism and introducing various packages for the guests/tourists visiting
Rajasthan during the games. The Committee recommends the Ministry of Tourism to
provide adequate funds to the Government of Rajasthan for promotion of various tourism
products in the State. It also recommends that the tax incentives/benefits as provided to the
hotels in the National Capital Region (NCR) of Delhi may suitably be extended to the hotels
in Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, so as to remove the imbalance
in the demand and supply of hotel rooms’ inventory. The Committee also recommends that
the Government of Rajasthan should make concerted efforts and coordinate with the
Ministry of Tourism (for promotional support), Ministry of Civil Aviation (for introduction
of more international flights to and from Jaipur and development of Airports and air
connectivity from Ajmer and Kota) and Ministry of Railways (for increasing the speed of the
trains and double lining of rail line between Delhi and Jaipur). The State Government should

6
also impress upon the hotels in the State to take adequate security measures such as
installing x-ray machines for screening of baggage which is a must in the present scenario.
14. While going around the Amber Fort, the Committee saw preparation for some film shooting
by erecting big sets. The Committee was assured that it was not going to cause any damage to
the monuments. The Committee’s apprehension came true just few days after when it was reported
that a part of wall inside the monuments came crashing down. The Committee recommends that
while allowing any activity including commercial in the monuments, which should
necessarily be remain very exceptional, the Governments must ensure that safety, security,
originality and cleanliness of the monuments is not impaired upon and no damages of any
kind is caused.
15. The Committee notes that the conservation work is being carried out in Amber Fort
by Amer Development Authority. The Committee however, desires that the concerned
agencies be cautioned not to destroy/alter the originality while making effort to renovate
the monuments. The Committee also notes with concern that the condition of monuments
like Jantar Mantar and Albert Hall is not upto the mark and desires that Amer
Development Authority should provide funds for their maintenance an upkeep.
16. The Secretary (Tourism), Government of Uttar Pradesh during the deliberations with the
Committee on the 8th February, 2009 in Agra stated that the State Government was already
engaged in preparation for the games and several new hotels were coming up. But in view of the
global meltdown, travel and tourism industry requires financial incentives. Further access roads to
Taj Mahal, Taj Express way right from Noida, Greater Noida was already under construction and
will be completed by the Commonwealth Games and this will considerably reduce the travel time
between Delhi and Agra. When the Committee enquired about the condition of roads inside the Agra
city, the Secretary informed that the Government of U.P. was already seized with the matter and
there was a proposal for construction of an under pass from Prithvi Nath to Shahganj and for
which an MoU had been signed with the Ministry of Railways. However, the approval from the
Ministry of Defence was awaited, he informed.
17. As regards the induction and training of tourist guides, it was informed that they were
inducted on demand and supply basis under the ASI Acts and are trained by the Ministry of
Tourism. Ministry of Tourism had issued guidelines for Regional Level guides, State Level guides
and Local guides. A number of court cases were pending filed by the guides/unauthorized guides.
The State Government emphasized the need for conducting training for these guides keeping
international travelers in mind. As per the figures available during 2007, around 37.5 lakh tourists
visited Agra including 7.5 lakh foreign tourists and 30 lakh domestic travelers. The State
Government demanded that there should be more state level and local level guides.
18. The Committee notes that a large number of persons were likely to stay in the
vicinity of Delhi during the games and the city of Taj Mahal is gearing up to meet the
expected tourists rush during the CWG 2010. The Committee also notes that the
Government of Uttar Pradesh is assessing and preparing the infrastructural needs of the
city to accommodate around a million tourists likely to visit the Taj Mahal during the
Games. The Committee feels that there is a need for expansion of hotels as more rooms
would be required to accommodate the tourist and recommends that the Government should
come up with some concessional/incentive packages to motivate the hoteliers to add rooms
to their existing structures. The Committee recommends that the guidelines for funding
existing hotels structures needs to be looked into and the Government should amend the
guidelines to provide financial assistance to the hotels which are under construction. The
State Governments of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan should be provided central
grants in order to meet the shortfall in hotel accommodation.

7
19. The Committee notes the problems like long and arduous train/road journey from
New Delhi to Agra, lack of tourist buses attached to the railway stations in Agra and Delhi,
inadequate access from Agra Cantt. Railway station to Taj Mahal and Sikandara, poor
condition of the battery operated vehicles, lack of adequate parking, cafeteria, security
check, long queues for tickets, drinking water, toilets, luggage room, facilitation centers,
etc. The Committee feels that these are not big issues and can be resolved by way of better
coordination among different agencies especially the Ministry of Defence for construction of
underpass in Shahganj area for proper road connectivity to Taj Mahal. The Committee,
therefore, recommends the Government to find immediate solutions to these problems and
introduce easy ticketing procedures like prior ticketing, e-ticketing, composite tickets,
flexible tickets, group tickets, tatkal system, transit passes system, etc. for gaining entry
to Taj Mahal, besides restructuring and strengthening of the security. The drinking water,
toilet facilities and facilitation centers should be provided outside the Taj Mahal to facilitate
the tourists. The problems of guides should be resolved by the Ministry of Tourism, Culture
and Government of Uttar Pradesh with mutual interaction.
20. The Committee notes that the view of Taj from the other side of Yamuna from
Mehtab Bagh may be a thrilling experience for the tourists during full moon night that
creates a view of Taj being black. The Committee recommends that viewing of Taj Mahal
from this side should be promoted and permission for adequate parking and toilet facilities
should be provided there. The Committee desires that in maintaining the monuments,
environmental developments including horticulture works and landscaping, civic amenities
for tourists and display of cultural notice boards and signages should be taken care of. The
Government should make concerted efforts to involve public and corporate sector for the
purpose. The Committee also recommends that a survey should be conducted by the
Government to ascertain the carrying capacity of the monument to protect it from being
damaged by over crowd.
21. The Committee found the practice of night viewing of Taj more restrictive due to
tight security arrangements as well as lack of coordination between U.P. Police and CISF.
The distance between the monument and the tourists is too long to be able to feel the
beauty of the monument. The Committee without compromising the need for security of
Taj, feels that with a proper coordination and communication between the two forces and
with proper training for good behavior with the tourists, efforts can be made to allow the
tourists to see the Taj in night from the floor where the stairs reach the main structure.
It would be a lifetime experience for them.
AUGMENTATION OF HOTEL ACCOMMODATION FOR COMMONWEALTH GAMES-2010
22. The Committee raised the question of availability of accommodation for the tourists during
the period of the Games and the details of incentives which have been announced in the Union
Budget for this purpose and their utilization by various agencies. The representative of the Ministry
of Tourism informed the Committee that with a view to encourage the growth of new budget
category hotels, the Finance Ministry had given a five-year tax holiday under Section 80-ID to
2, 3 and 4-star category hotels and convention centers which will be functional between 1.4.07
to 31.3.2010, in NCT of Delhi and the districts of Faridabad, Gurgaon, Gautam Buddh Nagar
(NOIDA) and Ghaziabad. In order to ensure that private sector takes benefits of incentives
proposed by the Government, the DDA have auctioned 33 hotel sites with a provision of 6000 Plus
rooms. DDA and the Ministry of Urban Development have been actively monitoring, from time to
time, the process to complete formalities regarding construction, approval and subsequent progress.
23. The Committee was informed that against about 30,000  rooms needed during the Game
period located in and around Delhi, only 1,924 rooms came under the ‘definite’ category; 2,015

8
rooms were under the ‘likely’ category; and the remaining 1,990 rooms come under the ‘doubtful’
category. However, this position was expected to undergo a change depending upon the future
progress of work. Based on the latest site inspection, it is expected that a large number of cases
under ‘likely’ category may become ‘definite’ category. In addition to what DDA was facilitating,
there were, some other hotel proposals which were being pursued with the concerned agencies.
24. The Ministry of Tourism submitted that as far as motels are concerned, as per the
provisions of Master Plan Delhi 2021, no fresh motels will be permitted. As per the information
available, a total of 104 motels had been sanctioned. About twelve motels were functioning, as
reported by the MCD. Conversion of motels into hotels goes against the very spirit of town and
city planning and more than a planning activity, it becomes a regularization exercise. Taking the
overall scenario into account, it is felt that since the zonal-development plans, which is the next
layout for the Master Plan, are under preparation, the actual number of motels that will be falling
in the commercial zone will be reflected in these plans and as such, such motels falling in the
commercial and permissible use zones may become eligible for construction of hotels.
25. About the development plan of DDA, the Ministry informed that another task mandated to
the DDA is to construct the Games Village at East Delhi, competition and training venues at Siri
Fort Complex, Yamuna Sports Complex and Saket Sports Complex. The Games Village is planned
to provide residential accommodation to 8,000 athletes and team officials. It also consists of
training areas for athletics, swimming pools, indoor halls, Village operation and other support areas.
With a view to supplementing the efforts to have more accommodation for the visitors during the
Games, DDA has initiated the process of identifying about 2,000 flats which will generate around
5,500 rooms in centrally located areas, which can be made available for augmenting
accommodation during the Games. The shortfall in hotel rooms, which were mandated to be
created on the hotel sites auctioned by the DDA, to a great extent is expected to be compensated
by providing these accommodations.
26. During the course of the discussion, the Hoteliers Associations submitted before the
Committee that with the current economic meltdown and terror attack on Mumbai had adversely
impacted the India’s tourism scenario. This had caused massive cancellation of hotel booking
throughout the country resulting in revenue losses to the tune of around Rs. 9731 crore. They
desired that the tourism may be declared as industry and given infrastructure status for the hotels
sector. This would provide added impetus to the development of tourism greatly. The
representatives of the Hotel Association of India and Federation of Hotels and Restaurants
Association of India presented the key issues highlighting the long and short terms challenges
impeding the growth of tourism infrastructure and amenities in the country and NCR. Some of
these are: absence of an updated Master Plan for tourism, high cost of land, creation of land banks
on lines of SEZ, FAR, tough lending norms by Indian banks, multiplicity of taxes, local Government
being unaware of the potential, Luxury tax computed on published rates in many States, lack of
enough fiscal incentives for entrepreneurs to invest in this capital intensive industry, Opaque
licensing process causing for delay in project execution, Archaic laws governing the operations of
Hotels, outdated Hotel Classification/rating system, acute lack of value-for-money proposition and
poor tourist infrastructure and ground support. They desired that the same may be addressed at
the highest level to bring tourism in the main stream of the national economy.
27. The Committee notes that the hotel accommodation is the key component of the
tourism infrastructure needed for the CWG-20l0. At present there is huge gap demand and
supply of the hotel rooms in India in general and Delhi in particular. The Committee finds
that the hotel development in India is ailing with many impediments such as regulatory,
financing, clearances, operations etc. The Committee is perturbed to note that the
countdown to CWG has begun but there seems inadequate infrastructure in all sectors such

9
as road, airport, accommodation, surface transport, entertainment, basic amenities, parking,
information centers, security, stadia and supply of powers. The Committee feels that the
problems brought out by the Hotel Association of India and Federation of Hotels and
Restaurants Association of India before the Committee are justified and needs serious
attention of Governments. The Committee therefore, recommends the Government to
address the key issues and challenges faced by the hotel sector in India including NCR for
development of tourism infrastructure and amenities for the CWG-2010.
28. The Committee notes that the Government has extended tax holiday scheme for
construction of budget hotels in NCT of Delhi and the districts of Faridabad, Gurgaon,
Gautam Buddh Nagar (NOIDA) and Ghaziabad. It seems to the Committee that the financial
incentives and tax holidays announced by the Government have not been used optimally by
the private parties for construction of the new hotels in Delhi and adjoining areas. The
Committee recommends the Government to pursue the State Governments of Haryana and
Uttar Pradesh and Delhi and various land owning agencies, DDA/Ministry of Urban
Development to allocate land on joint venture/revenue sharing basis and provide tax
incentives/benefits and tax holidays with single window clearances for the hotel projects to
these private players in State of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajashthan and Madhya Pradesh
who are interested in setting up of new hotels to facilitate the growth of the accommodation
sector to tourist during the period of the Games. The Committee also recommends that
since the CWG are almost the round the corner, the Government may, if necessary, further
liberalize the incentive schemes to attract investment in the hotel projects.
29. The Committee has serious doubts about the capability of the DDA for expediting the
issue of identification and allotment of hotel sites for construction of budget hotels for the
Games. The Committee notes with concerns that the pace of creation of additional hotel
accommodation at 39 hotel sites auctioned by DDA since January 2006 is lagging behind
schedule, though the Committee has been assured by the Ministry of Urban Development
that completion of these sites would generate 6019 rooms and the DDA and the Ministry
have been actively monitoring from time to time the process to complete the formalities
and progress of work. The Committee does not agree with the contention of the Ministry
of Urban Development as the recent assessment reveals that only 1924 rooms will be
available under the definite category, 2015 rooms under the likely category and the
remaining 1990 rooms under the doubtful category. This way only fewer rooms will be
available as per the assessment. The Committee therefore, recommends the Government to
once again ascertain the position with the concerned agencies and come out with more
realistic assessment in this regard. A concrete plan for facilitating the hotel proposals
including the alternative proposal for conversion of motels into hotels and identification of
vacant DDA flats to offset the deficit of hotel room before the commencement of the Games
should be considered. The Committee hopes that the Government will take the steps to
address the problem of shortage of rooms and complete the exercise for developing the
accommodation to the visitors well in time.
30. The Committee has been informed by the Ministry of Tourism that a ‘Task Force’ has been
constituted in the Ministry of Tourism for monitoring the progress of the various agencies for
creation of additional hotel accommodation in NCT of Delhi. These agencies include the
Governments of Uttar Pradesh and Haryana, the Ministries of Railways, Urban Development and
Civil Aviation, the Delhi Development Authority (DDA), Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC),
Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) etc. Regular meetings are held to review the progress
and so far, 18 meetings of the Task Force have been held since last two years. The Hon’ble
Minister of Tourism and Culture personally met the Hon’ble Minister of Urban Development on
4.1.2007 for expediting issues relating to DDA and MoUD. The Ministry of Urban Development

10
was requested to identify 75 hotel sites for construction of budget hotels. Secretary, Tourism met
Secretary (UD) on 21.11.07 to expedite the allotment of hotel sites for the Games. The issue of
infrastructure development and augmentation of accommodation has been also taken up in the
Meetings of the Group of Ministers (GOMs). Since the year 2004, the meetings of the GOM have
been held 14 times, the last one having being held on 9.4.08. The Committee of Secretaries (COS)
discussed the issue of infrastructure development and the augmentation of hotel accommodation
during its various meetings in the last three years. In order to assess the ground reality and exact
position, meetings were also held with the entrepreneurs of hotel projects. The meeting with
entrepreneurs of DDA projects was held on 14.5.2008 and the meeting for review of projects in
Haryana was held on 18.5.2008. All the land owning agencies have also been advised to regularly
document the project by taking periodical photographs during the review. The DDA is also holding
regular meetings with the entrepreneurs for close monitoring of the projects and also to facilitate
various clearances. Meetings to review and monitor the arrangements for the Commonwealth
Games-2010 are also being conducted regularly by Lt. Governor, Delhi, Chief Minister of Delhi and
Minister of State (Sports).
31. During the course of the oral evidence, the Secretary, Ministry of Tourism deposed before
the Committee that the Ministry of Tourism monitors and reviews all the hotel projects for the
Commonwealth Games by holding regular meetings of the Task Force. Nineteen such meetings
have been held. The Commonwealth Games projects and issues are also being reviewed regularly
by the Group of Ministers, in the Committee of Secretaries, headed by the Cabinet Secretary and
also by the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi. All efforts are being made to facilitate the promoters of
hotel projects to expedite the clearances and permissions. Attempts are being made to have a single
window clearance because various clearances are required by the hoteliers. The Ministry of
Tourism is also exploring all the possibilities for augmenting additional accommodation. Attempts
are being made, apart form the DDA, with the Ministry of Railways, Ministry of Civil Aviation, the
State Governments of Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, DMRC, etc., in this regard.
32 The Ministry of Tourism has been requesting the Land Owning Agencies to create land
banks for hotels and facilitate the investment in the ‘Hotel Sector’ through friendly policies viz.

facilitating the creation of additional rooms by way of the hotel sites auctioned by the Delhi

Apart from this, several other measures have been undertaken by the GNCTD to upgrade the city

Commonwealth Games 2010. Secretary (Tourism) has been in constant touch with Secretary (UD)
for allotment of hotel sites and other issues since 2005. The Minister, Tourism and Culture had
requested MoUD the following:
(a) To identify 75 hotel sites for construction of budget hotels with a total room capacity

(b) In the meeting of the CoS, held on 18.10.07, nine to ten additional sites for budget
hotels were to be identified and the possibility be explored to give it on a long lease
and revenue sharing basis.
(c) It was also proposed that area within 4 kms around International airport in Delhi be

(d) DDA/MoUD was also requested to consider extending additional FAR/FSI for existing

(e) Permission to allow hotels in commercial areas.
(f) MoT had also requested for the re-classification of Farm land on payment of

(g) Decision on conversion of motels into hotels was also proposed.
33. The Ministry of Tourism further informed that the L&DO had identified 3 sites in Delhi.

37. The Government of Haryana was asked to identify hotel sites for 10,000 hotel rooms in the
