project is scheduled to be completed by June, 2010.  The Committee recommends that the 
Ministry should coordinate with the Ministry of Culture for timely completion of its project.

(v) Skill testing and certification of the existing  service providers.

of an FCI. To begin with, each IHM will run craft c ourses in five streams and degree course (B.Sc. in 
Hospitality and Hotel Administration). 
61.  In addition to the above, during 2009-10, the Ministry has extended Central Financial

assistance will be available to all. The assistance  will be utilized for creation of infrastructure 
necessary for the conduct of courses/trainings. 
63.  The Committee is not satisfied with the efforts mad e by the Ministry regarding human 
resource development. The Government has not made s ufficient plan outlay under the head 
‘assistance for manpower training’. In the year 200 9-10, an amount of Rs. 100.70 crore was 
allocated. For the 2010-11 there is negligible increase in the plan outlay i.e. Rs. 102.50 crore. The 
Committee is constrained to note that up to Februar y 2010, ones 64% of plan outlay is likely to 
be utilized. Government have plans to set up new IHM in various parts of the country. However, 
the Committee has not been informed whether any target has been fixed for completion of these 
institutes. The Committee feels that the huge shortage of about 1.9 lakhs can not be met only by 
the Government’s initiatives alone. The Committee r ecommends that the universities under the 
UGC and the technical institutions under AICTE may be encouraged to open courses on 
hospitality industry and necessary financial assist ance for infrastructural and other required 
facilities may be extended by the Ministry of Touri sm. They should be come out with ambitious 
courses in coordination with the hospitality indust ry which will provide employability to those 
opting for the courses in those universities and te chnical institutions. External support may be 
extended by the Ministry of Tourism to these agenci es as they have the men and material for 
conducting quality courses.

(IITTM), Gwalior. There is no scheme/proposal at pr esent to set up Training Institutes for guides.

scrutinizing the applications received for part-tim e Foreign Language Linguist Guides Training 

Programme has commenced at IITTM, Gwalior and train ing for the same is likely to commence

65.  The Committee is concerned that with a huge manpowe r and resources within the 
country, it seems the will to facilitate tourist visiting India is lacking on the part of Government. 
Tourism Sector cannot grow without the support of g uides. Often foreign visitors complain of 
lack of guides as they are made to suffer from the hands of touts. With thousands of historical 
places and monuments all over the country, there is  need to have interpretation centres from 
where tourists can obtain all information regarding a particular site.

assistance to those institutions and universities f or starting foreign language courses/imparting

85.  The Ministry has informed that in order to ens ure safety and security of tourists, Ministry of 
Tourism has advised all the State Governments/Union  Territory Administrations to deploy Tourist 
Police in the States/Union Territories. Ministry of  Tourism in consultation with Ministry of Home 
Affairs, Ministry of Defence and Directorate Genera l of Resettlements has framed guidelines for 
formation of Tourist Security Organization (s) comp rising Ex-Servicemen, for the safety and security 
of the tourists. The guidelines have been sent alon g with the letter dated 02 
nd  May, 2008 of Hon’ble 
Minister to the State Governments / Union Territory Administrations. 
86.  Further, a detailed note along with the guidel ines for setting up of Tourist Facilitation and 
Security Organization comprising primarily of Ex-Se rvicemen in States/Union Territories for 
providing the safety and security to the tourists, under CFA Scheme was forwarded to the Planning 
Commission for in-principle approval. The matter ha s been taken up with the Deputy Chairman, 
Planning Commission vide  letter of Hon’ble Minister (Tourism and Housing an d Urban Poverty 
Alleviation) dated 02nd January, 2010. 
87.  The guidelines stipulate that the tourist poli ce be constituted from a pool of ex-servicemen 
maintained by the Director General of Resettlement. It will be a three-tier structure-state level, district 
level and destination level-which will be supervised by a Joint Committee comprising the State Home 
Secretary and the Tourism Secretary. The Chief Tour ist Warden will be a retired commissioned 
officer while the District Tourist Warden may be a retired Junior Commissioned Officer. The 
destination tourist warden will be preferably a sub eadar or equivalent the guideline state while 
maintaining that a working knowledge in spoken Engl ish is a prerequisite. The Governments of 
Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Goa, Kerala, Maharashtra , Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Orissa, Uttar 
Pradesh, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Jammu an d Kashmir are reported to have deployed 
Tourists Police, in one form or the other.

be given paramount importance to ensure that India is recognized as popular tourist 
destination. Many of the States have not constitute d the tourism police and wherever they are 
constituted it is just tokenism. The Committee, the refore recommends that all the State 
Governments may be pursued to create effective police mechanism to protect the tourists.

96.  As per a study on the impact of tourism promot ion measure on the habitat of wildlife in Corbett 
National Park it was found out that there is a grow ing trend towards travel to eco-tourism destinations 
like National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries. The Ministry of Tourism conducted a survey through the 
students of the Institute of Hotel Management, Pusa , New Delhi to consider the ground factors like 
anti environmental activities that hampers the peac eful living of the wild life. The survey was 
conducted from December 16, 2009 to December 22, 20 09 and the outcome had very revealing 
information about the misuse of opportunities in th e guise of tourism by the hoteliers and resort 
operators.

surveys at Kaziranga National Park. The Ministry of Tourism has informed that they held a meeting to 
plan a National Workshop for Sustainable Tourism Criteria for India to discuss the modalities with the 
various stakeholders of the Tourism industry.

interfere with the ecosystem. The Committee also recommends that strict action should be taken 
against all who are violating the prescribed norms and setting hotels etc. in the restricted area, 
and ecologically sensitive forest areas.

103.  The Committee had observed that the present form in  which budget related data is given 
to the Committee while examining Demands for Grants of the Ministry does not provide a clear 
picture about actual performance/achievements during a particular year.  
104.  Domestic tourism is getting comparatively lesser importance by the Ministry, which leaves 
the most local tourism potential unexploited. More infrastructure development is needed, 
keeping in view the domestic tourists potential. The target set for each and every projects need a 

review and a more scientific approach should be ado pted. Even small countries are able to 
achieve their targets within a stipulated time, it is a matter of concern that India is lagging 
behind its project implementation ultimately resulting cost escalations and revenue losses.  
105.  The Committee also pointed out that travel by train  is an integral part of the domestic 
tourism. Moreover, many exclusive tourist trains have started plying exclusively for the tourists. 
The Committee recommends that Ministry of Tourism s hould coordinate with the Railway 
authorities in order to provide safe, secure and enjoyable to the tourists.  
106.  The Committee notes that connectivity to tourist de stination is the pivotal aspect of the 
development of tourism. Many of the areas which have huge tourism potential are left out by the 
Ministry of Civil Aviation, Ministry of Railways and Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

helicopter services are started in these areas lot of tourists will be attracted to these areas and it  
will be a big boost for tourism in these two places . The Committee recommends that the 
Ministry of Tourism may take up with the Ministry o f Civil Aviation and Airport Authority of 
India to construct airstrips in Thekkady and Bekal Fort in Kerala.  
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS –– AT A GLANCE  
  The Committee observes that the tourism resources  of India have the potential to generate 
significantly higher levels of demand from the dome stic and international markets, and if 
exploited in a sustainable manner, it can prove to be an engine of growth for the economy. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Governmen t should provide more funds for 
promoting tourism and tapping the vast and varied potential - modern and ancient. (Para 4)  
BUDGETARV ALLOCATIONS AND ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2010-11 
  The Committee notes that during the year 2009-10,  the allocation was reduced to 
Rs.950.00 crore at RE stage, out of which, an amoun t of Rs.776.16 crore is likely to be utilized 
till Feb. 2010. Thus, 19% of allocation is likely t o be utilized in just one month. The Committee 
does not approve the practice of last minute spendi ng at the fag end of the financial year. The 
Committee in its earlier Reports, has conveyed this  feeling to the Ministries concerned. The 
Ministry should follow the existing norms strictly to ensure that the funds are utilized, as far as 
possible, evenly throughout the year. The Committee also does not find any reason for reducing 
the allocation at RE stage. Tourism is the largest service industry with a contribution of 6.23 % 
of the GDP and 8.78% of the total employment in Ind ia. Since Tourism projects are 
implemented by the States, there is need to sensitize them to ensure optimum utilization of funds 
and issuing user utilization certificates on time. The Ministry should make concerted efforts and 
evolve a coordination mechanism with the States.    
TOURIST INFRASTRUCTURE 
  The Committee, however, finds that in the case of  utilization of fund for 
product/infrastructure development for circuit duri ng 2007-08, 2008-09 and 2009-10, 
expenditure has been more than what was allocated i n the budget. The Committee recommends 
that if the schemes are chalked out well in time by the Ministry, they can approach the Planning 
Commission /Ministry of Finance for allocation of more funds at BE stage itself.             (Para 16)  
  The Committee is of the view that the Ministry sh ould make all out efforts for the 
development of a particular circuit which is approv ed for implementation. Moreover various 
States should coordinate and develop inter-state ci rcuits. Southern and central circuits need to 
be developed with more emphasis on travel connectivity.                                                     (Para 17)  
  The Committee finds no justification for making p rovision of plan outlay in the Budget 
under the Head-Creation of Land Bank for Hotels when the plan allocation remained unutilized 
since the inception of the scheme. The Committee, t herefore, recommended the scheme may be 
reviewed and modified with view to ensure that deve lopment of accommodation for tourists is 
not affected. 
(Para 20)  
  The Committee came to know that ITDC is doing the  illumination work in some of the 
major monuments in Delhi. Further, ITDC also host l ight and sound show in some of the 
monuments which is being appreciated. Particularly Delhi will be hosting XIX Commonwealth 
Games this year the light and Sound show can be use d to attract more tourist and to acquaint 
them with the history as well as majesty of our fam ous monuments. The Committee, therefore, 

recommends that the Ministry should ensure that thi s year sufficient funds are allocated to 
ITDC for this job. (Para 22)  
  The Committee notes the projects and funds sancti oned to various States. However, the 
Committee is not aware of the targets fixed for com pletion of these projects. It has also come to 
the notice of the Committee that in some cases proj ects received from the State Governments 
are not processed/ sanctioned in time which result in delay and non-utilisation of funds. The 
Committee, therefore recommends that the progress o f these projects need to be monitored 
regularly to ensure that there is no delay and cost overrun in the projects. (Para 25)  
  The way-side facilities may appear to be insignif icant things in comparison to other 
tourism infrastructure, these are, however, very important from the tourist’s point of view. The 
Committee desires that this scheme needs to be wide ly publicized and the States be impressed 
upon to take benefit from this. In fact, the Minist ry of Tourism should set target for each State 
and implementation of the scheme should be monitored in a time-bound manner. (Para 27)  
  The Committee, however, recommends that Ministry may consider evolving the approach 
for development of region/State-wise tourism infras tructure development in order to promote 
the domestic tourism more vigorously which has a great potential. The Committee is of the view 
that such approach may generate interest among the local people and Government of the State 
concerned which can ensure their speedy development and timely completion. (Para 29)  
  The Committee is of the view that Ministry of tou rism should concentrate on promoting 
accommodation for the domestic tourists who usually prefer affordable and safe accommodation 
rather than the costly star hotels. The Committee, therefore, recommends that budget hotels 
aimed at the domestic tourists should also be given  priority by the Ministry of Tourism and 
accordingly all the promotional measures and tax be nefits should also to be extended to the 
budget hotels and restaurants also. (Para 30)  
  The Committee notes that huge amount is pending w ith various State Governments and 
they are yet to complete the projects and submit th e utilization certificates. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should pursue with the State Governments to identify 
the reasons for delay of each of the projects and i f it is found that the project is not feasible due 
to one or the other reasons, alternate projects may  be allowed for the States. The Committee 
also recommends that in future projects may be allo wed only after getting all the necessary 
clearance from various agencies. 
  (Para 33)  
  The Committee also pointed out that in many cases  the projects are approved without 
doing adequate home work and later on abandoned mid way, because of functional and 
operational difficulties. The Committee noted that in certain cases even 80 per cent of the total 
sanctioned amount was released to the project, but later on it was abandoned due to unknown 
reasons. This is because of poor planning and imple mentation methodology adopted by the 
ministry while sanctioning the projects. The Committee in this respect is of the view that before 
a project is approved by the ministry, they should ensure the feasibility of the project and get all 
the necessary clearances from other related agencies before releasing the money.            (Para 34)  

  The Committee conveys its displeasure over the wa y the projects are sanctioned and 
implemented by the Ministry where there are lots of  wastages of money and manpower. Land 
related issues and environmental clearances should be dealt with in order to ensure a smooth 
implementation and completion of the projects. (Para 35)  
  The Committee is constrained to say that the work  Ajanta-Ellora Phase-II which was 
started in in 2003-04, is yet to the completed. It appears that the project progress has not been 
monitored properly and expected obstacle in its com pletion could not be identified. Now the 
project is scheduled to be completed by June 2010. The Committee recommends that the 
Ministry should coordinate with the Ministry of Culture for timely completion of its project.  
(Para 37)  
DOMESTIC CAMPAIGN 
  The Committee notes that out of Rs.54 crore appro ved for domestic campaign for the year 
2009-10, only an amount of Rs. 16.11 crore was expected to be utilized till December. It presents 
a very dismal state of affairs. The Committee finds  that the actual utilization, in the domestic 
tourism promotion measures up to the month of Febru ary 2010, is only 30 per cent of the 
budgetary provision during 2009-10 and how the rema ining funds would be utilized within a 
month in a suitable and effective manner, is not kn own. It seems that the Ministry’s main focus 
is on overseas campaigning and has neglected the domestic tourism promotion activities. It must 
be noted that domestic tourism has great importance  as a large number of people are visiting 
places in connection with marriage, pilgrimage and other such occasions where overtly or 
covertly tourism is promoted. The Committee feels that there is need to tap the existing domestic 
market by informing domestic travelers through sust ained campaigning. The Committee 
recommends that the promotion of domestic tourists should be the main agenda of the Ministry 
of Tourism as compared to the domestic tourists, th e number of foreign tourists is very 
miniscule. The State Governments must also be involved in the process. The domestic campaign 
should also concentrate on the facilities etc. avai lable at major tourist spots and the means and 
modes of transportation to reach those places. The malpractices and misleading propaganda of 
touts and middlemen at tourist place also be brought out through domestic campaigns. 
(Para 43)  
OVERSEAS CAMPAIGN 
  The Committee notes that the Incredible India cam paign launched abroad has brought in 
foreign tourists to various parts of country. This has also helped tourist and gained popularity 
amongst travellers all over the world. The Committe e recommends that allocation made under 
this head should be utilized scrupulously for conti nuing the overseas campaign so that more 
foreign tourists are attracted and in turn help foreign exchange earnings. (Para 52)  
  India also, like China and USA, need to do a lot like development of infrastructure at the 
tourists places, etc. Private participation needs to be encouraged. (Para 53)  
  The Committee expresses its serious concern for o ver sensitizing even local issues which 
hampers the tourism promotion. The Committee critic izes the way in which the terrorist 
attacks, the swine flu and stray cases of harassmen t of foreign tourists etc, were handled, had 
quite an adverse impact over the image of India abr oad. The committee is of the view that the 

Ministry should take necessary steps in ensuring th at media should not unnecessarily create 
panic. 
(Para 54)  
TRAINING 
  The Committee is not satisfied with the efforts m ade by the Ministry regarding human 
resource development. The Government has not made s ufficient plan outlay under the head 
‘assistance for manpower training’. In the year 200 9-10, an amount of Rs. 100.70 crore was 
allocated. For the 2010-11 there is negligible increase in the plan outlay i.e. Rs. 102.50 crore. The

institutes. The Committee feels that the huge shortage of about 1.9 lakhs can not be met only by

courses in coordination with the hospitality indust ry which will provide employability to those

conducting quality courses.                                                                                                      (Para 63)

REPORT  
  Roads have an important role in the economic deve lopment of a country. India has a vast road network  of 3.62 
million km. that consists of Expressways, National Highways, State Highways, major district roads, other district roads 
and village roads. The National Highways and the St ate Highways together account for 2,04,000 kms. The  length of 
National Highways network at present is 70,934 kms.  constituting about 2 per cent of the total road ne twork in the 
country and carrying about 40 per cent of the total  traffic across the length and breadth of the count ry. Between 2001-
02 and 2005-06 the number of vehicles had grown at an average pace of 10 per cent per annum and consequently traffic 
on the roads has increased at 7 -10 per cent per an num. The share of roads in total traffic has been g rowing from 13.8 
per cent of freight traffic and 15.4 per cent of th e passenger traffic in 1950-51 to 60 per cent of fr eight traffic and 87.4 
per cent of passenger traffic respectively by the end of 2005-06. 
2.  This unprecedented growth of road traffic, call s for a massive expansion and improvement of the road network in 
the country. This would require a massive infusion of funds supported by efficient mechanisms and trained manpower. 
Historically in India, investments in roads, especi ally highways, were mainly made by the Government b ecause of the 
large volume of resources required, long gestation period of projects, uncertain returns and various a ssociated 
externalities. But in recent times, the private sec tor has been actively involved in the development a nd maintenance of 
the National Highways. 
3.  The Ministry has formulated policy guidelines t o encourage private sector participation in the hig hway sector, 
besides providing several incentives such as tax ex emptions and duty free import of road building equi pment and 
machinery. Model Concession Agreements have also been finalized for major road projects, under PPP model. 
4.  The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is basically responsible for the construction and main tenance of 
National Highways (NH), administration of Motor Veh icle Act and Central Motor Vehicles Rules, formulat ion of 
broad policies relating to road transport, environmental issues relating to vehicular movements, automotive norms, etc. 
besides making arrangements for movements of vehicular traffic with neighbouring countries. 
5.  The development and maintenance of National Hig hways are being done on agency basis mainly by the National 
Highways Authority of India (NHAI), State Public Wo rks Departments (PWDs) and the Border Roads Organiz ation. 
Out of the total length of 70,934 km of National Hi ghways, 42,598 km is with the State Public Works De partments 
(State PWDs), 20,666 km with the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and 3,892 km with the Bor der Road 
Organization. Remaining 3,778 km is yet to be entrusted to the executing agencies. 
6.  The National Highways have further been classif ied depending upon the width formation. Generally, a lane has a 
width of 3.75 metres in case of single lane and 3.5  metres in case of multi lane National Highways. Th e break-up of 
National Highways in terms of width is as under: 
  Single Lane/Intermediate lane 19,803 km. (28%) 
  Double Lane 38,006 km. (53.5%) 
  Four/Six/Eight Lane 13,125 km. (14%)

the financial year 2010-11 was considered by the  Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, 
Tourism and Culture at its meeting held on the 22nd  March, 2010. During the meeting, the Committee too k oral 
evidence of the Secretary and other officers of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

10.  The tables above do not reflect a very good perform ance in achieving the financial and physical target s 
except a few. The Committee finds the reasons given  for the savings are of routine nature. For example , one of 
the reasons for saving CRF is non-submission of proposals and non-receipt of utilisation certificates by the State 
Governments. Reasons for these, if provided could h ave been more revealing to the Committee. The State -wise 
details also could have further provided a real pic ture in this regard. Saving of Rs.50 crores due to retendering 
of works of development of National Highways and St ates roads in naxal affected areas which is a sensi tive 
programme is a cause of concern. Efforts should hav e been made for avoiding the problem necessitating re-
tendering. Further an amount of Rs.20 crore meant f or development of Vijaywada-Ranchi National Highway s 
could not be utilized because draft note for solici ting approval of CCI is still under process even af ter one year 
has passed. Another area of major concern is non-ut ilisation of Rs.600 crore under SARDP-NE due to slo w 
progress of work by BRO. The reasons for slow progr ess are not known. There is a saving of Rs.15 crore  in the 
projects of strategic and Border Roads Project due to non-materialization of supply orders and contrac t for 
procurement of Constructional stores and materials.  Here also, reasons are not given. An amount of Rs. 30 
crores for POSCO could not be utilized due to non-r eceipt of utilization certificates from the Governm ent of 
Orissa. Obviously, due to non-utilization of funds the project must be languishing. An amount of Rs.20  crore 
could not be utilized because Mughal Road Project i s being funded directly by the Planning Commission.  If it 
was so, why the allocation was provided in the Budg et? . What is the status of project? Who is monitor ing the 
project? What is the role of Ministry of Road Trans port and Highways in this project? The explanations  given 
for saving by the Ministry are not clear and convin cing. In view of these, the Committee is of the vie w that the 
Ministry should have been more proactive and taken necessary steps on time to ensure that these delays  in 
execution of projects should have been avoided.  
11.  Another pattern the Committee noted is that many ro ad projects are delayed due to delay in obtaining 
necessary clearances including environmental cleara nce. The delays result in cost and time overruns an d the 
non-achievement of the targets which ultimately imp inges upon national growth and development. The 
Committee is of the view that it leaves an impressi on in the minds of public there being a nexus betwe en the 
contractors and the authorities concern to delay th e projects deliberately so that the project cost go es up 

resulting in more profit. The Government of India should take effective steps to tackle such problems existing in 
the process of award of the road projects including  the grant of environmental clearance. The Committe e is 
aware about the steps taken recently such as consti tution of Task Force headed by the Finance Minister  and 
Inter-Ministerial Group, but feels that process of environmental clearance needs to be further streamlined. The 
infrastructure projects including National Highways  are as important as protecting our national habita t. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport should obtain the environmental clearance before 
finalizing or awarding the cost of project, not vice-versa.  
POOR PERFORMANCE OF CONTRACTORS, NEXUS AND DELAYS  
12.  As regards corruption and unholy collusion bet ween contractors and authorities, The Secretary, Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways was candid enough to accept the operation of such a nexus. He also pointed out about the 
agencies where the real problem existed. He said th at there was nothing wrong with contract with the r ules and 
regulation but the real problem was of enforcements . As regards non-performance, blacklisting and puni shments “in 
few cases they (NHAI) have really declared contract ors as non-performers”. He emphasized that although the Minister 
himself was concerned about it, but “need was to vi gorously pursue them and penalize”. He further clar ified that 
“failure was on the part of NHAI or the State Gover nment or our system “Expressing his helplessness to  do anything 
about it the Secretary called upon the Members of the Committee to do something. He said: 
"... it is these areas where you as a Member of Sta nding Committee must come out strongly and must pass some 
law and those fellows should be punished mercilessl y which is not happening. It is a fact. You see how  the 
contractors, the engineers and the consultants join hands and create disputes. We have seen and the Mi nister has 
said that. Even in land acquisition in NHAI project , the Director and the contractors sometimes join h ands 
together and they de1ay. These have been observed. Really the question is, we have to see how we can i mprove 
the system. How we can check the malaise. This is what I would say..." 
13.  When asked about his responsibility, Secretary , Road Transport and Highways submitted that he was  not 
excluding himself. In first stance, he said the per sons on the ground level were mainly responsible fo r this and 
complaints have been received about it, but “these were mainly enforcement issues and ground level iss ues”, Ministry 
had a limitation as these were basically NHAI matters. 
14.  While concluding the discussion on this issue,  Secretary, Road Transport and Highways said:  
“... All of us have to play our roles, right from m y level, down to the Chairman, NHAI, DG and others.  They 
have to play their roles. They must take action wherever something is wrong...” 
15.  The Committee is also aware of the existence of suc h a nexus leading to corruption and delays not only  in 
this sector but in other sectors as well. A substantial portion of our developmental funds is being siphoned off, as 
a result of which, the desired benefits of our sche mes and programmes are not reaching upto the ground  level. 
What worries the Committee most is the general sens e of helplessness in fighting out this unholy nexus  and the 
consequent alarmingly high “delivery leakages”. The  Committee did not find any serious attempt made or  
proposed against such a nexus in the road sector. T he Committee would like to know the steps taken or 
proposed by the Ministry and NHAI in this regard.  
16.  The Committee enquired from the Ministry how m any Projects were delayed due to the poor performan ce of 
contractors. The Ministry replied that the projects  under NHDP had been delayed mainly due to problems  associated 
with land acquisition, shifting of utilities, obtai ning environment, forest and railway clearances, po or performance of 
contractors, law and order problems in some States,  etc. In most cases projects were delayed due to mo re than one 
factor. It was, therefore, not appropriate to single out one reason for delay on projects. 

17.  The Committee notes that apart from land acquisitio n and various clearances, poor performance of 
contractors is another major reason for delay in ro ad projects. Possibility of a nexus between middlem en, bad 
contractors and corrupt officials to delay the proj ects can not be ruled out. Ministry’s officials cou ld not give 
any information about the projects delayed due to p oor performance of contractors, in fact only one co ntractor 
had been blacklisted so far. The Committee recommen ds that the Ministry should compile the information  
regarding non-performing contractors and they should be black listed.  
ANNUAL  PLAN 2010-11  
18.  The Committee was informed that the Planning C ommission provided an annual outlay of Rs 25,455.00 crore for 
2010-11 (Rs. 25,155 crore for Central Sector Roads and Rs. 300 crore for Road Transport) to the Minist ry of Road 
Transport and Highways including IEBR of Rs. 7,455 crore. The break-up is as follows:

NON-PLAN BUDGET (2010-11) MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS OF NATIONAL HIGHWAYS  
65.  The maintenance of National Highways is of par amount importance. Under this head, funds are provi ded for the 
preservation and proper upkeep of National Highways  all over the country. Over the past six decades, t he volume of 
traffic on Indian roads has increased exponentially ; between 1950-51 and 2002-03, the freight traffic increased 101 
times and passenger traffic 132 times. During this period, the share of the road sector in total freig ht traffic increased 
from 12% - 65% and passenger traffic from 25% - 85% . However, notwithstanding the vast network of road s and of 
National Highways, there are serious concerns about  their quality and capacity. The rise in labour wag es and steep 
increase in prices of materials, particularly, of p etroleum products in recent years are reflected in the high cost of 
maintenance and repair of National Highways. For th e year 2010-11 funds for Maintenance and Repairs ha ve been 
proposed at Rs.l,032.86 crore for the National Highways. 
66.  In reply to a query regarding projected and al located amount of funds the Ministry submitted that regarding Non-
Plan works for maintenance of National Highways a provision of Rs.1032.86 crore has been made against the projected 
demand of Rs.2000 crore. This amount will not be sufficient for proper maintenance and upkeep of National Highways. 

At the RE stage demand will be made for additional allocation depending on the pace of expenditure and  condition of 
National Highways. 
67.  The Committee feels that the Ministry would be in a  position to maintain the national highways in good  
condition with this allocation. The Committee is of  the opinion that national highways in the country require 
timely and planned maintenance and upkeep in view o f overload they bear. The Committee hopes that the 
Ministry will maintain a uniform quality and improv e the capacity of national highways in due course b y 
utilizing the allocated money to the maximum. The C ommittee recommends that those areas which are affe cted 
by Monsoon and hilly areas affected by landslide an d rain Deed special attention as far as maintenance  and 
repairs of roads are concerned.  
68.  When asked about the quality and safety on the hig hways in India, Chairman, NHAI argued that our cost 
of road construction was only one-fourth of that in Europe and America. He also argued that toll amount the we 
are collecting in India was only one-eighth/tenth o f that in western countries. He perhaps was arguing  that we 
can not but construct only sub international standa rds roads as we don’t spent as much as USA and Euro pean 
countries do. The Committee finds this comparison, both in terms of cost and amount of toll in India a nd other 
countries, in fact fallacious. This argument overlooks the role of locally available material, technology and cheap 
labour for which most of the multi nationals were o ut sourcing these works to India. NHAI should lay m ore 
emphasize on using indigenous techniques, material suitable to our needs and conditions. The Committee agreed 
with him that quality does not come free but wants to know if we are getting best possible quality eve n with the 
limited funds that we are spending. Answer to this, undoubtedly would be in negative.

suitable incentives.

Setting up of Inspection and Maintenance Centre  
89.  The Committee was informed that under Section 59 of the M.V. Act, 1988, Central Government have p owers to 
fix the age of motor vehicles of different categori es. However, as yet this Section has not been invok ed, the Ministry 
has only fixed the ‘age’ of certain categories of v ehicles for the purpose of tourist permit and natio nal permit, under 
rule 82 and 88 of CMVR, 1989. The Ministry’s stand has been that a well maintained older vehicle can b e less 
polluting than an ill maintained newer vehicle. A vehicle can ply on the road as long as it meets the requirements of the 
Motor Vehicles Act and Central Motor Vehicles Rules , 1989 with regard to safety, emission and fitness norms. 
Fixation of age of vehicle would also be not advisable, keeping in view the socio-economic condition of the country. 
90.  The Committee was further informed that a tran sport vehicle has to undergo fitness test every yea r after two 
years of the date of initial registration. There is  no such requirement for non-transport vehicle for 15 years once they 

are registered. Hence the Ministry is of the considered view that proper inspection and maintenance system must be put 
in place to identify the vehicles which do not meet  the emission and safety norms. Such inspection and  maintenance 
centres would need to be set up in various states with Public- Private Partnership. A scheme to set up model Inspection 
and Certification centres has been approved by Plan ning Commission and the same is being processed for  approval of 
competent authority. During the year 2010-11, allocation of Rs. 54.00 crore has been made under the scheme. 
91.  The Committee feels that the Ministry is spending m ore time in conception of projects rather than 
implementing the same. The Committee would like to know the steps taken by the Ministry in this regard so far. 
The Committee feels that as the country is already overloaded with old vehicles, time has come for set ting up of 
Inspection and Maintenance Centers to maintain uniform emission and safety norms throughout the country.

AUTOMATIC FARE COLLECTION BASED ON GPS  
92.  The Ministry informed the Committee that decli ne of public transport has been one of the failures of our transport 
planning over the years. The percentage of buses in  the total fleet of vehicles has come down from mor e than 11% in 
1951 to 1.1 % in 2004. This leads to increase in th e personalized transport which in turn has a number  of adverse 
consequences such as congestion, pollution, and acc idents apart from being inequalitarian as the poor get excluded 
from transport services. This needs to be reversed.  It is proposed that in the 11th Five Year Plan the  provisions should 
be made at the Central level to provide financial assistance to help the States to strengthen their public transport system 
including application of IT like automatic fare collection system based on GPS. However such financial assistance shall 
be restricted to those States who undertake to take  measures for reforms in the public transport syste m. The 
Expenditure Finance Committee and Planning Commissi on have approved the scheme. The scheme has now bee n 
approved by Hon’ble Finance Minister on 5.3.10 and the scheme is being circulated to all States/UTs in viting 
proposals. 
93.  To a specific query on the response of the Sta te Governments in promoting public transport to reduce congestion 
on national highways and other strategically import ant roads, the Ministry replied that the State Gove rnments were 
requested by the Ministry to take measures to disco urage use of private vehicles and promote public tr ansport system. 
In order to impress upon the States to revamp their  public transport, a meeting of Chief Executives of  State Road 
Transport Undertakings was held under the chairmans hip of Secretary (RT&H) on 30.10.2009. The State Tr ansport 
Undertakings were eager to revamp their corporations to meet the growing demand for public transport. However, they 
have asked the Government to provide financial assi stance for this purpose and also desired that the i ssues concerning 
public transport need to be addressed adequately. A  Committee under the chairmanship of MD, KSRTC has been 
constituted to identify core problem areas to strengthen public transport system. 
94.  The Committee is distressed to note the failli ng share of public transport system as percentage o f buses in the 
total fleet of vehicles has come down from more tha n 11% in 1951 to 1.1% in 2004. The Committee feels that by 
revamping the public transport systems in the count ry, congestion as well as pollution on the roads ca n be reduced 
drastically. The Committee while welcoming the effo rts taken by the Ministry in this regard hopes that  the Ministry 
will pursue the issue with more vigour so that the allocated funds do not remain unutilized or under-utilized.

arbitrator(s)/constitution of Dispute Resolution Board(DRB) depending upon cost of the project. Howeve r, it has been 
experienced on numerous occasions that their awards  are frequently contested in the Court of Law resul ting into delay 
in settlement of disputes. Considering the problem being faced, particularly in NHDP projects, this is sue has also been 
covered under the purview of the Committee headed by Shri B.K. Chaturvedi, Member, Planning Commission. 
98.  The Committee notes that there exist no effective dispute redressal mechanisms for resolving the problems 
affecting road sector. This leads to unbridled bureaucratic control and scope for manipulation by those elements 
which have connections and links with middlemen and corrupt authorities.  
99.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that an effect ive dispute redressal mechanism in the form of 
tribunals or other mechanism for speedy resolution of conflicts may be put in place at the earliest.  
TOLL  POLICY  
100.  The Committee was informed that as per existi ng toll policy is in perpetuity. For the concession  for a particular 
BOT (Toll) project, toll period is decided on the basis of projected traffic, total project cost, financial expenditure. 15% 
return on investment and maximum 40% viability gap funding. BOT toll rates per km. and rates for 
bridges/tunnel/bypass on the basis of cost is provided. 
101.  The Committee feels that the toll policy in perpetu ity is fundamentally wrong and it needs to be revie wed 
according to the changing situations. The Committee notes that there are instances of collecting tolls  from areas 
where condition of the roads were so poor. There we re also instances that 23 toll plazas being operate d in a 
stretch of 60 kms of National Highway-62 in Meghalaya.  

  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Rules  and Regulations regarding collection of toll shoul d 
be revisited and brought at par with the modern day  requirements of road users instead of keeping it a s an 
instrument of unjust profiteering by unscrupulous elements.  
LESS  ALLOCATION  TO  KERALA  
102.  Another aspect brought before the Committee is that the State of Kerala is getting less fund allocation and 
National Highway projects though the State is alway s demanding more for funds and new highway projects . 
Many of the highway projects are delayed especially  the project from Kochi to Kollam. Construction of various 
bypasses undertaken by the Government especially th e Kollam Alleppy and Thrissur by-passes are lying i n 
limbo for years together.  
103.  The Committee recommends that the Ministry may look  into the delay and expedite the completion of the 
projects.  
GENERAL OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
104.  The Committee while examining the demands of the Mi nistry felt that one of the major impediments in 
implementing road projects whether it is NHDP or no n-NHDP was the absence of an effective coordination  
among different agencies at different level and at various stages of road constructions. The Committee  is of the 
opinion that absence of such a mechanism in road pr ojects causes delay at every stage from conception to final 
operation. Issues like quality of and safety on roads, development and maintenance of national highways, tolling 
policy, land acquisition and role of States, corrup tion such that they need to be taken for further co nsideration 
separately.  
105.  The Committee also feels that the Ministry should g ive adequate importance to road safety as that of 
development of national highways. The Committee fin ds that the Indian roads lack way side amenities to  users. 
The Committee feels that the Ministry should give a mple consideration in this aspect by providing park ing 
facilities, cafeterias and trauma care centers along national highways and strategically important roads.  
106.  The Committee hopes that the Ministry would utilize  the allocated funds diligently to the maximum 
possible.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  

OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS –– AT A GLANCE  
  The tables above do not reflect a very good perfo rmance in achieving the financial and physical targ ets 
except a few. The Committee finds the reasons given  for the savings are of routine nature. For example , one of 
the reasons for saving CRF is non-submission of proposals and non-receipt of utilisation certificates by the State 
Governments. Reasons for these, if provided could h ave been more revealing to the Committee. The state -wise 
details also could have further provided a real pic ture in this regard. Saving of Rs. 50 crores due to  retendering 
of works of development of National Highways and St ates roads in naxal affected areas which is a sensi tive 
programme is a cause of concern. Efforts should hav e been made for avoiding the problem necessitating re-
tendering. Further an amount of Rs.20 crore meant f or development of Vijaywada-Ranchi National Highway s 
could not be utilized because draft note for solici ting approval of CCI is still under process even af ter one year 
has passed. Another area of major concern is non-ut ilisation of Rs.600 crore under SARDP-NE due to slo w 
progress of work by BRO. The reasons for slow progr ess are not known. There is a saving of Rs.15 crore  in the 
projects of strategic and Border Roads Project due to non-materialization of supply orders and contrac t for 
procurement of constructional stores and materials. Here also, reasons are not given. An amount of Rs.30 crores 
for POSCO could not be utilized due to non-receipt of utilization certificates from the Government of Orissa. 
Obviously, due to non-utilization of funds the proj ect must be languishing. An amount of Rs.20 crore c ould not 
be utilized because Mughal Road Project is being fu nded directly by the Planning Commission. If it was  so why 
the allocation was provided in the Budget? What is the Status of project? Who is monitoring the projec t? What 
is the role of Ministry of Road Transport and Highways in this project? The explanations given for saving by the 
Ministry are not clear and convincing. In view of t hese, the Committee is of the view that the Ministr y should 
have been more proactive and taken necessary steps on time to ensure that these delays in execution of  projects 
should have been avoided.  (Para 10)  
  Another pattern the Committee noted is that many road projects are delayed due to delay in obtaining  
necessary clearances including environmental cleara nce. The delays result in cost and time overruns an d the 
non-achievement of the targets which ultimately imp inges upon national growth and development. The 
Committee is of the view that it leaves an impressi on in the minds of public there being a nexus betwe en the 
contractors and the authorities concern to delay th e projects deliberately so that the project cost go es up 
resulting in more profit. The Government of India should take effective steps to tackle such problems existing in 
the process of award of the road projects including  the grant of environmental clearance. The Committe e is 
aware about the steps taken recently such as consti tution of Task Force headed by the Finance Minister  and 
Inter-Ministerial Group, but feels that process of environmental clearance needs to be further streamlined. The 
infrastructure projects including National Highways  are as important as protecting our national habita t. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport should obtain the environmental clearance before 
finalizing or awarding the cost of project, not vice-versa. (Para 11) 
 
POOR  PERFORMANCE  OF  CONTRACTORS,  NEXUS  AND  DELAYS 
  The Committee is also aware of the existence of s uch a nexus leading to corruption and delays not on ly in 
this sector but in other sectors as well. A substantial portion of our developmental funds is being siphoned off, as 
a result of which, the desired benefits of our sche mes and programmes are not reaching upto the ground  level. 
What worries the Committee most is the general sens e of helplessness in fighting out this unholy nexus  and the 
consequent alarmingly high “delivery leakages”. The  committee did not find any serious attempt made or  
proposed against such a nexus in the road sector. T he Committee would like to know the steps taken or 
proposed by the Ministry and NHAI in this regard. (Para 15)  
  The Committee notes that apart from land acquisit ion and various clearances, poor performance of 
contractors is another major reason for delay in ro ad proiects. Possibility of a nexus between middlem en, bad 

contractors and corrupt officials to delay the proj ects can not be ruled out. Ministry’s officials cou ld not give 
any information about the projects delayed due to p oor performance of contractors, in fact only one co ntractor 
had been blacklisted so far. The Committee recommen ds that the Ministry should compile the information  
regarding non-performing contractors and they should be black listed. (Para 17)  
ANNUAL  PLAN 2010-11 
  The Committee could see that in the BE 2010-11 al so most of the allocations have been increased, but  
financial as well as physical performance indicator s do not inspire much confidence, not at all in the  year 2009-
10. Some of the good schemes have suffered due to n on-utilisation of funds, for whatsoever reasons. Th e 
Committee quite appreciates certain limitations in the development of roads/highways, but it feels tha t the pace 
can still be improved with better inspection, monit oring and coordination between the Ministries, NHAI , States 
Governments and Private agencies. Association of lo cal representatives, particularly those of M.Ps and  M.L.As 
can prove to be quite effective in many ways. (Para 26)  
CONSTRUCTION OF 20 KMS. OF ROAD PER DAY 
  The 20 Kms per day project is the need of the hou r but based on our past experience and the issue 
involved, it appears to be quite an ambitious targe t, particularly in view of the construction of road s just 2 kms 
per day in previous years so far, we are nowhere ne ar this target. Odds are many, especially those rel ating to 
land acquisition and environmental clearances that have acquired graver proportion now. In view of the se 
limitations, the Committee only hopes that achievin g this target would be a difficult task. It is, how ever, happy 
that the Ministry was working with such a huge target before it. (Para 31)  
NATIONAL  HIGHWAYS  AUTHORITY  OF  INDIA 
  The Committee could see that BE last year had to scale down by about 2,000 crores at RE stage, which the 
Committee only hopes would be actually utilized. Increases in BE 2010-11 would be a challenge before the NHAI 
to utilize fully along with additional amount received as remittance of toll receipts. (Para 35)  
  The Committee is very much concerned over the tar dy progress of projects under NHDP. The Committee 
fails to understand the logic behind delay in compl etion of NS and EW corridors even after the lapse o f 
reasonable period. The Committee feels that the NHAI which is having sufficient funds in its coffer is not serious 
in implementing major projects up to its potential.  The Committee is of the opinion that expanding NHD P 
further without completing the NHDP phase I and II even in the extended schedule will not going to yie ld any 
result. The Committee would also like to have the i nformation on the guidelines/policies followed by N HAI on 
rehabilitation of land owners for the land acquired  for road projects. The Committee is of the opinion  that the 
NHAI is not following standard guidelines in the ca se of offering compensation to the landowners in ro ad 
projects. The Committee feels that timely completio n of such mega projects will benefit both the gover nment 
and the road users. The Committee hopes that NHAI will concentrate more on development of roads rather than 
finding venues to fill its coffers. (Para 40)  
REVISED STRATEGY FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL  HIGHWAYS DEVELOPMENT 
PROJECT (NHDP) 
  The Committee hopes that with the implementation of recommendations of the BK Chaturvedi Report on 
the revised strategy for implementation of National  Highways Development Project, this sector should g et the 
required facelift. The NHAI should not shield itsel f behind delays due to land acquisition, environmen tal 
clearance and other contractor related issues for t he completion of NHDP projects. The Committee feels  that 
development of national highways in the country so far has been rather slow. The Committee hopes that 

ambitious projects of NHAI such as six lane highway s and expressways which are the need of the hour to  keep 
pace with the economic growth of the nation and the ever increasing vehicular traffic should be implemented on 
priority rather than keeping them in approval stage for a longer period. (Para 43)  
ROADS  OF  INTER-STATE  CONNECTIVITY  AND  ECONOMIC  IMPORTANCE 
  The Committee noticed that development of roads o f inter-state connectivity and economic importance are 
not getting their due attention they require. The Committee notes that only one project at a cost of Rs. 6.28 crore 
was approved in the year 2009-10 as against 20 projects in the previous year and only 10 projects were approved 
as against 27 under the Inter-State connectivity projects. The Committee feels that the Ministry should expedite 
faster development of these roads as they play a vi tal role in giving connectivity to major national h ighways 
across the country. The Committee hopes that the Mi nistry will give due consideration for the developm ent of 
these roads during 2010-11 so that more projects could be approved and implemented under these heads. 
(Para 47)  
NATIONAL  HIGHWAYS  (ORIGINAL) WORKS 
  The Committee notes that the budgetary provision for National Highways (O) works in 2009-10 (BE) was  
Rs.3359.55 crore, which was substantially increased  to Rs.4359.55 crore at the RE stage, out of which,  an 
amount of Rs.3370.05 crore was expended till 28.2.2010. However, the allocation has been reduced in the annual 
plan 2010-11 by around Rs. 500 crores that has been  fixed at Rs.3,850.10 crore. The Committee wishes t o 
understand the reasons for enhancing the allocation  at RE stage by Rs.I000 crore and allocating much r educed 
amount in the BE 2010-11. The Ministry on their par t should justify the enhancement in allocation at R E stage 
in 2009-10 by spending up to the level of BE level only. The Committee expresses its concern about the  pattern 
of utilization of funds by the Ministry under this head. It appears that the Ministry is more committe d to 
develop national highways under the NHDP and not th e non-NHDP national highways. The Committee feels 
that such approach of the Ministry in maintaining t he Non-NHDP national highways will definitely affec t the 
already beleaguered national highways network adversely. (Para 50)  
  The Committee also notes that the Ministry may sp end around Rs.I000/crore i.e. 25% of the allocation 
during the month of March 2010. The Committee is of the view that the last minute spending of huge amount of 
money at the fag end of the financial year is again st the norms of a healthy fiscal discipline and tra nsparency. It 
should be avoided. Utilization of plan funds should  be evenly spread throughout the year. Otherwise, t he 
monitoring of the spending of the allocation and quality of the roads may be impossible. (Para 51)  
DEVELOPMENT  OF  NA TIONAL  HIGHWAYS  IN  NORTH-EASTERN  REGION 
  The Committee notes that an amount of Rs.1200 cro re was allocated for SARDP-NE during the year 2009-
10 and an amount of Rs.465.70 was expended till 28.2.2010.Total 270 km roads of 2-lane equivalent stan dards 
were constructed. Together with the roads completed  upto the previous year, total of 450 km roads have  been 
completed under SARDP-NE against 1400 km for execution on EPC basis. The Committee finds the reasons that 
funds could not be utilized fully because of slow p rogress of works under implementation by BRO, 
unconvincing. The Committee recommends that the Gov ernment must look into the actual reasons and help 
BRO to do away the obstacles that delay the project s. The Committee hopes that the development of nati onal 
highways between Jakhilabandha to Upper Assam which is pending for environmental clearance will be cleared 
on priority as also the construction of another bridge over Brahmaputra which is also a longstanding demand of 
North-Eastern Region. The Committee also hopes that NHs 51 and 62 which are in a bad shape will also g et due 
attention from the Ministry since these national hi ghways play a vital role in providing connectivity in the 

North-Eastern Region as national highways are lifeline of the people of this region in the absence of proper road 
and air connectivity. The Committee also ask the NH AI to look into the cases of large numbers of toll gates in 
North-East, particularly NH 62 in Meghalaya.  (Para 57)  
SPECIAL PROGRAMME FOR DEVELOPMENT OF ROADS IN THE L EFT WING EXTREMISM (LWE) 
AFFECTED AREAS AND PROGRAMME FOR DEVELOPMENT OF VIJAYAWADA - RANCHI ROAD 
  The Committee notes the steps taken by the Minist ry for developing roads in the naxalite affected ar eas 
covering 33 districts in eight States. The Committee is at a loss to see that the savings of 2/3rd of plan fund Rs.75 
crore allocated for the development of roads in the  naxal affected areas, only Rs.25 crore is likely t o be spent 
during 2009-10. The Committee finds the reasons ret endering of works in the case of Chhattisgarh and d elay in 
approval of works in Andhra Pradesh due to court ca se, quite routine ones. The Committee would like to  know 
the reasons for retendering of the work in Chhattis garh and the steps taken or advice given to the Sta te 
Governments to sort out the problems. This being a very good scheme, the Government should monitor the  
programme on a regular basis to ensure that the fund is utilized and required infrastructure is constructed in all 
the 33 districts. The Committee is of the opinion t hat the Ministry should coordinate with the Ministry of Home 
Affairs for the successful implementation of this project. The State Governments involved may also be consulted 
on a regular basis for the implementation of the projects. (Para 59)  
CENTRAL  ROAD  FUND 
  The Committee feels that increase in accrual to C RF will naturally result in increased allocation of  more 
funds to the States. The Committee hopes that the M inistry should evolve a monitoring mechanism to ens ure 
that funds allocated under this head are judiciously expended. The Committee notes that an amount of Rs.86.56 
crore is likely to remain unutilized during 2009-10  due to lack of proposals for approval or non-recei pt of 
utilization certificate from States/Union Territori es. The Committee feels that delays in the developm ent that 
should take place in a particular year is further d elayed/ postponed for subsequent years just because of the lax 
execution of the projects and programmes. There is always a cost overrun on the delayed projects which  
ultimately affects the public exchequer and national growth. The Committee recommends that Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways should be proactive and take  up the matter with the State Governments concerned  to 
ensure that proposal and utilization certificate are received from there so that funds are released and utilized. 
       (Para 64)  
NON-PLAN BUDGET (2010-11) MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS OF NATIONAL HIGHWAYS 
  The Committee feels that the Ministry would be in  a position to maintain the national highways in go od 
condition with this allocation. The Committee is of  the opinion that national highways in the country require 
timely and planned maintenance and upkeep in view o f overload they bear. The Committee hopes that the 
Ministry will maintain a uniform quality and improv e the capacity of national highways in due course b y 
utilizing the allocated money to the maximum. The C ommittee recommends that those areas which are affe cted 
by Monsoon and hilly areas affected by landslide an d rain need special attention as far as maintenance  and 
repairs of roads are concerned. (Para 67)   
 
  When asked about the quality and safety on the hi ghways in India, Chairman NHAI argued that our cost  
of road construction was only one-fourth of that in Europe and America. He also argued that toll amount the we 
are collecting in India was only one-eighth/tenth o f that in western countries. He perhaps was arguing  that we 
can not but construct only sub international standa rds roads as we don’t spent as much as USA and Euro pean 
countries do. The Committee finds this comparison, both in terms of cost and amount of toll in India a nd other 

countries, in fact fallacious. This argument overlooks the role of locally available material, technology and cheap 
labour for which most of the multi nationals were o ut sourcing these works to India. NHAI should lay m ore

REFRESHER TRAINING OF DRIVERS IN UNORGANISED SECTOR  AND HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT 
  The Committee is surprised to find that the HRD s ector is not being given due importance by the 
Government. During 2009-10, an amount of Rs.20 crore approved at BE stage was reduced to Rs.10 crore at RE

fully for this purpose.   (Para 75)  
NATIONAL  HIGHWAYS  ACCIDENT  RELIEF  SERVICE  SCHEME 
  The Committee finds that out of the allocated amo unt of Rs.29.49 crore (RE) in 2009-10, the Ministry  was

the desired priority of the Ministry. In view of in creased number of road accidents, the under utiliza tion of 
funds for such a life saving activities can hardly be justified. The Committee feels that the Ministry  should 
provide adequate number of ambulances and the traum a care equipments along the national highways for 
providing much needed emergency medical aids to accidents victims. (Para 78)  
  The Committee also recommends that the toll colle cting plazas may be equipped with sufficient cranes and

  The Committee feels that enhanced allocation of f unds under this head will further strengthen the 
pollution control in the country. Number of vehicle s is increasing day by day resulting in more chaos and

equipments, enforcement of tightened PUC norms will  definitely have positive impact on the green earth .

suitable incentives.   (Para 82)  
NATIONAL  DATA  BASE  NETWORK 
  The Committee notes the performance of the Minist ry in implementing information technology enabled 
system around 14 States and the steps taken to impl ement the same in other States also. The Committee

yet fully computerized. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways should 
further pursue with States which have not implement ed the Vahan (Registration Certificate) and Sarathi  

(Driving Licence) projects to implement it in a tim ebound manner. The Committee hopes that with the 
allocation of Rs.30 crore in the BE 2010-11, the Ministry could achieve their target during the current fiscal.

REPORT  
  The Ministry of Shipping encompasses under its ma ndate Shipping and Port Sector, which include Shipbuilding and Ship-
repair, Major Ports, National Waterways and Inland Water Transport Systems. This Ministry also formula tes policies and 
programmes on these subjects and is responsible for  their implementation. Ministry of Shipping is also  responsible for the 
development of the Major ports With the objective t o provide necessary and adequate cargo handling cap acity and other 
infrastructure required for this. 
ORGANISATIONAL STRUCTURE  
2.  The Ministry of Shipping has the following Subo rdinate and Attached offices under it: 
(i) Director General of Shipping, Mumbai (including  Minor Ports Survey Organisation, Mumbai) 
(ii) Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightsh ips, Noida (U.P.)

embarkation facilities in Lakshadweep group of islands.

berths; 28 capital dredging projects for deepening of channels and berths; 73 projects for procurement/replacement/upgradation 
of cargo handling equipments and floating crafts; 53 rail/road connectivity projects and 101 other associated works. The details 
of projected outlay and the actual allocation for the 11th Plan are as follows:

per cent and 23 per cent respectively during the 11 th plan period. By 2011-12 it is projected that India’s merchandise trade will 
reach 650 billion US Dollars as against 312.86 billion US Dollars during 2007-08. 
7.  The Committee notes that the shipping sector plays an important role in India’s economy. Almost 90% of  the 
country’s trade by volume is conducted via  sea and the country boasts of having the largest m erchant shipping fleet 
among the developing nations. The Indian shipping i ndustry not only transports national and internatio nal cargos, but 
also provides various other facilities such as ship building, ship-repairing, lighthouse facilities, fr eight forwarding, etc. 
However, certain core problems such as Port congest ion and lack of depth in channels are plaguing the shipping 
industry.  
8.  The Committee notes that the working group constitu ted for Eleventh Plan had recommended an outlay of 
Rs.7689 crore as GBS for Shipping and IWT Sector, b ut the Planning Commission restricted it to Rs.1301  crore only. 
The Committee, in view of the increasing share of S hipping Sector in Indian trade, feels that the curr ent level of 
allocations is highly inadequate and it will curtai l the growth of shipping and IWT. The Committee, th erefore, 
recommends that the Government of India should increase the allocation for both shipping as well as port sectors for the 
remaining Plan period. The Ministry of Shipping, th erefore, should also come forward with proposals fo r development 
and the Planning Commission should allocate the funds for the purpose.  
9.  The Committee emphasises the need for strengthening the shipping sector to take up with the demands granted by 
the globalisation and liberalisation. The Indian sh ipping industry must acquire new heights in terms o f demand and 
infrastructural development.   
ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2010-11  
10.   The Department-related Parliamentary Standing  Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture consid ered Demand 
No.87 containing the details of the budgetary provi sions of Ministry of Shipping for the financial yea r 2010-11, at its meeting 
held on the 26th March, 2010. The Committee took or al evidence of the Secretary and other officials of  the Ministry of 
Shipping in the meeting.

Transport, Shipbuilding and Ship repair Sectors. Mi nistry of Shipping informed that the Annual Plan of  Rs.6494.15 crore for 
the year 2010-11 will be financed through a GBS of Rs.630.00 crore and IEBR of Rs.5864.15 crore. The M inistry of Shipping 
was allocated a Revised Plan outlay of Rs.4349.61 c rore during 2009-10 consisting of Rs.555.15 crore a s GBS and Rs.3794.46 
crore as IEBR support.

14.   The Committee observed that there was a consi derable reduction in the revenue and capital heads at the RE stage during 
2009-10. In reply to a question, the Secretary submitted the following before the Committee :– 
 “........Coming to the question of the reduced out lay during the previous year, the reason for the re duction that took 
place during the preparation of the Revised Estimates, is the general cut in expenditure introduced as a result of the fiscal 
restrictions that came during the year as well as t he slow pace of development. I must confess that th ere was a slow pace 
of expenditure during the initial part of the year and there were certain factors which led to it. 
Further, although there are some claims for payment on the work done in the past, the revised cost estimate is yet to 
be formally approved by the Government. That is one  of the reasons for not being able to spend on the Setu Samundran 
Project. 
In respect of the Ship Building Subsidy, again, the re was a major reduction in expenditure and this ye ar, also, in 
fact, even in the Revised Estimate, we are unlikely  to spend the amount allocated because of the non a vailability of 
complete applications. As the hon. Committee may no te, this is a scheme for subsidy which is applicabl e to the public 
sector shipyards as well as to the private sector s hipyards. There is a well-defined scheme with very detailed procedures 
and clear requirements of documentation, that have been prescribed and since the requirements are fair ly rigid and 
detailed and we have not really looked at relaxatio n of those requirements, there has been some slowdo wn in the 

distribution of this subsidy. Also, the Subsidy Scheme which was discontinued with effect from August, 2007 has not yet 
been revived. So, we are dealing only with the pre- 2007 cases where ‘in principle’ approval has been g iven. So, that is 
one area where there has been a lot of delay. Other wise, Sir, generally, the pace of expenditure has b een satisfactory, and 
for the year 2010-11, we have already started planning for the appropriate phasing of the expenditure.  
Sir, on the question of actual expenditure for the current year, under the Plan Outlay of Revised Esti mate of 
Rs.548.74 crore, the expenditure at the end of the year is expected to be Rs.460 crore, and non-Plan, out of Rs.1,017.89 
crore, it would be Rs.670 crore.” 
15.  The Committee notes that one of the reasons for the  under utilization of the allocation during 2009-10 is a general 
cut in expenditure introduced as a result of fiscal restrictions. The Committee strongly disapproves the across the board 
imposition of fiscal restrictions without taking in to account the relative merit and importance of the  schemes/projects 
for our economy. The Committee recommends that Mini stry of Shipping may take up the matter with Planni ng 
Commission for a review and not apply such general restrictions on Shipping and Port Sectors that play  major role in 
Indian trade.  
16.  The Committee notes the that Ministry of Shipping could not utilize even the reduced allocation made at RE stage. 
Out of Rs.1566.33 crore, only an amount of Rs.1110 crore is likely to be utilized during 2009-10. The Committee finds no 
justifiable reason for this. In such a situation, t he Ministry of Shipping may not justify any demand for higher 
allocation. The Committee recommends the Ministry s hould be proactive and take steps in advance to ens ure that 
allocated amount is utilized evenly and optimally.  
17.  The Committee expresses dismay over non-utilisation  of funds under Ship Building Subsidy Scheme till d ate, 
though the Scheme was discontinued in August, 2007.  The reason given to the Committee was that it bein g a ‘well 
defined’ Scheme with ‘fairly rigid and detailed requirement’, none of the applications pertaining to pre-2007 cases were 
found complete, where ‘in principle’ approval was g iven. It appears to the Committee that the Scheme h ad not been 
structured properly and was full of inherent compli cations. It sounds very strange that the requiremen t under the 
scheme were so unrealistic that these could not be met so far since 2007. The Committee recommends the  Government 
to revisit this scheme by taking a practical and ho listic view. And if it wishes to utilize the amount  kept for the Subsidy 
Scheme, the applicants be helped to meet the requirement to avail the benefit of the Scheme.  
PORT SECTOR  
18.   Ports provide an interface between ocean tran sport and terrestrial transport and a gateway to international trade. There are 
12 major ports under the Ministry of Shipping. Thes e 12 ports are handling about 72 per cent of the ma ritime cargo of the 
country. 
19.   The Port Sector has been allocated an outlay of Rs.2212.63 Crore during 2010-11, consisting of R s.388.48 Crore as GBS 
and Rs.1824.15 Crore as Internal and Extra Budgetar y Resources (IBER). The scheme for which Gross Budg etary Support for 
plan activities will be provided to Ports sector for the year 2010-11 are as under:
